news.body: Dak Prescott completed 22-of-34 passing attempts for 175 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Dak Prescott underwhelming in loss Sunday
news.impact: Prescott didn't deliver a great performance on Sunday night. He was held to under 200 passing yards against the Giants and lost one turnover in Dallas' loss to their divisional rival. He will have a good opportunity to bounce back next week against the Commanders, but this is not the type of performance fantasy managers wanted to see out of him in the season opener.

news.body: Drake Maye completed 22-of-37 passes for 269 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in the win over the Bills. He added 54 rushing yards on eight carries, while losing one fumble.
news.head: Drake Maye tosses three touchdowns in Week 4 win
news.impact: Maye led the Patriots to a comeback win on the road against the Bills, despite struggling again with some turnovers. The former first-round pick was able to find Efton Chism on a 23-yard pass to give the team the lead with under two minutes remaining. He will look to build on this performance against the Raiders in Week 5.

news.body: Drake Maye (shoulder) is off of the injury report ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Drake Maye (shoulder) off injury report for Sunday
news.impact: Maye was dealing with a minor shoulder injury throughout the week, but it's not a big deal currently and he will carry no injury designation heading into the weekend. He isn't startable in most fantasy leagues at this point in the season, but this would be a good week for him to bounce back from his rough start against a struggling Buffalo defense.

news.body: Drake Maye was a full participant in practice on Thursday.
news.head: Drake Maye (shoulder) logs full practice Thursday
news.impact: Maye continues to battle through a shoulder injury. He is a borderline QB1 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Drake Maye (shoulder) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
news.head: Drake Maye (shoulder) practices in full Wednesday
news.impact: Maye is featured on New England's injury report to start the week. He's managing a minor shoulder injury right now, but he told reporters that it hasn't affected his throwing up to this point. Fantasy managers shouldn't be starting him this week, even if he wasn't on the injury report in any capacity.

news.body: Jacoby Brissett completed 21-of-35 passing attempts for 166 yards, two touchdowns, and three interceptions in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Jacoby Brissett throws three interceptions Sunday
news.impact: Brissett didn't have a good game on Sunday. He was only able to hit 166 passing yards and threw three interceptions over the course of the afternoon, including a pick-six at the end of the game that secured the loss for Arizona. He won't be a good fantasy option moving forward, though he should continue to support Arizona's offensive weapons just fine.

news.body: Jacoby Brissett completed 38-of-52 passes for 280 yards and two touchdowns in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers.
news.head: Jacoby Brissett throws two touchdowns Sunday
news.impact: Brissett was able to play a complete game without any turnovers. They played from behind in the second half where they scored 24 points. Brissett also added a rushing score. He'll take on the Giants next week.

news.body: Jacoby Brissett completed 17 of 28 passes for 95 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks.
news.head: Jacoby Brissett struggles in loss to Seattle
news.impact: Brissett did not look good in this game, failing to even crack a hundred passing yards on the day. He will try to do better against the 49ers next time out. But even that matchup is on the difficult side.

news.body: Jacoby Brissett completed 27-of-37 passes for 277 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Jacoby Brissett leads the Cardinals to victory in Week 1
news.impact: Brissett was efficient and showed his typical veteran leadership in what most would call a season-opening upset of the Chargers. Brissett added 14 yards rushing on six carries, with a long of 11, giving him nearly 300 yards of total offense. The 11th-year veteran is coming off a career-best season, and he's now picked up right where he left off. Brissett could be a matchup-based streamer in standard leagues for the duration of the campaign.

news.body: Jalen Hurts completed 12-of-27 passing attempts for 93 yards and two touchdowns while adding 18 yards on the ground in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Jalen Hurts totals 111 yards in loss Sunday
news.impact: Hurts didn't play well on Sunday. He completed less than half of his passing attempts against the Rams and finished with just 93 passing yards, though he was still able to pick up two touchdowns through the air. He will continue to be underwhelming until DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is back in the lineup for the Eagles.

news.body: Jalen Hurts completed 16 of his 25 pass attempts for 153 yards and an interception while adding four rushes for 25 yards and a touchdown in a 27-7 loss to the Bears in Week 3.
news.head: Jalen Hurts runs for a TD, throws INT in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Hurts and the Philadelphia offense struggled in the loss to Chicago on Monday night. He briefly left the game to get checked for a concussion but was cleared to return to the contest shortly after. Hurts has thrown for 620 yards, five touchdowns, and three interceptions while adding 87 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground in three games this season. He will be a solid QB1 in fantasy heading into Week 4 against the Rams.

news.body: Jalen Hurts completed 26 of his 37 passes for 264 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions while adding five rushes for 16 yards in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.head: Jalen Hurts throws two TDs in Week 2
news.impact: Hurts saved the day for the Eagles, throwing a three-yard touchdown to Darius Cooper with 14 seconds left in regulation. The veteran quarterback also made some mistakes, tossing two interceptions and taking three sacks. Hurts now has five touchdown passes through two games, but he has yet to score any rushing TDs. He will be a high-end QB1 in Week 3 against the Bears on the road.

news.body: Jalen Hurts completed 14-of-25 pass attempts for 203 yards and three touchdowns while also rushing seven times for 46 yards in the Eagles’ 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Jalen Hurts tosses three touchdowns in Week 1 win over Commanders
news.impact: Hurts made the most of an inconsistent season-opening performance behind center, averaging 14.5 yards per completion in the win. The quarterback will look to reward fantasy managers with more explosive dual-threat production in a favorable Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

news.body: Jameis Winston completed 18-of-29 passing attempts for 250 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Jameis Winston tosses three touchdowns in win Sunday
news.impact: Winston struggled in his first couple of games as New York's starter, but he looked much better on Sunday and was able to throw three touchdowns while leading New York to a nice win over the Cardinals. He still threw two interceptions, which was less than ideal, but this performance at least showed that he's still capable of supporting fantasy options on this offense, which is great news. He will likely remain their starter for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Giants coach John Harbaugh confirmed Jameis Winston remains the team’s starting quarterback.
news.head: Jameis Winston to remain Giants starting QB
news.impact: Harbaugh confirmed this statement after the team traded for JJ McCarthy on Monday. Winston has struggled in two games, but he'll remain the team's starter for now.

news.body: Jameis Winston completed 14-of-22 passing attempts for 118 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Jameis Winston doesn't score in win Sunday
news.impact: Winston got the start for the Giants on Sunday, but it didn't look the best. He wasn't able to lead New York's offense to a single touchdown against one of the NFL's worst defenses in the Titans, but they were still able to come away with the win. It looks like Winston, and nearly all of New York's offense, is going to be irrelevant moving forward.

news.body: Jameis Winston completed 11-of-27 passing attempts for 111 yards and an interception in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Jameis Winston underwhelms in loss Monday
news.impact: The veteran quarterback came into the game when Jaxson Dart left with a knee injury. Winston didn't look good against the Rams, finishing with just over 100 scoreless yards in a blowout loss. It looks like Jaxson Dart is going to miss a bit of time with a sprained MCL, leaving Winston as the short-term starter for New York, which will be less than ideal for most of the fantasy options on their roster.

news.body: Jared Goff completed 32 of 52 passes for 412 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
news.head: Jared Goff airs it out for 412 yards in Sunday night's loss
news.impact: Through Sunday, Goff now holds the NFL's highest single-game total in passing yards for the season. The Lions threw the ball 52 times compared to just 15 runs, leading to Goff's seventh career 400-yard passing performance. Surprisingly, the Lions' QB only connected for one touchdown pass on the night. Overall, Goff has been excellent through four weeks, completing 67.7% of his throws for better than 300 yards per game with a 9-0 TD/INT ratio.

news.body: Jared Goff completed 25-of-32 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns in a 31-24 win over the Jets. He also rushed for six yards on four carries.
news.head: Jared Goff tosses two touchdowns in Week 3
news.impact: Goff found Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs through the air to help pace the Lions to a home win over the Jets. Goff has yet to throw an interception this year and has three straight multi-touchdown games to open the season. The Lions will take on the Panthers on the road in Week 4.

news.body: Jared Goff completed 26-of-38 passing attempts for 327 yards and four touchdowns in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Jared Goff throws four touchdowns in win Thursday
news.impact: Goff and Detroit's offense struggled at the start of the game on Thursday night, but they were able to get things going later, and he ended up throwing four touchdowns in a shootout loss to the Buffalo Bills. He has looked terrific to start the season and should continue to be a safe week-to-week streaming option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Jared Goff completed 26-of-39 pass attempts for 206 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing twice for two yards in the Lions' 31-30 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1.
news.head: Jared Goff tosses two touchdowns in Week 1 win over Saints
news.impact: Goff took what the New Orleans defense allowed, relying on dynamic running back Jahmyr Gibbs to carry a rusty Detroit starting offense in the Week 1 win. The veteran signal-caller remains a stable mid-tier option with QB1 upside ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

news.body: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said the goal is for Jayden Daniels to return in Week 5.
news.head: Jayden Daniels (elbow) hopeful to return in Week 5
news.impact: Daniels is slated to return to practice this week. His status will need to be monitored throughout the week.

news.body: Jayden Daniels (elbow) will not play Sunday against the Colts.
news.head: Jayden Daniels (elbow) out for Week 4
news.impact: Daniels has been progressing this week from his elbow injury, even getting in some limited practice sessions. He's still not quite ready to go, however, as Marcus Mariota will draw a second straight start behind center. Daniels will look ahead to a Week 5 matchup against the Giants.

news.body: Jayden Daniels (elbow) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: Jayden Daniels (elbow) limited again Thursday
news.impact: Daniels was limited for a second-straight practice on Thursday as he continues to rehab an elbow injury that he suffered in Week 2. He doesn't look likely to play in Week 4, but we won't have official word on his status until sometime after practice on Friday probably.

news.body: Jayden Daniels is taking his recovery day to day.
news.head: Jayden Daniels (elbow) taking recovery day-to-day
news.impact: Daniels opened the week with a limited session on Wednesday. He remains unlikely to play this week, but he has a chance to return in Week 5 or 6.

news.body: Joe Burrow completed 39-of-54 passing attempts for 428 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions while adding six yards and a touchdown on the ground in Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: Joe Burrow throws two interceptions Sunday
news.impact: Burrow had an up-and-down performance on Sunday. On the one hand, he was able to throw for over 425 yards and logged two total touchdowns against the Jaguars. On the other hand, he threw two interceptions and led Cincinnati to score just 17 points in a loss at home. His fantasy value for next week will heavily depend on the health of Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) for their matchup against the Dolphins.

news.body: Joe Burrow completed 28-of-37 passes for 282 yards and three touchdowns in a 30-27 loss to the Steelers. He rushed for 13 yards on two carries.
news.head: Joe Burrow tosses three touchdowns in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Burrow was excellent for the majority of the game Sunday, finding Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Mike Gesicki for his three touchdown passes. The veteran did fumble on what would be the final drive for the Bengals, sealing the win for the Steelers. Burrow and the Bengals will welcome the Jaguars to town in Week 4.

news.body: Joe Burrow (back) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 3's matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
news.head: Joe Burrow (back) off injury report for Week 3
news.impact: Burrow was reportedly dealing with some soreness coming into the week, but it's not a serious issue and he carries no injury designation ahead of Week 3. He should be a full go against the Steelers, assuming he suffers no setbacks between now and then.

news.body: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said Joe Burrow is dealing with soreness.
news.head: Joe Burrow dealing with soreness
news.impact: It is unclear how much Burrow will practice on Wednesday. He is day-to-day for now.

news.body: Jordan Love completed 22 of his 30 passes for 197 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers in Week 4.
news.head: Jordan Love throws two TDs in Week 4
news.impact: Love turned in a solid game in the close win over Tampa Bay. His touchdown passes went to Tucker Kraft and Matthew Golden. Love has now thrown for 1,041 yards, eight touchdowns, and three interceptions through four games. He will be a high-end QB2 heading into Week 5's matchup against the Bears.

news.body: Jordan Love completed 28 of 53 passes for 312 yards with two touchdowns and a pick in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons. He also ran once for no gain.
news.head: Jordan Love passes for 312 yards in loss
news.impact: Love was a bit up and down in this game. He was struggling against the pressure Atlanta was bringing, missing several forced throws and causing tipped passes. The Green Bay offense has no run game, which has worked out decently well for the pass catchers, but until they get things going on the ground to make the defense respect the run, it will be hard for the receivers and Love to have a ceiling week in, week out.

news.body: Jordan Love told reporters that his elbow injury is a non-issue for Week 3 against the Falcons.
news.head: Jordan Love says elbow is non-issue for Week 3
news.impact: Love said discomfort in his elbow went away before Jets game ended. He indicated the elbow is a non-issue for the Falcons game, even on a short week.

news.body: Jordan Love completed 16-of-29 pass attempts for 145 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: Jordan Love tosses two touchdowns in Week 2 win over Jets
news.impact: Love continues a solid start to the season as part of a Green Bay offense battling inconsistency early on, throwing two touchdowns in each of the first two games. The quarterback will look for more sizeable success for fantasy managers in a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.body: Josh Allen completed 23-of-33 passes for 254 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the loss to the Patriots. He rushed for four yards and a touchdown on five carries.
news.head: Josh Allen accounts for two touchdowns in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Allen turned in a solid day Sunday, including a touchdown pass to Keon Coleman late in the game. Allen was without DJ Moore, who left the game in the first half with a shoulder injury. His interception late in the game ended up a comeback and handed the Bills their first loss of the season. Allen and the Bills will travel to Los Angeles to take on the Rams in Week 5.

news.body: Josh Allen is without an injury designation ahead of Week 4's matchup against the New England Patriots.
news.head: Josh Allen without injury designation for Week 4
news.impact: There was some concern that Allen suffered a minor injury of some kind in last week's win over the Chargers, but that's not the case and he carries no injury designation heading into Week 4. He should be a full go and remains a top-tier fantasy option moving forward.

news.body: Josh Allen completed 16-of-26 pass attempts for 204 yards and two interceptions while also rushing eight times for 22 yards and two touchdowns with one fumble lost in the Bills' 24-16 Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Josh Allen reaches end zone on ground twice in Week 3 win over Chargers
news.impact: Allen made up for a mistake-filled day behind center rushing for two touchdowns for the third consecutive contests. The quarterback remains locked in as an elite dual-threat option behind center in all formats, with a Week 4 divisional matchup against the New England Patriots up next.

news.body: Josh Allen completed 20-of-31 passing attempts for 248 yards and three touchdowns while adding 69 yards and two touchdowns on the ground in Sunday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Josh Allen scores five touchdowns in dominant showing Thursday
news.impact: Allen had an insane showing on Thursday night. He totaled over 300 yards and scored five total touchdowns en route to a big win over the Lions in primetime, all while protecting the ball and committing zero turnovers. He has been absolutely dominant through the first two games of the season and is pacing to be one of, if not the most valuable individual player that anyone can roster at this point.

news.body: Justin Herbert completed 19-of-31 passes for 189 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions in the Chargers 30-23 loss against the Seahawks on Sunday.
news.head: Justin Herbert continues to struggle Sunday
news.impact: Herbert added 40 yards rushing on the ground. He threw a pair of interceptions to linebackers, including on the first offensive play of the game. He remains someone tough to trust heading into a matchup against the Broncos next week.

news.body: Justin Herbert completed 20-of-34 pass attempts for 226 yards, one touchdown, and one interception while also rushing four times for 17 yards in the Chargers' 24-16 Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Justin Herbert struggles again behind center in Week 3 loss to Bills
news.impact: Herbert has struggled to make an impact behind center to begin the season, finishing with less than 230 passing yards in each of the first three contests. The quarterback will look to break out of his early season struggles as part of an underperforming Chargers offense against a tough Seattle Seahawks defense in Week 4.

news.body: Justin Herbert completed 15-of-27 passing attempts for 192 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.head: Justin Herbert struggles in loss Sunday
news.impact: Herbert didn't look very good on Sunday. He failed to hit 200 total yards and had more interceptions than touchdowns in what turned out to be a two-score loss at the hands of the Raiders, who are frequently regarded as one of the worst teams in the NFL. Los Angeles' offense has been spiraling through the first two weeks of the season, and it's not getting any easier for them with an absolute gauntlet of a schedule coming up over the next 7-9 weeks.

news.body: Justin Herbert connected on 17-of-27 passes for 209 yards with one touchdown and one interception, adding 29 yards on five carries in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.head: Justin Herbert starts new season with mediocre performance
news.impact: Herbert and the Chargers' offense definitely disappointed under new OC Mike McDaniel on Sunday. This was expected by many to be an opening act for a dynamic offense against a sub-par defensive unit. It turned out to be anything but that. Herbert was sacked three times and picked off once while just clearing 200 yards on 27 throws. He did find top receiver Ladd McConkey for an eight-yard TD toss in the third quarter, but that was it as far as putting points on the board through the air. Herbert should still be viewed as a solid QB 1 going into a matchup with the Raiders, but if he disappoints again, the seventh-year pro will drop like a rock.

news.body: Kirk Cousins completed 31 of his 52 passes for 365 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs in Week 4. He also completed a two-point conversion pass to Cody White.
news.head: Kirk Cousins throws two TDs in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Cousins put up big numbers in the close loss but he couldn't quite knock off the Chiefs. His touchdown passes went to Brock Bowers and Ian Thomas in the contest. Cousins has looked reinvigorated for the Raiders this season, throwing for 1,026 yards, 11 touchdowns, and four interceptions through four games. He will be a high-end QB2 in Week 5 vs. the Patriots.

news.body: Kirk Cousins completed 22-of-33 passes for 248 yards with three touchdowns in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
news.head: Kirk Cousins throws three touchdowns Sunday
news.impact: Cousins enjoyed the return of Brock Bowers in a big way Sunday afternoon as the two connected on 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown. Cousins also threw touchdowns to Michael Mayer and Cody White. He'll face the Chiefs next week.

news.body: Kirk Cousins completed 19-of-29 passing attempts for 253 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Kirk Cousins tosses three touchdowns in win Sunday
news.impact: Cousins played a good game on Sunday. He threw three touchdowns over the course of the day and he led Las Vegas to a big win over their divisional rivals. He isn't expected to be a good fantasy option himself moving forward but should be good enough to support at least two fantasy options on this offense on a week-to-week basis.

news.body: Kirk Cousins completed 21-of-30 pass attempts for 160 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Kirk Cousins offers mixed results in Week 1 win over Dolphins
news.impact: Cousins was unable to find much success downfield, averaging just 7.6 yards per completion in the win. the veteran signal-caller will look to minimize turnovers moving forward, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.body: Kyler Murray completed 27-of-37 passing attempts for 247 yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Kyler Murray scoreless in win Sunday
news.impact: Murray took care of the ball on Sunday, but he wasn't able to get much going against the Dolphins and didn't score a touchdown during the team's win. He shouldn't be considered a good fantasy option moving forward, especially if Justin Jefferson (ankle) has to miss more time.

news.body: Kyler Murray completed 15-of-29 passes for 168 yards with one touchdown and one interception in the Vikings 23-16 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
news.head: Kyler Murray has underwhelming day Sunday
news.impact: Murray was playing in his first game back from the concussion protocol. He lost Justin Jefferson early for the day. He targeted Jordan Addison heavily, including on a 41-yard touchdown. He'll face the Dolphins next week.

news.body: Kyler Murray has cleared concussion protocol and will start against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday.
news.head: Kyler Murray clears concussion protocol, will start Week 3
news.impact: Murray missed the Vikings Week 2 slog of a win over the Bears, but he will be back in the lineup for Week 3 against a hapless Tampa defense. Murray is still a bit of an unknown at this point given he barely played in Week 1, but this is a perfect matchup to return to.

news.body: Kyler Murray (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Kyler Murray (concussion) ruled out for Sunday
news.impact: Murray was progressing well through the NFL's concussion protocols this week, but he will ultimately have to end up missing a game due to the big hit that he suffered in Week 1. It looks likely that he will be back in time for Week 3, but Carson Wentz is expected to serve as Minnesota's starter in the meantime, which is good news for the fantasy value of Justin Jefferson in a prime matchup against the Bears this week.

news.body: Lamar Jackson (ankle) has only an outside chance of playing Sunday against the Falcons.
news.head: Lamar Jackson (ankle) unlikely to play in Week 5
news.impact: Jackson sustained a sprained ankle in Week 4's win over the Titans. Now, the two-time MVP's status is uncertain for the next few weeks. The Ravens have not officially ruled him out for this Sunday's game, but the chances of him playing seem very thin. Tyler Huntley would be set to step in at quarter in Jackson's stead.

news.body: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Monday he didn’t know the chances of Lamar Jackson playing in Week 5.
news.head: Lamar Jackson (ankle) status for Week 5 uncertain
news.impact: Minter added that he didn’t think “it’s going to be crazy long-term.” Jackson will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

news.body: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is considered day-to-day with an ankle injury.
news.head: Lamar Jackson (ankle) considered day-to-day
news.impact: Jackson was listed as questionable to return Sunday, but he remained on the sideline for the rest of the game. Jackson was seen exiting the stadium in a boot, but head coach Jesse Minter appeared to be optimistic about Jackson's prognosis. The Ravens take on the Falcons in Week 5.

news.body: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) is questionable to return against the Titans.
news.head: Lamar Jackson (ankle) questionable to return
news.impact: Jackson was seen limping into the locker room to end the first half. He returned to the sideline prior to the start of the second half, but did not have his helmet. Tyler Huntley appears set to quarterback the Ravens the rest of the way Sunday. Jackson was 15-of-20 for 222 yards and two touchdowns prior to the injury.

news.body: Matthew Stafford completed 32-of-51 passing attempts for 317 yards and two interceptions in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Matthew Stafford doesn't score in win Sunday
news.impact: Stafford was able to lead the Rams to a win on Sunday, but he wasn't able to find a lot of personal success in the process. He failed to score even a single touchdown in this matchup, and he also threw two interceptions, which left him with a poor fantasy total. He should bounce back and return to form sometime in the near future, however,

news.body: Matthew Stafford completed 30-of-55 passing attempts for 390 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions while adding 13 yards on the ground in Sunday night's 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Matthew Stafford totals 403 yards in loss Sunday
news.impact: Stafford had an up-and-down game on Sunday night. He finished with over 400 total yards and two touchdowns, but he also threw two interceptions, one of which was returned for a touchdown. He made some mistakes that opened the door for Denver to win this game, but fantasy managers should be happy with his production and should continue to start him in favorable matchups moving forward.

news.body: Matthew Stafford completed 22-of-31 passing attempts for 327 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.head: Matthew Stafford tosses four touchdowns in win Monday
news.impact: The reigning MVP had a great bounce-back game on Monday night after a disappointing season opener last week. He scored four touchdowns against the Giants and limited his mistakes overall, helping lead Los Angeles to a blowout win over New York. The only questions for him moving forward will be consistency and the health of his wideouts, with Puka Nacua (hip) currently out of the lineup for the Rams.

news.body: Matthew Stafford completed 15-of-25 passes for 155 yards and a pick in the Rams' 27-7 blowout loss to the 49ers. He also ran twice for a loss of a yard.
news.head: Matthew Stafford quiet in loss to Niners
news.impact: Stafford was not in his best form on Thursday, missing throws and looking a little rusty. It's a rough start for a team that was deemed Super Bowl-bound, but he will look to get back on track next week.

news.body: Patrick Mahomes completed 15 of his 30 passes for 225 yards and two touchdowns in a 30-27 win over the Raiders in Week 4.
news.head: Patrick Mahomes II throws two TDs in Week 4
news.impact: Mahomes managed to hold off an upstart Raiders squad that gave the Chiefs everything they could handle. Both of his touchdown passes went to Tyquan Thornton in the win. Mahomes has now thrown for 1,037 yards, nine touchdowns, and two interceptions through four games. He will be on bye in Week 5 before going up against the Chargers in Week 6.

news.body: Patrick Mahomes II completed 20-of-24 pass attempts for 246 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception while also rushing once for one yard in the Chiefs' 24-10 Week 3 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Patrick Mahomes II tosses two touchdowns in Week 3 win
news.impact: Mahomes II continues a dynamic start to the season behind center, posting two or more touchdowns in each of the first three games. The superstar quarterback has turned back the clock for head coach Andy Reid to begin the season, with a Week 4 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders up next.

news.body: Patrick Mahomes II completed 32-of-47 passing attempts for 382 yards and three touchdowns while adding 17 yards on the ground in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Patrick Mahomes II tosses three touchdowns Sunday
news.impact: Mahomes had an electric game on Sunday night, throwing three touchdowns and totaling nearly 400 yards en route to a narrow win over the Colts. He has been terrific since his return from injury and should be considered a worthwhile starter with week-to-week upside on any given week.

news.body: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) was listed as a full participant in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) listed as full participant Wednesday
news.impact: As expected, Mahomes continues to carry on at full health, logging a full practice session to start the week on Wednesday. Fantasy managers should have very few concerns with his premature return from injury at this point, since he demonstrated his health in Week 1 in Kansas City's big win over the Broncos.

news.body: Sam Darnold completed 13-of-22 passes for 168 yards with two touchdowns and one interception in the Seahawks 30-23 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Sam Darnold throws two touchdowns Sunday
news.impact: Darnold threw an interception on the Seahawks first offensive play of the game. He didn't seem to be comfortable in the pocket for most of the afternoon. He'll be a QB2 next week against the 49ers.

news.body: Sam Darnold completed 31-of-45 pass attempts for 379 yards, four touchdowns, and two interceptions while also rushing once for five yards in the Seahawks’ 33-31 Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Sam Darnold tosses four touchdowns in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Darnold made the most of his opportunities in his return from a glute injury suffered in Week 1, averaging 12.2 yards per completion in the loss. The quarterback will look to keep rolling against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4.

news.body: Sam Darnold is off the injury report and good to go for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
news.head: Sam Darnold (glute) good to go Sunday
news.impact: Darnold was able to practice all week. He winds up missing only two games (including Week 1 when he was injured in the first series). He'll look to keep keep the Seahawks offense rolling heading into Washington on Sunday.

news.body: Sam Darnold was a full participant in practice on Thursday.
news.head: Sam Darnold (glute) logs full practice Thursday
news.impact: Darnold continues to trend in the right direction after he was limited to start the week on Wednesday. He is on track to return on Sunday against the Commanders.

news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passing attempts for 227 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Trevor Lawrence scores once in win Sunday
news.impact: Lawrence was able to lead the Jaguars to a win on Sunday, but he wasn't able to rack up many fantasy points in the process, finishing with just one touchdown over the course of the afternoon. Almost all of Jacksonville's fantasy options disappointed in this matchup, but they should be able to bounce back in a competitive matchup against the Eagles next week.

news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 19-of-29 passing attempts for 182 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception while adding 25 yards on the ground in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Trevor Lawrence tosses three touchdowns in blowout win Sunday
news.impact: Lawrence played a stellar game on Sunday, finishing with over 200 total yards and three touchdowns in a big win over the Patriots. He has been playing well so far this season and will continue to be a viable starting option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 17 of his 29 passes for 189 yards and an interception while adding six yards on two rushes in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Trevor Lawrence throws for 189 yards in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Lawrence got the Jaguars off to a fast start as they were leading 10-3 at halftime, but the Broncos came to life on defense starting in the third quarter. Lawrence has now thrown for 434 yards and four touchdowns through the first two games of the season. He will be a solid QB1 in fantasy in Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns. He also ran twice for three yards.
news.head: Trevor Lawrence flawless in big win over Browns
news.impact: Lawrence played on easy mode against a Browns defense that just couldn't create stops. He had only five incompletions to four touchdowns on the day, a great ratio to have. With their win over the Browns, the Jags are the only AFC South team to clinch a win on Sunday. He faces a much tougher test against the Broncos next week.

news.body: Tyler Shough completed 30-of-48 passing attempts for 286 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Tyler Shough throws for 286 yards in loss Monday
news.impact: New Orleans had a rough game on Monday night, suffering a blowout loss at the hands of their divisional rivals at home. Shough was personally able to have an okay game, however, logging close to 300 total yards and taking good care of the ball over the course of the night. Fantasy managers probably aren't satisfied with his output in this game, but he should bounce back and return to having high value sometime within the next game or two.

news.body: Tyler Shough completed 29-of-42 passes for 255 yards with four touchdowns and one interception in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday.
news.head: Tyler Shough throws four touchdowns, struggles with turnovers late
news.impact: Shough was dealing through the first three quarters, tossing four touchdowns with two of them going to Juwan Johnson and the other two going to Noah Fant. The Saints turned the ball over four times in the fourth quarter with three of them being committed by Shough on an interception and two fumbles. He'll face the Falcons next week.

news.body: Tyler Shough completed 27-of-34 passes for 252 yards and one touchdown in a 24-17 win over the Ravens.
news.head: Tyler Shough executes late comeback win in Week 2
news.impact: Shough also added 23 rushing yards on nine carries in the win. Both of the second-year quarterback's touchdowns came in the fourth quarter to tie the game and give the Saints the lead. Shough has looked great through his first two games of the season and will look to build on these performances in a Week 3 matchup with Las Vegas.

news.body: Tyler Shough completed 35-of-56 pass attempts for 410 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions while also rushing four times for eight yards in the Saints' 31-30 Week 1 overtime loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Tyler Shough electrifies late in Week 1 loss to Lions
news.impact: Shough carried the New Orleans offense late in the contest after trailing 21-0 at one point, throwing three second-half touchdowns to force overtime in the Week 1 loss. The second-year signal-caller faces a stiff test in Week 2 against a tough Baltimore Ravens defense next.

news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. rushed the ball 20 times for 94 yards and caught 4-of-8 targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. totals 128 yards Sunday
news.impact: The veteran played well on Sunday. He logged 128 total yards against the Dolphins, and he was able to do that while maintaining good efficiency. He will continue to be a worthwhile fantasy option for however long Jordan Mason (thumb) remains out of the lineup for the Vikings.

news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. ran for 58 yards on 17 carries in the Vikings 23-16 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday. He also caught 5-of-6 targets for 34 yards receiving.
news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. totals 22 touches Sunday
news.impact: It wasn't the most efficient performance for Jones, but his overall volume made up for it. He'll be an RB2 play next week against the Dolphins.

news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Jones was able to return to practice to finish the week. He should remain an RB2 play in a lead role in the Vikings backfield.

news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. practiced again on Friday.
news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) practices Friday
news.impact: Jones was limited in his return to practice on Thursday. He should be in line for another lead role on Sunday against the Buccaneers. He'll be an RB2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Alvin Kamara rushed the ball seven times for 23 yards and two touchdowns while adding five receptions for 35 yards on the ground in Monday's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Alvin Kamara scores twice in loss Monday
news.impact: Kamara suffered an injury of some kind in the middle of Monday night's game, but he was able to return and finish out the contest. He ended up finishing with a good fantasy total thanks to his two touchdowns and five receptions on the night, though he wasn't where the team needed him to be in terms of efficiency. He will continue to be a worthwhile fantasy asset for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Alvin Kamara ran for 36 yards on nine carries in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday. He also caught his lone target for five yards receiving.
news.head: Alvin Kamara sees nine carries Sunday
news.impact: Kamara saw his role expand after Travis Etienne Jr. left the game early. He'll be in the flex conversation next week if Etienne is sidelined.

news.body: Alvin Kamara rushed for 15 yards on nine carries in the Saints' 24-17 win over the Ravens. He caught 5-of-6 targets for seven yards.
news.head: Alvin Kamara hauls in five passes in Week 2 win
news.impact: Kamara was very limited in his production in his 2026 debut, was clearly a focal point of the offense which cut into Travis Etienne's volume. Fantasy managers will want to be cautious with both running backs volume in question heading into a Week 3 matchup with Las Vegas.

news.body: Alvin Kamara is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
news.head: Alvin Kamara (knee) off injury report for Week 2
news.impact: Kamara will be good to go for his season debut. He should be in a third down/passing down role in the Saints backfield behind Travis Etienne.

news.body: Ashton Jeanty carried the ball 15 times for 58 yards and caught six of his eight targets for 68 yards in a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs in Week 4.
news.head: Ashton Jeanty runs for 58 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Jeanty salvaged another tough day on the ground with his work in the passing game. He briefly left the game with what appeared to be an ankle injury but was able to return to action, although it is concerning considering he has been dealing with an ankle issue since the preseason. The second-year running back has been held to 58 or fewer rushing yards in three straight games but continues to see the majority of the backfield work in Las Vegas. He will be a solid RB1 in Week 5 vs. the Patriots.

news.body: Ashton Jeanty ran for 56 yards on 19 carries in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints. He also caught 3-of-3 targets for 36 yards receiving.
news.head: Ashton Jeanty struggles on ground Sunday
news.impact: Jeanty was inefficient on the ground for the second straight week. He still remained active in the passing game. He remains an RB1 in a workhorse role moving forward.

news.body: Ashton Jeanty rushed the ball 21 times for 48 yards and caught 4-of-7 targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Ashton Jeanty inefficient in win Sunday
news.impact: Jeanty didn't look great on Sunday. He totaled just 63 on his 28 opportunities against the Chargers, and he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all, which left him with an underwhelming fantasy total. The Raiders have a tough schedule coming up, so the young running back will need to step up his game if he wants to deliver for fantasy managers.

news.body: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
news.head: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) logs full practice Wednesday
news.impact: Jeanty seems to be entirely over his ankle injury at this point, as he played through it in Week 1 and now logs a full practice session to start the week on Wednesday. He should be a full go and high-quality fantasy option moving forward, assuming he suffers no setbacks with his recovery.

news.body: Bhayshul Tuten rushed the ball 17 times for 73 yards and caught two passes for 18 yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Bhayshul Tuten racks up 91 yards in win Sunday
news.impact: Tuten had a good game on Sunday, finishing as the team's top rusher and dominating the touches in the backfield en route to a win over the Bengals. Chris Rodriguez Jr. was the one to get into the end zone for the Jaguars, however, which was annoying for fantasy managers to see. The young running back should continue to be a worthwhile fantasy asset moving forward.

news.body: Bhayshul Tuten rushed the ball 15 times for 73 yards and caught two passes for 17 yards in Sunday's 35-6 win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Bhayshul Tuten leads team in rushing Sunday
news.impact: Tuten had a good game on Sunday. He led the team in rushing yards at an efficient clip of 4.9 yards per carry, and he was also able to get into the end zone at one point, which left him with a great fantasy total. He should again be started in a matchup against the Bengals next week.

news.body: Bhayshul Tuten carried the ball 13 times for 65 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for minus-three yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Bhayshul Tuten finds the end zone in Week 2
news.impact: Tuten punched in a one-yard touchdown in the second quarter to give the Jaguars an early 7-0 lead. The second-year back also vastly outproduced Chris Rodriguez Jr., who had just 13 yards on six carries. Tuten has now racked up 131 rushing yards through two games. He will be a solid RB2 in fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.body: Bhayshul Tuten ran 15 times for 66 yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also caught his only target for 22 yards.
news.head: Bhayshul Tuten racks up 66 yards on the ground in win
news.impact: Tuten led the Jags in rushing attempts in the win, but didn't have much to show in terms of fantasy scoring in half- or full-PPR formats. But to be fair, he was efficient in his touches, and it's likely that better days are ahead for the apparent Jags RB1.

news.body: Bijan Robinson rushed the ball 19 times for 145 yards and two touchdowns in Monday night's 45-24 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Bijan Robinson dominant in blowout win Monday
news.impact: Robinson was absolutely dominant on Monday night. He led the Falcons in rushing with 145 yards on the night at a hyper-efficient clip of 7.6 yards per carry, and he was also able to get into the end zone on two separate occasions. He let a little to be desired in the passing game, but that was simply because the Falcons were up so much for so long. He has been stellar over the first four weeks of the season and should continue to be one of the best assets in all of fantasy moving forward.

news.body: Bijan Robinson ran 29 times for 194 yards and two touchdowns and caught both of his targets for 19 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
news.head: Bijan Robinson explodes in Week 3 win over Packers
news.impact: Robinson had his way with the Packers' defense, rushing for 6.7 yards per carry. He ripped off a huge 55-yard gain early on in the game, which opened the floodgates for many more big runs throughout the game. The Packers simply could not stop him, and once the ground game got going, QB Michael Penix and WR Drake London were able to carve up the Packers' secondary. With Penix back, the offense has new life, and Bijan stands to benefit greatly from it, even if Brian Robinson Jr. spells him.

news.body: Bijan Robinson ran 16 times for 72 yards and caught three of four targets for nine yards in the Falcons' 34-3 blowout loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
news.head: Bijan Robinson held in check in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Robinson was fine on the ground, 4.5 yards per carry, but still largely held in check. The Panthers didn't allow the Falcons to move the ball, mostly thanks to Atlanta's lack of competent QB play. If Michael Penix returns on Thursday, that will hopefully be a huge boost to Bijan's value. If not, it's looking like another long night for Bijan managers.

news.body: Bijan Robinson carried the ball 21 times for 83 yards and caught eight of his 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1.
news.head: Bijan Robinson hauls in touchdown catch in Week 1
news.impact: Robinson was basically the entire offense for the Falcons in the close loss to Pittsburgh. He scored the team's only touchdown on a 23-yard catch at the end of the first quarter. It was an excellent start to the season for the star running back, who will slot in as a high-end RB1 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Panthers.

news.body: Blake Corum rushed the ball five times for 14 yards and caught one pass for seven yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Blake Corum a non-factor in win Sunday
news.impact: Corum didn't play much of a role for the Rams in Week 4. He saw just six touches over the course of the game and was only able to turn them into 21 yards, as opposed to Kyren Williams' 26 touches for 147 yards. Fantasy managers shouldn't have much hope for Corum to have standalone value anytime soon.

news.body: Blake Corum rushed the ball six times for 15 yards and caught 2-of-4 targets for zero yards in Sunday's 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Blake Corum quiet in loss Sunday
news.impact: Corum wasn't able to contribute much on Sunday. He totaled just 15 yards on his ten opportunities over the course of the night, which left him with a very poor fantasy total. He will continue to see a good amount of work in Los Angeles' offense moving forward but will likely continue to fall behind Kyren Williams in competitive matchups.

news.body: Blake Corum rushed the ball 12 times for 79 yards and caught one pass for 13 yards in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.head: Blake Corum totals 92 yards in win Monday
news.impact: Los Angeles' offense looked great on Monday night, and Corum was no exception to that. He put up 92 total yards on just 13 opportunities, although he wasn't able to get into the endzone to put the capstone on that. The Rams' backfield is a situation to continue monitoring, with Corum and Kyren Williams each seeing the same amount of carries in this blowout win.

news.body: Blake Corum ran 10 times for 54 yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers on Thursday.
news.head: Blake Corum totals 54 yards in loss
news.impact: Corum was solid on the ground at 5.4 a carry, but that was about all he had going for him. Without a touchdown or receiving work to go along with his yardage, it was a disappointing fantasy performance. However, his usage is encouraging; the Rams at least trust him enough that they will split Kyren Williams' workload with Corum. It makes him a top-tier handcuff RB, and one that should be rostered in case anything happens to Kyren.

news.body: Braelon Allen carried the ball 14 times for 59 yards while catching both of his targets for eight yards in a 23-12 loss to the Bears in Week 4.
news.head: Braelon Allen runs for 59 yards in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Allen got all of the backfield touches but wasn't able to do much with them, averaging just 4.2 yards per carry in the loss. With Breece Hall (quad) looking at least another week or two away from returning, Allen should operate as the Jets' lead back again in Week 5 against the Browns.

news.body: Braelon Allen rushed for 14 yards on four carries in the 31-24 loss to the Lions. He caught all three of his targets for three yards.
news.head: Braelon Allen tallies seven touches in Week 3
news.impact: Allen continued to see limited work Sunday, but he could be in line for more touches in Week 4 if Breece Hall (thigh) misses time. Hall was injured late in the game and will likely undergo testing Monday to determine the severity of the injury.

news.body: Braelon Allen rushed five times for seven yards and one touchdown while also catching his only target for eight yards in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
news.head: Braelon Allen reaches end zone in Week 2 loss to Packers
news.impact: Allen made the most of a forgettable performance as part of an underperforming backfield attack Sunday, scoring his first touchdown of the season in a losing effort. The running back remains more of a complementary option behind No. 1 running back Breece Hall for head coach Aaron Glenn, with a favorable Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions up next.

news.body: Braelon Allen carried the ball 10 times for 40 yards and failed to corral his lone target in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
news.head: Braelon Allen sees 10 carres in backup role in Week 1
news.impact: Allen mixed in as the backup behind Breece Hall, who handled 22 carries and caught two passes. The Jets will continue to utilize Allen to spell Hall throughout the season, but the former only has fantasy value as a handcuff for the time being. He will take on the Packers at home in Week 2.

news.body: Breece Hall (quad) ruled out for Week 4.
news.head: Breece Hall (quad) will not play Sunday
news.impact: Hall has not been practicing this week and, as expected, will not play Sunday. Braelon Allen should be the workhorse back for the Jets in a matchup with the Bears.

news.body: Breece Hall remained sidelined from practice on Thursday.
news.head: Breece Hall (quad) misses practice Thursday
news.impact: Hall remains on track to be sidelined on Sunday against the Bears.

news.body: Breece Hall will be sidelined from practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Breece Hall (quad) not practicing Wednesday
news.impact: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Hall is considered week-to-week. He is likely to sit this Sunday.

news.body: Ian Rapoport reports Breece Hall is considered week-to-week with a quad injury.
news.head: Breece Hall (quad) considered week-to-week
news.impact: Hall received “good news after the MRI” he received. Braelon Allen will figure to take over the lead role in the Jets backfield in his absence. He will be in the RB2/flex range for fantasy managers.

news.body: Brian Robinson Jr. rushed the ball 14 times for 62 yards and three touchdowns in Monday night's 45-24 blowout win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Brian Robinson Jr. scored three touchdowns in win Monday
news.impact: Robinson had one of the best games of his careers in Week 4, scoring three touchdowns en route to a blowout win over Atlanta's divisional rivals on Monday night. He was able to tack on 62 yards outside of that, and he should be considered one of the premier handcuff options in fantasy at this point, as he has week-to-week upside even with Bijan Robinson healthy and starting ahead of him for the Falcons.

news.body: Brian Robinson Jr. ran 10 times for 50 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
news.head: Brian Robinson Jr. runs in touchdown in big win
news.impact: Robinson played second fiddle to Bijan Robinson, but he still got enough touches and some goal-line work that he was usable for those who started him. He's been splitting work with Bijan to keep the younger back rested, and he won't have outings like this all the time, but he's certainly a handcuff worth rostering.

news.body: Brian Robinson Jr. (ankle) is good to go for Thursday night's game against the Green Bay Packers.
news.head: Brian Robinson Jr. (ankle) good to go for Thursday
news.impact: Robinson is going to be good to go for Thursday night's game, despite being listed on the team's injury report earlier in the week due to an ankle issue of some kind. He will continue to be involved as the RB2 on this offense behind Bijan Robinson for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Brian Robinson Jr. was a full participant in practice on Tuesday.
news.head: Brian Robinson Jr. (ankle) logs full practice Tuesday
news.impact: Robinson is dealing with an ankle injury. He is on track to be good to go in his backup role on Thursday against the Packers.

news.body: Bucky Irving carried the ball 16 times for 61 yards in a 17-14 loss to the Packers in Week 4.
news.head: Bucky Irving goes for 61 yards in Week 4 loss
news.impact: He was not targeted in the passing game. Irving dealt with a glute injury throughout the week, but he did not seem affected by it during the game. He did watch as fellow running backs Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker both found the end zone in the close loss. Irving has run for 241 yards and one touchdown through four games this season. He will be on the RB2 radar in Week 5 against the Cowboys.

news.body: Bucky Irving is officially good to go for Sunday's game against the Packers.
news.head: Bucky Irving (glute) good to go Sunday
news.impact: Irving sat on the bench for the majority of the fourth quarter last week. He was limited in practice throughout the week and will be good to go on Sunday.

news.body: Bucky Irving (glute) was officially a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Bucky Irving (glute) officially limited Thursday
news.impact: Irving has been limited in two-straight practices to start the week. He's still managing a glute injury, but it looks more likely than not that he will play through it this week. If he's cleared to play heading into the weekend, fantasy managers should have no hesitations starting him in a matchup against the Packers.

news.body: Bucky Irving practiced again on Thursday.
news.head: Bucky Irving (glute) practices Thursday
news.impact: Irving was limited in practice to open the week on Wednesday. He remains on track to be good to go on Sunday.

news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 18 times for 58 yards and caught one pass for eight yards in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Cam Skattebo underwhelming in win Sunday
news.impact: New York was able to score 36 points on Sunday, but Skattebo wasn't really able to get in on the action. He totaled just 66 yards on his 19 touches on the day, and he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all. He'll have a good opportunity to bounce back next week in a favorable matchup against the Commanders.

news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 20 times for 60 yards and caught 3-of-4 targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Cam Skattebo totals 100 yards Sunday
news.impact: On Sunday, Skattebo was practically New York's entire offense. He was the team's leader in rushing and receiving yards, and he nearly doubled the yards of the next closest skill-position player. His workload is elite at this point, but he isn't likely to be a strong fantasy option moving forward given how weak this New York offense is looking without QB Jaxson Dart (knee).

news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 12 times for 36 yards and caught four passes for 19 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Cam Skattebo inefficient in loss Monday
news.impact: Skattebo was pretty well bottled up on Monday night. He was only able to rush for 36 yards at an inefficient clip of 3.0 yards per carry, and he didn't add much in the passing game outside of four receptions. New York's offense as a whole was a mess with injuries in this game, but the young running back will have ample opportunities to bounce back with matchups against the Titans and Cardinals coming up over the next two weeks.

news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.head: Cam Skattebo leads team in rushing Sunday
news.impact: Skattebo looked pretty solid in his first game back from an injury that ended his 2025 season early. He led the team in rushing yards and scored a touchdown against the Cowboys, and he was clearly the team's top RB in terms of carries, outnumbering the next closest back three to one in that area. He didn't see a single target or catch over the course of the night, however. If Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy Jr. continue to serve as the team's primary receiving backs, Skattebo's fantasy ceiling could be capped by that on a week-to-week basis.

news.body: Chase Brown rushed the ball nine times for ten yards and hauled in 11 catches for 71 yards in Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: Chase Brown hauls in 11 passes Sunday
news.impact: Brown was very ineffective as a rusher on Sunday, finishing with just ten yards in a loss to the Jaguars. He was able to contribute heavily through the passing game, however, logging 71 yards on a whopping 11 catches. The Bengals may need to lean on him in the passing game again next week with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both at risk to be sidelined against the Dolphins.

news.body: Chase Brown rushed for 61 yards on 13 carries in a 30-27 loss to the Steelers. He caught both of his targets for eight yards.
news.head: Chase Brown quiet in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Brown saw a season low in rushing attempts and targets. Despite the lower volume against Pittsburgh, fantasy managers should expect Brown to remain the workhorse running back for the Bengals in Week 4 against the Jaguars.

news.body: Chase Brown ran for 80 yards on 20 carries in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also caught 3-of-5 targets for two yards receiving.
news.head: Chase Brown sees 20 carries Sunday
news.impact: Brown did not find the end zone. He ran well, but it was still a fairly quiet day for him overall for fantasy managers. He'll remain an RB1 against the Steelers next week.

news.body: Chase Brown ran for 56 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers. He also caught 5-of-6 targets for 22 yards receiving.
news.head: Chase Brown finds the end zone Sunday
news.impact: Brown did not have the most efficient afternoon, but it still got the job done for fantasy managers. He draws a tougher matchup in Week 2 against the Texans.

news.body: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said RB Chris Brooks is still undergoing tests on an ankle injury.
news.head: Chris Brooks (ankle) undergoing tests
news.impact: Brooks ran for 30 yards on four carries in Sunday's win over the Buccaneers. There should be an update on his status by Wednesday.

news.body: Chris Brooks carried the ball four times for 30 yards and added a five-yard catch in a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers in Week 4.
news.head: Chris Brooks runs for 30 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Brooks injured his ankle during the second quarter and did not return. It remains to be seen if the injury is serious. MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson will split the backfield while Brooks is sidelined.

news.body: Packers RB Chris Brooks (ankle) is questionable to return against Tampa Bay.
news.head: Chris Brooks (ankle) questionable to return
news.impact: Brooks exits the game in the second quarter as the leading rusher for the Packers. MarShawn Lloyd will serve as the primary running back with Brooks sidelined.

news.body: Chris Brooks rushed four times for 11 yards while also catching one of his two targets for 15 yards in the Packers' 20-17 win over the New York Jets in Week 2.
news.head: Chris Brooks sees five touches in Week 2
news.impact: Brooks has struggled to make an impact out of the backfield to begin the season, finishing with less than 30 offensive yards in each of the first two games. The running back is difficult to trust as part of an underwhelming Green Bay backfield to begin the season, with a Week 3 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.body: Chris Rodriguez Jr. rushed the ball six times for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Chris Rodriguez Jr. scores once in win Sunday
news.impact: Rodriguez was able to contribute on Sunday, finishing with a touchdown in the team's narrow win over the Bengals. He saw 13 less opportunities than Bhayshul Tuten over the course of the afternoon, however, so he will clearly continue to be a depth contributor for the Jaguars for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Chris Rodriguez Jr. rushed the ball eight times for 37 times and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Chris Rodriguez Jr. finds end zone Sunday
news.impact: Rodriguez was clearly the RB2 for the Jaguars on Sunday, but he was still able to contribute quite effectively for them with 37 yards and a touchdown on just eight carries. Still, his current workload won't be enough to offer any sustained fantasy success anytime soon.

news.body: Chris Rodriguez Jr. carried the ball six times for 13 yards and was not targeted in the passing game in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Chris Rodriguez Jr. held to 13 yards in Week 2
news.impact: Rodriguez was quiet in the loss while Bhayshul Tuten went for 65 rushing yards and scored a one-yard touchdown. It appears that Tuten is pulling away from Rodriguez in the Jaguars' backfield committee after easily outproducing him across the first two games of the season. Rodriguez will not be a strong fantasy option heading into Week 3 against New England.

news.body: Chris Rodriguez Jr. ran six times for 23 yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 Week 1 win over the Browns.
news.head: Chris Rodriguez Jr. quiet in win over Browns
news.impact: Rodriguez wasn't involved much in the blowout win, carrying the ball only six times. It's possible the team wanted to see more of Tuten today than CRod, but that's purely speculation. As for now, it's hard to start Rodriguez until we know more about what his workload could look like on a weekly basis.

news.body: Christian McCaffrey rushed 15 times for 52 yards and a touchdown while catching three of his five targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Christian McCaffrey scores touchdown in win Sunday
news.impact: McCaffrey didn't have his biggest day from a yardage standpoint, but he found the end zone on a one-yard run in the fourth quarter. He finished with 18 touches and remains the clear lead back in San Francisco. McCaffrey remains a must-start option heading into Week 5 against Seattle.

news.body: Christian McCaffrey ran for 75 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries in the 49ers 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. He also caught 4-of-5 targets for 41 yards receiving.
news.head: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone Sunday
news.impact: McCaffrey took over as the clear lead back on Sunday. He found the end zone in the fourth quarter as the Cardinals were making a comeback. He remains a strong RB1 moving forward.

news.body: Christian McCaffrey (rest) did not take part in San Francisco's practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Christian McCaffrey (rest) doesn't practice Wednesday
news.impact: McCaffrey was given Wednesday off as a veteran rest day, which is normal for him at the first practice of the week. He should be a full go for Sunday's game and remains a must-start fantasy option in all league formats for as long as he stays healthy and on the field.

news.body: Christian McCaffrey gained 23 yards on 10 carries and 43 yards on four catches, scoring twice on the ground in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.head: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone twice in Week 2
news.impact: The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Week 2, but McCaffrey did score a pair of one-yard plunges. As usual, the dual-threat back was also active in the passing game. McCaffrey is up to 29 total touches through two games, averaging 4.6 yards per carry and 7.0 yards per reception. The 49ers appear to be capping the 30-year-old's usage a bit, but he's still a clear RB1, particularly in PPR formats, when healthy.

news.body: Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
news.head: Chuba Hubbard delivers big performance Sunday night
news.impact: The Lions' defense could not stop the pass or the run Sunday night. Hubbard turned in his highest rushing total since December 2024 in this contest. The 27-year-old back has now gained more than 200 yards on 39 carries over the last two weeks, proving himself capable of being a workhorse back yet again. Hubbard will return to the field for a matchup with the Eagles in Week 6.

news.body: Chuba Hubbard (rest) was a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Chuba Hubbard (rest) a full participant Thursday
news.impact: Hubbard was able to practice in a full capacity on Thursday, which was the expectation from the start. He should be a full go for Week 4 and remains a must-start fantasy option at this point in the season.

news.body: Chuba Hubbard was back at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Chuba Hubbard (rest) returns to practice Thursday
news.impact: Hubbard got a rest day from practice to open the week on Wednesday. He remains a strong RB2 for fantasy managers.

news.body: Chuba Hubbard (rest) did not take part in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Chuba Hubbard (rest) doesn't practice Wednesday
news.impact: Carolina is making some efforts to limit Hubbard's workload, giving him the day off on Wednesday to recover from any bumps and bruises that he has sustained through the first few weeks of the season. He should be back at practice on Thursday and is expected to be a full go for Sunday night's matchup against the Lions.

news.body: David Montgomery ran for 24 yards on 10 carries in the Texans 34-30 loss against the Cowboys.
news.head: David Montgomery shut down Sunday
news.impact: Montgomery continued his recent struggles on the ground. Woody Marks was the running back to find the end zone again. He'll be a low-end RB2/flex play next week against the Titans.

news.body: David Montgomery rushed for 33 yards on 11 carries in a 19-17 loss to the Colts. He caught both targets for 15 yards.
news.head: David Montgomery quiet in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Montgomery continues to struggle, tallying 43 rushing yards on 17 carries over the last two games. The veteran also saw Woody Marks come into the game on a short-yardage touchdown run in the forth quarter. Montgomery and the Texans will take on the Cowboys in Week 4.

news.body: David Montgomery ran for 10 yards on six carries in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught 2-of-2 targets for 14 yards receiving.
news.head: David Montgomery sees just six carries Sunday
news.impact: After a huge Week 1 performance, it was a game to forget for Montgomery and the entire Texans run game. He'll look to bounce back next week against the Colts.

news.body: David Montgomery rushed for 60 yards and two scores on 20 carries, adding three receptions for 19 yards and another touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.head: David Montgomery has big debut for Texans
news.impact: Montgomery was given 23 touches in his debut with the Texans, as the veteran back was a focal point of the offense. Granted, he only averaged 3.0 yards per carry, but he found the end zone three times while being involved both on the ground and through the air.

news.body: Derrick Henry rushed for 73 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in the Ravens win over the Titans. He caught both of his targets for six yards.
news.head: Derrick Henry finds the end zone in Week 4 win
news.impact: Henry opened the scoring with a five-yard plunge into the end zone in the first quarter. The veteran running back has found the end zone at least once in each of the team's first four games. Fantasy managers should expect Henry to remain a key factor for the Ravens heading into a Week 5 matchup in Atlanta.

news.body: Derrick Henry carried the ball 26 times for 89 yards and two touchdowns while catching his lone target for no gain in a 34-31 win over the Cowboys in Week 3.
news.head: Derrick Henry scores two more TDs in Week 3
news.impact: Henry continued to dominate in the high-scoring win over the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro. The veteran running back punched in scores from three and four yards out in the win, giving him six touchdowns through the first three games of the season. Overall, he's rushed for 301 yards while adding five catches for 38 yards this year. Henry will be a high-end RB1 in Week 4 against the Titans.

news.body: Derrick Henry rushed for 68 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints. He caught all three of his targets for 19 yards.
news.head: Derrick Henry finds the end zone in Week 2
news.impact: Henry found the end zone on a one-yard rush in the first quarter. The veteran was held in check after that, unable to find any big gains on the ground. Henry and the Ravens will take on Dallas in Week 3.

news.body: Derrick Henry carried the ball 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns while also hauling in his lone target for 19 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Derrick Henry rushes for three touchdowns in Week 1 win over Colts
news.impact: Henry capitalized on a sizeable workload out of the Baltimore backfield, averaging an impressive 6.0 yards per carry in the Week 1 win. The superstar running back remains locked in as a reliable RB1 ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

news.body: Emanuel Wilson ran for 81 yards and a touchdown on 21 carries in the Seahawks 30-23 win over the Chargers. He also caught 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards receiving and another score.
news.head: Emanuel Wilson scores twice Sunday
news.impact: After a fumble on a muffled punt by the Chargers early, Wilson took a screen pass from Sam Darnold to the house for the first score of the day. He was the clear workhorse in the first game since Jadarian Price was placed on IR.

news.body: Emanuel Wilson rushed nine times for 14 yards in the Seahawks’ 33-31 loss to the Washington Commanders in Week 3.
news.head: Emanuel Wilson quiet in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Wilson has struggled to make an impact out of the backfield to begin the season, recording less than 10 carries in two of three contests. The running back remains difficult to trust in a Seattle backfield with more questions than answers currently, with a Week 4 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.body: Emanuel Wilson ran 21 times for 92 yards and failed to catch his only target in Seattle's 31-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.head: Emanuel Wilson goes for 92 yards in win over Arizona
news.impact: Wilson led the Seahawks backfield in the big win, out-touching Jadarian Price on the ground 21 to 13. He's a speculative add at best as the Seahawks continue to rotate running backs.

news.body: Emanuel Wilson rushed the ball two times for three yards in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Emanuel Wilson uninvolved in win Wednesday
news.impact: There were many questions about Seattle's backfield split over the course of the offseason, and we finally got some answers on Wednesday. One of the takeaways is that Wilson is not likely to be a significant contributor in the rotation, as he saw just two out of the team's 20 RB rushing attempts on the night. It looks like Jadarian Price and George Holani have squarely established themselves as the top two backs on this team, with Wilson being a distant third.

news.body: Emmett Johnson caught his lone target for a 10-yard gain in a 30-27 win over the Raiders in Week 4.
news.head: Emmett Johnson hauls in 10-yard pass in Week 4
news.impact: Johnson did not record a carry as Kenneth Walker III dominated the backfield work in the win. Johnson will continue to mix in behind Walker as a high-end fantasy handcuff moving forward. He will be on bye in Week 5 before a Week 6 matchup against the Chargers.

news.body: Emmett Johnson rushed six times for 17 yards in the Chiefs' 24-10 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 3.
news.head: Emmett Johnson sees six touches in Week 3
news.impact: Johnson has struggled to make an impact out of the backfield to begin the season, finishing with less than 25 rushing yards in each of the first three contests. The running back remains more of a handcuff option for Kenneth Walker owners ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

news.body: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Emmett Johnson will continue to get more and more snaps.
news.head: Emmett Johnson expected to continue to see more snaps
news.impact: Reid added that Johnson will see more snaps and take some of the workload off of Kenneth Walker. The rookie has flashed in a limited role over the first two weeks of the season. He remains a solid stash for fantasy managers in his current role.

news.body: Emmett Johnson rushed the ball two times for 25 yards and caught two passes for 20 yards in Sunday's 33-30 OT win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Emmett Johnson a non-factor Sunday
news.impact: The Chiefs didn't give Johnson much work in their close overtime win on Sunday night. He saw just four touches over the course of the game, but he was still able to turn that into an efficient 35 yards. He shouldn't be considered much more than a handcuff fantasy option at this point in the season.

news.body: George Holani ran for 18 yards on seven carries in the Seahawks 30-23 win over the Chargers.
news.head: George Holani sees seven carries Sunday
news.impact: Emanuel Wilson was the workhorse in the Seahawks backfield. Holani remains off the fantasy radar.

news.body: George Holani (rib) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: George Holani (rib) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: Holani's rib injury isn't serious at this point and won't prevent him from playing in Week 4. He will continue to split the backfield with Emmanuel Wilson now that rookie Jadarian Price (chest) has been ruled out for this matchup against the Chargers.

news.body: George Holani (rib) was limited at practice on Thursday.
news.head: George Holani (rib) limited Thursday
news.impact: Holani was able to log another limited practice session on Thursday. It looks like he's going to play in Week 4, and he may see more work than usual with Jadarian Price (chest) trending the wrong way and Zach Charbonnet (knee) still awaiting clearance to play after recently making his return to the practice field.

news.body: George Holani was limited in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: George Holani (rib) limited in practice Wednesday
news.impact: Holani remains off the fantasy radar in his current role in the Seahawks backfield.

news.body: Isaiah Davis did not record a carry in a 23-12 loss to the Bears in Week 4.
news.head: Isaiah Davis held without a touch in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Davis appeared in line to work behind Braelon Allen with Breece Hall (quad) out but Allen was the only New York running back to record a touch. Davis will hope for a larger role in Week 5's home matchup against the Browns.

news.body: Isaiah Davis (knee) has been cleared to play in Week 1's matchup against the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Isaiah Davis (knee) cleared to play Week 1
news.impact: Davis will be available to play in Week 1, as his knee injury is nothing more than a minor issue at this point. He isn't expected to have much of a role on Sunday, especially with Breece Hall (groin) fully healthy and set to play against the Titans.

news.body: Isaiah Davis (knee) was a full participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Isaiah Davis (knee) full participant Wednesday
news.impact: Davis was a full participant for the Jets on Wednesday. He's still listed on the injury report due to a knee injury, but it shouldn't affect his availability for Week 1. He will continue to play a depth role in this backfield behind Breece Hall moving forward.

news.body: Jets RB Isaiah Davis will miss a couple of weeks.
news.head: Isaiah Davis (knee) to miss a couple of weeks
news.impact: It is unclear how serious the injury is. “He had a minor knee [injury],” Jets coach Aaron Glenn said. “He’ll be out maybe a couple of weeks, but he’ll be back.
