I’m confident that he’ll be just fine going into the regular season.” Davis is expected to compete for a depth role in the Jets backfield alongside Braelon Allen.

news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 15 yards on nine carries in the Commanders loss to the Colts. He caught 2-of-4 passes for 35 yards.
news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt quiet in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt and the entire Commanders' rushing attack struggled to get anything going against the Colts. With the current quarterback situation in Washington, Croskey-Merritt and the rest of the running backs could be asked to see more work in a Week 5 matchup with the Giants.

news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 19 times for 36 yards while also hauling in his only target for seven yards in the Commanders’ 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt bottled up in Week 3 win
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt has struggled to make an impact out of the backfield of late, rushing for less than 50 yards in each of the last two games. The running back remains a risky lineup option in all formats ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 43 yards on 12 carries and caught his lone target for five yards in the loss to Dallas Sunday.
news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt sees 12 carries in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt was out targeted by Rachaad White 6-to-1, but each tallied 43 yards on the ground. The Commanders' offense took a massive blow losing Jayden Daniels to a dislocated elbow, so the running game will likely be relied upon more heading into Week 3.

news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt carried the ball 16 times for 63 yards and one touchdown while also catching his only target for a loss of seven yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt reaches end zone in Week 1 loss
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt made the most of his opportunities out of the backfield, accounting for 50% of the carries for the Commanders in Week 1. The running back seems poised to receive as much volume as he can handle as the primary option out of the backfield to begin the season for head coach Dan Quinn, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.body: The Seahawks placed RB Jadarian Price on injured reserve.
news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) placed on IR
news.impact: Price aggravated a chest injury during Wednesday's practice. He will now miss at least four games. Emanuel Wilson and George Holani will lead the backfield with Zach Charbonnet returning as early as next week.

news.body: Jadarian Price has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) ruled out Sunday
news.impact: Price was unable to practice this week due to a chest injury. Emanuel Wilson becomes a potential flex streamer this week.

news.body: Jadarian Price (chest) was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) downgraded to non-participant Thursday
news.impact: The rookie was limited at practice to start the week on Wednesday, but he has since been downgraded and was a non-participant on Thursday. He seems to be trending the wrong way for Week 4, and fantasy managers should expect George Holani (rib) to see a lot of work if Price is unable to play on Sunday.

news.body: Jadarian Price was limited in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) limited in practice Wednesday
news.impact: Price has fumbled each of the past two weeks with last week's turnover leading to him being benched for most of the first half. He is a risky RB2/flex play for now.

news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 46 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries, adding 31 yards on four catches in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs finds the end zone in Week 4
news.impact: Gibbs was limited to a season-low 77 yards of offense Sunday, but he still found the end zone for the seventh time in four weeks. The Panthers' defense did a solid job of holding Gibbs to 3.1 yards per carry and another season-low of four receptions. Still, the dynamic back remains an elite, dual-threat option heading to Arizona in Week 5.

news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 99 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries in a 31-24 win over the Jets. He caught 7-of-8 targets for 65 yards and a touchdown.
news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs tallies three touchdowns in Week 3 win
news.impact: Gibbs continues to impress this season, tallying six touchdowns in his first three games of the season. He caught an 11-yard pass in the fourth quarter to put the Lions on top of the Jets to seal the win. Gibbs and the Lions will take on the Panthers in Week 4.

news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed the ball 16 times for 52 yards and caught 6-of-8 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs plays well in loss Thursday
news.impact: Thursday's game wasn't great for Gibbs in terms of efficiency, but he was still able to accumulate over 100 yards and a touchdown on Thursday night, which left him with a great fantasy total in this shootout matchup against the Bills. He will continue to be a top-tier fantasy option at the RB position for the remainder of the season, provided he remains healthy for most of it.

news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs carried the ball 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns while also hauling in all five of his targets for 30 yards in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs leads backfield attack in Week 1 win over Saints
news.impact: Gibbs was dynamic out of the backfield for head coach Dan Campbell, averaging 5.4 yards per carry in the win. The running back remains an explosive RB1 option in all formats, with a Week 2 road matchup against the Buffalo Bills up next.

news.body: James Cook III rushed for 75 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in the loss to the Patriots. He caught both of his targets for eight yards.
news.head: James Cook III finds the end zone in Week 4
news.impact: Cook averaged 6.3 yards per carry on his 12 carries, providing the Bills with an incredibly efficient effort. Despite the strong performance, his 12 rushing attempts are a new season low. Cook and the Bills will take on the Rams in Week 5.

news.body: James Cook III carried the ball 24 times for 154 yards and one touchdown with one fumble lost in the Bills' 24-16 Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: James Cook III dominates on ground in Week 3 win over Chargers
news.impact: Cook III has been dynamic out of the backfield of late, rushing for over 130 yards with one touchdown in each of the last two contests. The running back remains an explosive RB1 option in all formats ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the New England Patriots.

news.body: James Cook III rushed the ball 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.head: James Cook III plays well in win Thursday
news.impact: Buffalo's offense was firing on all cylinders on Thursday night, and that included Cook. He rushed for 135 yards at an efficient clip of 6.5 yards per carry on the night and was able to get into the end zone on one of those carries. He wasn't very involved in the passing game, but he still dominated the backfield and was the only running back to receive even a single opportunity for the Bills.

news.body: James Cook III ran 13 times for 57 yards and caught three of four targets for 12 yards in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.head: James Cook III goes for 69 yards in big win over Texans
news.impact: Cook was fine on his touches and was saved by his three receptions in PPR formats, but it fantasy managers will be hoping for more. He’s still a premium running back, and he will get his chance early this week as the Bills play the Lions on Thursday night.

news.body: Jaylen Warren rushed for 93 yards on 17 carries and caught 3-of-6 targets for 33 yards in Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
news.head: Jaylen Warren gains 126 yards of offense Thursday night
news.impact: With backfield mate Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined again, Warren took advantage of a workhorse load for the second straight game. He has yet to find the end zone this season, but Warren is averaging an elite 5.6 yards per carry while gaining over 300 yards on the ground through four games. He has also hauled in 13 of 19 targets for better than 35 yards per game. Warren is locked in as an RB2, especially in PPR formats.

news.body: Jaylen Warren rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries in a 30-27 win over the Bengals. He caught 3-of-4 targets for 49 yards.
news.head: Jaylen Warren excellent in Week 3 win
news.impact: Warren averaged 7.5 yards per carry and he dominated the rushing attempts with Rico Dowdle (toe) inactive Sunday. With the Steelers taking on the Browns on Thursday, Warren could be in line for a similar workload if Dowdle is unable to play.

news.body: Steelers RB Jaylen Warren (shoulder) is officially active for a Week 3 matchup with the Bengals.
news.head: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) officially active for Week 3
news.impact: Warren was limited in practice throughout the week but will play and start against the Bengals. With Rico Dowdle (toe) inactive, Warren could be in line for a workhorse role in Week 3.

news.body: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) is expected to play on Sunday against the Bengals after being listed with a shoulder injury this week. He was able to get some limited practice sessions in later in the week, and is likely good to go.
news.head: Jaylen Warren (shoulder) expected to play against Cincy
news.impact: Fellow RB Rico Dowdle is out for the game, so Warren’s availability is crucial for the team that lacks an experienced back behind him. He should be an RB2 with upside thanks to his pass catching skillset.

news.body: Jaylen Wright carried the ball five times for seven yards in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Jaylen Wright quiet in loss Sunday
news.impact: Wright didn't see a large workload on Sunday. He finished with just five carries for seven yards against the Vikings, and he wasn't able to get involved in the passing game either. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him moving forward.

news.body: Jaylen Wright (foot) is officially good to go for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Jaylen Wright (foot) officially good to go for Sunday
news.impact: As expected, Wright is off of Miami's injury report heading into the weekend and should be a full go against the Vikings on Sunday. Week 4 will be very telling on how the backfield reps will be split between him and Ollie Gordon II in the absence of De'Von Achane (knee), so fantasy managers should keep tabs on what his workload looks like this week.

news.body: Jaylen Wright (foot) should be "good to go," according to Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley on Friday.
news.head: Jaylen Wright (foot) expected to play Sunday
news.impact: Wright practiced in full on Thursday and is expected to be on the field Sunday. With De'Von Achane (knee) done for the season, the Dolphins need all the RB depth they can get. After missing Week 3, Wright should share the load with Ollie Gordon.

news.body: Jaylen Wright (foot) was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Jaylen Wright (foot) upgraded to full participant Thursday
news.impact: Wright was able to log a full practice session on Thursday after being limited by a foot injury on Wednesday. It seems like he's trending towards playing in Week 4, and if he does, he and Ollie Gordon II are both primed for a sharp increase in work with De'Von Achane (knee) set to be sidelined for the remainder of the season.

news.body: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love was dealing with an ankle injury on Sunday.
news.head: Jeremiyah Love dealt with ankle injury Sunday
news.impact: LaFleur clarified that Love's discomfort in Sunday's game is not the same ankle from the sprain he suffered in the preseason. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week.

news.body: Jeremiyah Love rushed the ball 14 times for 63 yards and caught one pass for -8 yards in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Jeremiyah Love underwhelming in loss Sunday
news.impact: The rookie didn't put up a good game on Sunday, netting just 55 total yards in the team's loss to the Giants. He is apparently dealing with some bumps and bruises of some kind and didn't see many touches in the second half as a result. Fantasy managers should keep close tabs on updates about his health throughout this next week of practice.

news.body: Jeremiyah Love ran for 90 yards on 21 carries in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday. He also caught 5-of-5 targets for 19 yards receiving and a touchdown.
news.head: Jeremiyah Love has career day Sunday
news.impact: Love totaled a career-high 26 touches. It was the first game so far where he clearly out-snapped Tyler Allgeier. He'll look to continue the workhorse role into next week against the Giants.

news.body: Jeremiyah Love ran nine times for 29 yards and caught three passes for 16 yards in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to Seattle.
news.head: Jeremiyah Love struggles in loss to Seattle
news.impact: Like the rest of the Cardinals' offense, Love struggled to move the ball against the Seahawks' stout defense. He will face yet another tough matchup next week, as Arizona takes on San Francisco.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins rushed 11 times for 40 yards, while RJ Harvey had seven carries for 25 yards in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Harvey also caught 10 passes for 68 yards out of the backfield.
news.head: J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey struggle in loss Sunday
news.impact: Denver couldn't get much going on the ground, with Dobbins and Harvey combining for just 65 rushing yards. Dobbins, however, continued to handle more of the rushing work. Harvey, meanwhile, was much more involved as a receiver and ended up leading the Broncos' offense in both receptions and receiving yards. The backfield remains a split, with Dobbins having the better chance at early-down work and Harvey carrying more upside in the passing game.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the 49ers.
news.head: J.K. Dobbins (hip) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Dobbins will remain a touchdown dependent low-end RB2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins is practicing in full for Week 4 against the 49ers.
news.head: J.K. Dobbins (hip) practicing in full for Week 4
news.impact: Dobbins will remain in his lead role in the Broncos backfield.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins rushed the ball 17 times for 49 yards and caught 1-of-2 passes for four yards in Sunday night's 30-26 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: J.K. Dobbins leads team in rushing Sunday
news.impact: Dobbins saw the vast majority of carries out of the backfield on Sunday night, but he wasn't able to make much out of them, finishing with just 49 rushing yards in a narrow win over the Rams. He will likely maintain a large workload moving forward, however, especially now that rookie Jonah Coleman (ankle) has been placed on injured reserve.

news.body: The Broncos placed RB Jonah Coleman on injured reserve.
news.head: Jonah Coleman (ankle) placed on IR
news.impact: Coleman had already been ruled out for this week's game. He will now miss at least the next four games. J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey will continue to lead the Broncos backfield.

news.body: Jonah Coleman (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Jonah Coleman (ankle) ruled out for Sunday
news.impact: The rookie will be forced to miss a game after suffering an ankle injury last week. Both J.K. Dobbins (hip) and RJ Harvey (hamstring) have been cleared to play on Sunday night, however, so Denver's backfield will continue to function as it usually does this week against the Rams.

news.body: Jonah Coleman (ankle) did not take part in Denver's practice on Thursday.
news.head: Jonah Coleman (ankle) doesn't practice Thursday
news.impact: The rookie has now missed two-straight practices to start the week, so he seems to have an uphill battle to play in Week 3. RJ Harvey (hamstring) and J.K. Dobbins (hip) are both back to practicing in full, so it looks like they will be the two guys holding things down for Denver's backfield on Sunday.

news.body: Jonah Coleman (ankle) was officially a non-participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Jonah Coleman (ankle) officially a non-participant Wednesday
news.impact: Initial reports indicates that the rookie may have been practicing for the Broncos on Wednesday, but it turns out that he was a non-participant because of the ankle issue that he's dealing with. He is currently trending the wrong way for Week 3, and his absence would likely lead to more work for RJ Harvey (hamstring) against the Rams.

news.body: Jonathan Taylor rushed for 95 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries in the win over the Commanders. He caught 1-of-4 targets for two yards.
news.head: Jonathan Taylor finds the end zone twice in Week 4 win
news.impact: Taylor found the end zone on a pair of five-yard touchdown runs in the second and third quarter. Taylor's strong 2026 season continues, as he has three multi-touchdown games in the team's first four games. Taylor and the Colts will take on the Steelers in Week 5.

news.body: Jonathan Taylor rushed for 68 yards on 23 carries in a 19-17 win over Houston. He caught 2-of-3 targets for four yards.
news.head: Jonathan Taylor held in check in Week 3 win
news.impact: Taylor continues to receive plenty of touches in the Colts' offense this season, but struggled to make the most of them in Week 3. His 72 total yards are a season low for Taylor. He will look to bounce back against the Commanders in Week 4.

news.body: Jonathan Taylor rushed the ball 24 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns while adding four receptions for 40 yards through the air in Sunday night's 33-30 OT loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Jonathan Taylor scores twice in overtime loss Sunday
news.impact: Taylor was the engine for Indianapolis' offense on Sunday night. He totaled 132 yards over the course of the night and was able to score two touchdowns on the ground. He has been very strong to start the season and should continue to be considered an elite fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Jonathan Taylor carried the ball 19 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns while also catching three of his four targets for 23 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.head: Jonathan Taylor rushes for two touchdowns in Week 1 loss
news.impact: Taylor was the lone bright spot in an underwhelming Colts offense to begin the season, averaging 5.2 yards per carry in the loss. The superstar running back will look to remain an impactful backfield option in Week 2 against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.body: Jonathon Brooks (core) is expected to be sidelined for around 6-8 weeks.
news.head: Jonathon Brooks (core) expected to miss 6-8 weeks
news.impact: The Panthers recently placed Brooks on injured reserve due to a core injury that he suffered last week. HC Dave Canales told reporters that he is expected to be sidelined for 6-8 weeks, which puts him in line for a return sometime in November. Chuba Hubbard is now expected to be Carolina's workhorse running back for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Jonathon Brooks (core) was officially placed on IR on Wednesday.
news.head: Jonathon Brooks (core) officially on IR
news.impact: Brooks had core muscle surgery on Wednesday and will be out for at least four weeks on IR. The 23-year-old's timetable is actually projected to be around six weeks. Chuba Hubbard will continue to shoulder the load ouf of the backfield for the Panthers.

news.body: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is expected to undergo surgery on his core to repair an injury he sustained on Sunday. His expected time to recover is six weeks and is expected to land on IR.
news.head: Jonathon Brooks (groin) undergoing surgery, will miss about 6 weeks
news.impact: It’s a tough blow for Brooks, who had just gotten back to the playing field after roughly two years away from it. When Brooks returns, he’ll still have time to make some noise before the season ends, but there’s no telling how much work he will get. Chuba Hubbard will carry the load in Carolina with Brooks out, so be expecting at least RB2 numbers from him thanks to volume.

news.body: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said RB Jonathon Brooks is undergoing tests on his groin injury.
news.head: Jonathon Brooks (groin) undergoing tests
news.impact: The team is still gathering information on the severity of the injury. There should be an update on Brooks this week.

news.body: Jordan Mason (thumb) has been placed on injured reserve, knocking him out for at least the next four weeks.
news.head: Jordan Mason (thumb) placed on injured reserve
news.impact: Surprisingly, Mason is being placed on injured reserve due to a thumb injury that he is dealing with. It's not expected to be a long-term issue for him, but he is going to be sidelined for at least the next four weeks while he recovers. Aaron Jones Sr. will serve as the team's clear RB1 in his absence, with Minnesota also signing DeeJay Dallas to their active roster to help with depth.

news.body: Vikings head coach O'Connell said RB Jordan Mason is being evaluated for a sore thumb.
news.head: Jordan Mason being evaluated for sore thumb
news.impact: Mason came into the building on Monday with the injury. He is day-to-day for now after leading the backfield on Sunday.

news.body: Jordan Mason ran for 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.head: Jordan Mason sees 15 carries Sunday
news.impact: Mason led the way in the Vikings backfield as both he and Aaron Jones saw double-digit carries. He will be in the low-end RB2 conversation next week against the Bears.

news.body: Jordan Mason carried the ball 14 times for 94 yards as the Vikings defeated the Packers, 16-3, in the regular season finale.
news.head: Jordan Mason rushes for game-high 94 yards Sunday
news.impact: Mason finished his first season in Minnesota as the team's leading rusher with 758 yards despite only starting five games for the Vikings. His 94 yards on the ground on Sunday was his second-highest total of the season. With both Mason and Aaron Jones on affordable contracts for next season, the duo figure to form a similar backfield timeshare in 2026.

news.body: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs had his initial court appearance moved up to Sept. 10 from Nov. 17 regarding Jacobs' misdemeanor charges.
news.head: Josh Jacobs has court appearance date moved up
news.impact: Jacobs was charged with battery and criminal destruction of property and is scheduled to appear at the Brown County courthouse on Sept. 10, multiple days before Green Bay's season opener against Minnesota. It is unclear how this will affect his return timeline; Jacobs is currently on the commissioner's exempt list, with a potential suspension looming.

news.body: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said he expected Josh Jacobs to play for the team in 2026.
news.head: Josh Jacobs expected to play for Packers in 2026 per GM
news.impact: Gutekunst said he wants to let the process play out when asked if there’s a scenario in which the Packers release Jacobs. He was placed on the Commissioners Exempt List on Sunday. This will remain a situation to monitor.

news.body: Josh Jacobs has been placed on the commissioner exempt list by the National Football League according to Tom Pelissero.
news.head: Josh Jacobs placed on commissioner of exempt list
news.impact: Jacobs is now ineligible to practice or play for the Packers while the league continues their investigation into alleged improper behavior while being charged with two misdemeanors related to his conduct earlier in the week. If the running back is forced to sit out for any period of the regular season, MarShawn Lloyd will be in line to receive the majority of backfield work while the recently acquired Kaleb Johnson gets up to speed on the offensive playbook with Week 1 approaching.

news.body: Josh Jacobs has been charged with two misdemeanors following an incident in May. His initial court date is set for mid-November. The NFL is conducting its own investigation, and a suspension could soon follow.
news.head: Josh Jacobs charged with two misdemeanors stemming from May incident
news.impact: It's important to remember that the NFL has the ability to either suspend Jacobs at the start of the season or wait until the legal process is over. If they wait, then Jacobs will likely not face suspension until next year. If not, we could be looking at a potential 6-8 game absence, though that is more of an educated guess at this point. For anyone taking Jacobs in drafts right now, Marshawn Lloyd is a must-have handcuff and is a great target for Zero-RB builds.

news.body: Justice Hill carried the ball five times for 33 yards in a 34-31 win over the Cowboys in Week 3.
news.head: Justice Hill runs for 33 yards in Week 3 win
news.impact: Hill averaged 6.6 yards per carry in the exciting win over Dallas in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday. The veteran running back continues to mix in behind starter Derrick Henry, with Week 3 being his most productive game of the season. Hill will not be a strong fantasy option heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Titans.

news.body: Justice Hill rushed for six yards on two carries in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints.
news.head: Justice Hill quiet in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Hill was uninvolved in the passing game and saw his touches drop from Week 1. Fantasy managers should expect Hill to continue to see limited usage as long as Derrick Henry is healthy.

news.body: Justice Hill rushed six times for 18 yards while catching his only target for 10 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1.
news.head: Justice Hill sees seven touches in Week 1
news.impact: Hill operated as more of an afterthought out of the Baltimore backfield, with Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson finishing ahead of the running back in carries. He remains more of a change-of-pace option behind Henry ahead of a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

news.body: Ravens coach John Harbaugh said Justice Hill will be out three to four weeks with a neck injury.
news.head: Justice Hill (neck) to miss 3-to-4 weeks
news.impact: Hill will miss at least the next few weeks. He'll have a chance to still return this season.

news.body: Kaelon Black rushed six times for 13 yards in Sunday's 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Kaelon Black sees six carries in win Sunday
news.impact: Black saw some work behind Christian McCaffrey but wasn't able to do much with it, averaging just 2.2 yards per carry. He remains a lottery ticket in San Francisco's backfield and doesn't have standalone fantasy value as long as McCaffrey is healthy.

news.body: Kaelon Black ran for 17 yards on four carries in the 49ers 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.head: Kaelon Black quiet Sunday
news.impact: Black saw one target which he didn't haul in. Christian McCaffrey took over as the clear lead back on the afternoon. Black remains a stash for fantasy managers.

news.body: Kaelon Black gained 25 yards on seven carries in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.head: Kaelon Black gets seven carries in Week 2
news.impact: After gaining 65 yards on 14 carries in Week 1, Black saw his attempts cut in half in Week 2. The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Sunday's win, but Brock Purdy more than made up for that with his passing prowess. Black has gained 90 yards on 21 carries through two games, and he maintains decent fantasy value as the backup to Christian McCaffrey.

news.body: Kaelon Black (groin) is active for Week 2 for the San Francisco 49ers against the Miami Dolphins according to Nick Wagoner.
news.head: Kaelon Black (groin) active for Week 2
news.impact: Black is good to go after not experiencing any setbacks during pregame warmups for head coach Kyle Shanahan, offering another dynamic option alongside Christian McCaffrey out of the San Francisco backfield against the Dolphins Sunday.

news.body: Kaleb Johnson carried the ball eight times for 42 yards and lost a fumble in a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers in Week 4.
news.head: Kaleb Johnson runs for 42 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Johnson continued to split the carries three ways as MarShawn Lloyd got seven carries and Chris Brooks four. Johnson did most of his damage on a 31-yard run. The entire Green Bay running game has struggled this season, but Johnson appears to be the running back to roster in fantasy going forward. He will face the Bears in Week 5.

news.body: Kaleb Johnson ran four times for six yards and caught one of three targets for 10 yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons.
news.head: Kaleb Johnson goes for 16 scrimmage yards in loss
news.impact: Johnson had just as many carries as Marshawn Lloyd, but half the yards. He's not doing enough at this point to warrant taking over the backfield, so expect a split to continue.

news.body: Kaleb Johnson rushed eight times for 32 yards in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: Kaleb Johnson leads ground attack in Week 2 win
news.impact: Johnson made the most of modest involvement in his first game action of the season, averaging 4.0 yards per carry in the win. The running back could be in line for an increased workload as part of a difficult Green Bay backfield for fantasy managers to trust, with a Week 3 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.body: Kaleb Johnson is being traded to the Green Bay Packers by the Pittsburgh Steelers according to Tom Pelissero.
news.head: Kaleb Johnson traded to Packers
news.impact: Details of the trade are still being finalized between the two organizations, with Johnson receiving the fresh start the running back desperately needs after falling out of favor in a Pittsburgh backfield that will be led by the duo of Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle this upcoming season. Johnson’s role should become clearer as the National Football League continues their investigation into No. 1 running back Josh Jacobs, potentially resulting in a backup opportunity behind current No. 2 option MarShawn Lloyd.

news.body: Keaton Mitchell ran for 39 yards on 10 carries in the Chargers 30-23 loss against the Seahawks. He also caught 5-of-6 targets for 24 yards receiving.
news.head: Keaton Mitchell sees 10 carries Sunday
news.impact: Mitchell saw a team-high 10 carries on the day and 15 touches in total. It was a committee between him, Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal on Sunday.

news.body: Keaton Mitchell (ankle) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Keaton Mitchell (ankle) without injury designation for Sunday
news.impact: The veteran is going to be good to go on Sunday, despite being listed on the injury report throughout the week due to an ankle issue. He will continue to play second fiddle behind Omarion Hampton on this offense, although his exact snap share remains worth keeping an eye on this week.

news.body: Keaton Mitchell (ankle) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: Keaton Mitchell (ankle) limited again Thursday
news.impact: Mitchell was again a limited participant on Thursday due to the ankle injury that he's dealing with. It could leave him sidelined this week, in which case Kimani Vidal would be primed for more work in his absence.

news.body: Keaton Mitchell was wearing a walking boot on his left foot after practice.
news.head: Keaton Mitchell in walking boot
news.impact: Mitchell was listed as a limited participant in practice on Wednesday. His status will need to be monitored in practice the rest of the week.

news.body: Kendre Miller rushed the ball six times for just nine yards and lost a fumble in Monday night's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Kendre Miller struggles in loss Monday
news.impact: Miller had a bad game on Monday night. He totaled just 19 yards on the ground and through the air against the Falcons, and he also lost a costly fumble, which further hurt his fantasy total. He should not be started in any fantasy league formats moving forward, especially with Alvin Kamara still seeing the bulk of the work in New Orleans' backfield right now.

news.body: Kendre Miller ran for 14 yards on four carries in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday. He also caught 2-of-3 targets for five yards receiving.
news.head: Kendre Miller sees four carries Sunday
news.impact: Miller saw some opportunity with Travis Etienne Jr. exiting early. Alvin Kamara was still the lead back in that span.

news.body: Kendre Miller was back at practice on Friday.
news.head: Kendre Miller (illness) returns to practice Friday
news.impact: Miller had been absent due to an illness. He'll need to be monitored when the injury report is released.

news.body: Kendre Miller (illness) was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Kendre Miller (illness) downgraded to non-participant Thursday
news.impact: Miller is a new addition to New Orleans' injury report. He's dealing with some kind of an illness right now and wasn't able to practice on Thursday as a result. He's likely day-to-day for the time being, but of he's cleared to play on Sunday and Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) isn't, he will be primed for more work than usual against the Raiders.

news.body: Kenny Gainwell carried the ball three times for five yards and caught both of his targets for 22 yards and a touchdown in a 17-14 loss to the Packers in Week 4.
news.head: Kenny Gainwell catches TD in Week 4
news.impact: Gainwell found the end zone on a 10-yard pass from Jalon Daniels in the fourth quarter. It has been a quiet season thus far for Gainwell, who has just 26 rushing yards and eight catches for 44 yards through four games. He will be a low-end flex option in Week 5 vs. the Cowboys.

news.body: Kenny Gainwell ran for -4 yards on three carries in the Buccaneers 23-16 loss against the Vikings on Sunday. He also caught 2-of-5 targets for 14 yards receiving.
news.head: Kenny Gainwell quiet again Sunday
news.impact: Gainwell was once again not involved much. It is worth noting Bucky Irving was on the sideline for most of the final quarter. The status of Irving will need to be monitored this week.

news.body: Kenny Gainwell ran for 10 yards on two carries in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns. He also caught 3-of-4 targets for five yards receiving.
news.head: Kenny Gainwell remains in limited role Sunday
news.impact: Bucky Irving was the clear lead back for the second straight week. Gainwell remains a pure stash for fantasy managers in his current role.

news.body: Kenny Gainwell ran for 15 yards on five carries in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught his line target for three yards receiving.
news.head: Kenny Gainwell uninvolved Sunday
news.impact: This felt like the perfect time for Gainwell to make an impact with Tampa Bay falling behind 21-3 early, but it was Bucky Irving in the passing game out of the backfield who caught seven passes. Gainwell is a risky flex play for now in PPR leagues until we see him more involved.

news.body: Kimani Vidal ran for 25 yards on five carries in the Chargers 30-23 loss against the Seahawks. He also caught 2-of-3 targets for 11 yards receiving and a score.
news.head: Kimani Vidal hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Vidal caught the lone touchdown pass thrown by Justin Herbert on the day. It was a clear three-man committee in the Chargers backfield on Sunday between him, Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell.

news.body: Kimani Vidal rushed once for six yards while also catching one of his three targets for 14 yards in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 3.
news.head: Kimani Vidal sees two touches in Week 3
news.impact: Vidal has struggled to make an impact to begin the season, recording his first touches in three games in Sunday's loss. The running back can remain off rosters until further notice, with a Week 4 contest against the Seattle Seahawks up next.

news.body: The Chargers re-signed exclusive rights free agent Kimani Vidal to a one-year deal.
news.head: Kimani Vidal re-signs with Chargers on one-year deal
news.impact: Vidal figures to remain in a backup role behind Omarion Hampton in the Chargers backfield heading into next season. He'll remain a handcuff for fantasy managers.

news.body: Kimani Vidal rushed the ball three times for 12 yards in Sunday's 19-3 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Kimani Vidal uninvolved in Week 18 loss
news.impact: Vidal was cleared to play on Sunday after coming into the week with a neck issue of some kind. He didn't play much against the Broncos, however, touching the ball just four times in the team's loss. He will likely play a bigger role for them in the postseason, starting in a matchup against the Patriots next week.

news.body: Bears head coach Ben Johnson said RB Kyle Monangai is day-to-day with his thumb injury.
news.head: Kyle Monangai (thumb) day-to-day
news.impact: Monangai is coming off a huge performance in Sunday's win over the Jets. His status will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

news.body: Kyle Monangai (thumb) will be evaluated for a thumb injury on Monday.
news.head: Kyle Monangai (thumb) to be evaluated Monday
news.impact: According to the running back, he looked down at his hand before realizing any pain. His status is up in the air, so fantasy managers will need to monitor the situation as details emerge on whether he will miss time.

news.body: Kyle Monangai carried the ball 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns while catching his lone target for four yards in a 23-12 win over the Jets in Week 4.
news.head: Kyle Monangai runs for 146 yards, two TDs in Week 4 win
news.impact: Monangai dominated D'Andre Swift in the game as Swift lost a costly fumble and saw his playing time cut afterwards. Monangai rushed for touchdowns of one and five yards in the win. He will continue to split carries with Swift but it might be more of an even split after his Week 4 performance. He's on the flex radar in fantasy heading into Week 5 against the Packers.

news.body: Kyle Monangai carried the ball 10 times for 31 yards in a 27-7 win over the Eagles in Week 3's Monday night game.
news.head: Kyle Monangai rushes for 31 yards in Week 3 win
news.impact: Monangai mixed in behind starter D'Andre Swift. He was held to 3.1 yards per carry by the Philadelphia defense in the contest while failing to find the end zone for the second straight game. Monangai will continue to see a modest workload for the Bears but he won't be a very strong fantasy option unless Swift were forced to miss time. He will now prepare to take on the Jets in Week 4.

news.body: Kyren Williams rushed the ball 16 times for 80 yards and two touchdowns and caught 10-of-13 targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Kyren Williams dominant in win Sunday
news.impact: Williams had a stellar game in Week 4. He led team with 80 rushing yards, found the end zone two different times, and caught ten passes for 67 yards through the air in Sunday's win over the Eagles. Fantasy managers should be well pleased with this performance and with the fact that he has entirely pulled ahead of Blake Corum in terms of touches in close matchups.

news.body: Kyren Williams rushed the ball 15 times for 88 yards and caught 6-of-7 targets for 70 yards in Sunday night's 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Kyren Williams stellar in loss Sunday
news.impact: Williams had a great showing on Sunday night. He was the team's leading rusher and maintained great efficiency at 5.9 yards per carry, and he was also very involved in the passing game with six catches for 70 yards over the course of the night. He will likely continue to serve as the team's RB1 for the foreseeable future, even more so in close matchups like this one was.

news.body: Kyren Williams rushed the ball 12 times for 85 yards and caught two passes for 12 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.head: Kyren Williams finds end zone Monday
news.impact: Williams had a productive night on Monday. He led the team in rushing and fell just three yards shy of the 100-total yards mark over the course of the game, and he was also able to haul in a touchdown to put the cherry on top. Concerns still exist for his season-long outlook, though, with Blake Corum seeing just one less touch on the night and seemingly only getting better and better.

news.body: Kyren Williams ran 11 times for 41 yards and the Rams' only touchdown. He also caught all three of his targets for 24 receiving yards.
news.head: Kyren Williams punches in score in loss to Niners
news.impact: Williams' day was saved by the touchdown; otherwise it was fairly miserable. Blake Corum showed out in his opportunities, but he was limited to ground work only. Kyren appears to be in a committee now, but he at least has the edge in passing situations, giving him more appeal.

news.body: MarShawn Lloyd carried the ball seven times for 13 yards and caught all five of his targets for 36 yards in a 17-14 win over Tampa Bay in Week 4.
news.head: MarShawn Lloyd catches five passes in Week 4
news.impact: Lloyd struggled on the ground but he did some damage via the passing attack in the close win. The Packers continued with their three-man attack in the backfield with Kaleb Johnson getting eight carries and Chris Brooks four. No one has been able to find success running the ball in Green Bay this season, however. Lloyd will be a low-end flex option heading into Week 5 against the Bears.

news.body: MarShawn Lloyd ran four times for 11 yards and caught two of three targets for seven yards in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons.
news.head: MarShawn Lloyd snags two passes in loss
news.impact: Lloyd wasn't all that impressive in this game, but he was better than Kaleb Johnson this time out. The backfield is a mess right now with Josh Jacobs out, and everyone is struggling to run. Expect both Lloyd and Johnson to be irrelevant for fantasy moe often than not.

news.body: MarShawn Lloyd rushed six times for 20 yards while also hauling in both of his targets for six yards and one touchdown in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: MarShawn Lloyd catches touchdown in quiet Week 2 performance
news.impact: Lloyd has underwhelmed despite increased touches out of the Green Bay backfield to begin the season, finishing with less than 40 rushing yards in each of the first two games. The running back remains a risky option as part of a running back group leaving a lot to be desired, with a Week 3 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.body: MarShawn Lloyd ran for 37 yards on 13 carries in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings. He did not catch his lone target.
news.head: MarShawn Lloyd sees 13 carries Sunday
news.impact: Lloyd was the lead back in the Packers backfield without Josh Jacobs. He was very inefficient as he averaged less than three yards per carry. He'll be a flex play next week against the Jets.

news.body: Mike Washington Jr. carried the ball nine times for 18 yards and lost a yard on his lone catch in a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs in Week 4.
news.head: Mike Washington Jr. runs for 18 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Washington couldn't replicate his big game in Week 3, where he ran for 54 yards and a touchdown on just five carries. The rookie runner remains a solid fantasy handcuff in all leagues in case something happens to Ashton Jeanty. Washington will face the Patriots in Week 5.

news.body: Mike Washington Jr. ran for 54 yards and a touchdown on five carries in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
news.head: Mike Washington Jr. finds the end zone Sunday
news.impact: Washington found the end zone on an impressive run. He remains the clear backup behind Ashton Jeanty in the Raiders backfield.

news.body: Mike Washington Jr. rushed the ball three times for seven yards and failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Mike Washington Jr. uninvolved in loss Sunday
news.impact: Washington saw a decrease in opportunities on Sunday, falling to just three touches after having seven in the season opener a week ago. He isn't a big part of this offense right now and shouldn't be rostered in most league formats for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Mike Washington Jr. carried the ball seven times for 41 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Mike Washington Jr. sees seven touches in Week 1 win
news.impact: Washington Jr. was impactful operating behind Ashton Jeanty in the Las Vegas backfield, averaging 5.9 yards per carry in the win. The running back will look to continue to offer impactful touches as the primary handcuff to Jeanty in the Las Vegas backfield moving forward, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.body: Najee Harris rushed the ball nine times for 30 yards in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Najee Harris inefficient in win Sunday
news.impact: Harris remained involved on Sunday with nine carries over the course of the game, which was easily the second-most on the team. He wasn't able to do much with them and ended up with just 30 scoreless yards, however, so fantasy managers shouldn't have high expectations for him moving forward.

news.body: Najee Harris rushed the ball nine times for 52 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Najee Harris efficient in win Sunday
news.impact: The Giants were able to get Harris going on Sunday. He totaled 52 yards on just nine carries, which left him with an efficient clip of 5.8 yards per carry. He's still behind Cam Skattebo on this offense and isn't likely to be fantasy relevant moving forward, but he could eat more and more into the workload in this backfield if he continues to play well.

news.body: Najee Harris rushed the ball four times for six yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Najee Harris sees four carries in loss Monday
news.impact: Harris wasn't able to accomplish anything on the box score on Monday night, but it looks like he is starting to get involved on New York's offense. He saw the second-most carries out of anyone on the team, although he wasn't able to do much with them. It looks like he may be overtaking Tyrone Tracy Jr. in this backfield, who himself didn't see a single opportunity on offense against the Rams.

news.body: The Giants are signing RB Najee Harris.
news.head: Najee Harris signs with Giants
news.impact: Harris is working his way back from a torn Achilles suffered last season. He'll add depth in the backfield for the Giants behind Cam Skattebo.

news.body: Ollie Gordon II rushed the ball nine times for 100 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Ollie Gordon II plays well in loss Sunday
news.impact: Gordon was one of the only bright spots for Miami's offense this week. He finished with 100 yards and a touchdown on just nine carries, which left him with a great efficiency number in this game. He has clearly separated himself from Jaylen Wright in terms of talent and output, but they continue to be somewhat close together in terms of opportunities, which could limit Gordon moving forward.

news.body: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said all running backs on the roster are “going to have their roles.”
news.head: Ollie Gordon II: All RBs on Dolphins 'are going to have their roles'
news.impact: Gordon remains the most likely player to lead the backfield, but Jaylen Wright will figure to have a role when he is healthy. Gordon can be viewed as a borderline RB2 for now.

news.body: Ollie Gordon II carried the ball 17 times for 41 yards and one touchdown while also hauling in all three of his targets for 14 yards in the Dolphins' 24-10 Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Ollie Gordon II reaches end zone in Week 3 loss to Chiefs
news.impact: Gordon II took advantage of increased touches with De'Von Achane (knee) exiting early for head coach Jeff Hafley, posting more than three touches for the first time in three contests Sunday. The running back is in line to take over a No. 1 running back role with Achane expected to be sidelined for a significant amount of time according to Hafley, with a tough Week 4 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings up next.

news.body: Dolphins RB Ollie Gordon II (cramping) is questionable to return Sunday.
news.head: Ollie Gordon II (cramping) questionable to return
news.impact: Gordon jogged off to the locker room and is now officially questionable to return. This is a big blow to the Dolphins' offense with De'Von Achane (knee) already ruled out.

news.body: Omarion Hampton ran for 45 yards and a touchdown on nine carries in the Chargers 30-23 loss against the Seahawks. He also caught 2-of-2 targets for eight yards receiving.
news.head: Omarion Hampton finds the end zone Sunday
news.impact: Hampton saw just nine carries to 15 combined carries between Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. Hampton is a touchdown dependent flex play moving forward.

news.body: Omarion Hampton carried the ball 15 times for 56 yards while also failing to catch his lone target in the Chargers' 24-16 Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Omarion Hampton leads ground attack in Week 3 loss to Bills
news.impact: Hampton struggled to find consistent running room Sunday, rushing for less than 60 yards for the second time in the first three contests. The running back remains one of the more reliable options as part of an inconsistent Chargers offense to begin the season, with a Week 4 contest against the Seattle Seahawks up next.

news.body: Omarion Hampton rushed the ball 23 times for 94 yards and a touchdown and caught two passes for 21 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.head: Omarion Hampton scores once in loss Sunday
news.impact: Hampton was one of the lone bright spots for the Chargers on Sunday. He logged 115 total yards and found the end zone once over the course of the afternoon, though he left something to be desired in the passing game. He should continue to be a good fantasy option moving forward, though the present struggles of Los Angeles' offense may cap his upside from a fantasy perspective.

news.body: Omarion Hampton rushed for 43 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.head: Omarion Hampton finds the end zone in Week 1 loss
news.impact: A first-round pick in 2025, Hampton carried quite a bit of hype coming into his second NFL season, as did the Chargers' offense as a whole. At least some of that hype immediately died down after a disappointing season debut against a suspect Arizona defense, but it is only one game under new OC Mike McDaniel. Hampton found the end zone on an eight-yard run in the opening quarter, and this Chargers' attack will find its footing at some point. The Raiders are up next.

news.body: Quinshon Judkins rushed for 53 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries, adding 43 yards on six receptions in Thursday's 27-24 win over the Steelers.
news.head: Quinshon Judkins finds the end zone for the first time this season
news.impact: Judkins finally hit paydirt this season, plunging into the end zone from two yards out during the second quarter of Thursday's game. Judkins still averaged just over 3.0 yards per carry in this contest, but he totaled a season-high 96 yards of offense on 23 touches. After rushing for only 54 yards over the first two weeks, the second-year back has gained 123 yards over the last two.

news.body: Quinshon Judkins rushed the ball 18 times for 70 yards and caught two passes for nine yards in Sunday's 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: Quinshon Judkins underwhelming in win Sunday
news.impact: Week 3 was shaping up to be a perfect situation for Judkins, but he didn't end up performing well and finished with 79 scoreless yards against the Panthers. He isn't worth starting moving forward, especially in less than favorable matchups.

news.body: Quinshon Judkins is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
news.head: Quinshon Judkins (personal) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Judkins landed on the injury report for personal reasons this week. He'll remain an RB2 off volume this week for fantasy managers.

news.body: Quinshon Judkins (personal) was limited at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Quinshon Judkins (personal) limited at practice on Thursday
news.impact: The young running back was a limited participant at practice on Thursday due to a personal issue of some kind. It doesn't seem likely to threaten his availability for Sunday's game, but we won't know more for sure until later on in the week.

news.body: Rachaad White has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Colts.
news.head: Rachaad White (shoulder) ruled out Sunday
news.impact: White was unable to practice all week. Jacory Croskey-Merritt should handle a bigger role in the Commanders backfield.

news.body: Rachaad White did not practice Thursday.
news.head: Rachaad White (shoulder) not practicing Thursday
news.impact: White opens the week missing back-to-back practices. Austin Ekeler could be ready for his debut with Washington after signing with them this week.

news.body: Rachaad White (shoulder) did not take part in Washington's practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Rachaad White (shoulder) doesn't practice Wednesday
news.impact: As expected, White was not able to practice on Wednesday after suffering a shoulder injury last week. It looks likely that he will be sidelined in Week 4, which will open the door for Jacory Croskey-Merritt and rookie Kaytron Allen to see more work against the Colts.

news.body: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Rachaad White is receiving treatment for his shoulder injury.
news.head: Rachaad White receiving treatment for shoulder injury
news.impact: It is unclear if it will impact the status of White heading into Week 4. Jacory Croskey-Merritt could see more work with Austin Ekeler still uncertain to make his Commanders debut.

news.body: Raheim Sanders gained nine yards on two carries and seven yards on two receptions in Thursday's 27-24 win over the Steelers.
news.head: Raheim Sanders does little with four touches Thursday night
news.impact: Sanders now has 10 catches on 11 targets for 73 yards over the first four games of the season, but he's only carried the ball six times for 31 yards. He is the No. 2 RB behind Quinshon Judkins, but he just isn't getting enough volume to merit much fantasy consideration.

news.body: Raheim Sanders rushed the ball one time for 17 yards and caught 4-of-5 targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: Raheim Sanders efficient in win Sunday
news.impact: Sanders continues to be a good contributor for Cleveland's offense. He totaled 51 yards on just five touches on Sunday, and he was particularly involved as a pass catcher. He isn't likely to have much fantasy value himself moving forward, but his involvement will likely continue to hurt Quinshon Judkins for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Raheim Sanders ran for four yards on two carries in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers. He also caught his lone target for seven yards receiving.
news.head: Raheim Sanders sees two carries Sunday
news.impact: Sanders remains off the fantasy radar in his current role behind Quinshon Judkins.

news.body: Raheim Sanders ran five times for 26 yards and caught his only target for seven yards in the Browns' 20-18 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Raheim Sanders gets six touches in win
news.impact: Sanders played second fiddle to Dylan Sampson in this game, having exactly half the touches as Sampson. If the Browns retain him for 2026, he's likely the RB3 and will have little value other than as a handcuff.

news.body: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed for 47 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries in the Patriots win over the Bills. He caught 3-of-5 targets for 27 yards.
news.head: Rhamondre Stevenson sees 16 touches in Week 4 win
news.impact: Stevenson found the end zone on a one-yard plunge in the second-quarter. Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson split time in the backfield, and fantasy managers should expect more of the same against the Raiders in Week 5.

news.body: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed the ball seven times for 22 yards and caught three passes for 16 yards in Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: Rhamondre Stevenson inefficient in loss Sunday
news.impact: Stevenson was ineffective for the Patriots on Sunday. He was only able to contribute 22 yards on the ground, and he wasn't able to do much through the air either in their blowout loss to the Jaguars. He shouldn't be started in most fantasy leagues for the foreseeable future, especially with TreVeyon Henderson seeing more carries than him this week.

news.body: Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson tallied 43 rushing yards on six carries in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers. He caught 1-of-2 targets for three yards.
news.head: Rhamondre Stevenson limited to six carries in Week 2
news.impact: Stevenson saw the majority of the carries go to TreVeyon Henderson after Stevenson fumbled the ball in the first quarter. Stevenson struggled with fumbles in 2025 and that could impact his usage moving forward if he is unable to improve his ball security. Stevenson and the Patriots will take on the Jaguars in Week 3.

news.body: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed the ball 18 times for 51 yards and caught five passes for 44 yards in Wednesday night's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Rhamondre Stevenson totals 95 yards Wednesday
news.impact: Stevenson was New England's workhorse running back on Wednesday night with TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) out of the lineup. He ran at an inefficient clip of 2.8 yards per carry on the night, but his fantasy total was saved by the fact that he caught five passes. He will be more efficient than this in the future but will lose passing work to Henderson when he's back, so he will likely continue to be touchdown dependent on a week-to-week basis.

news.body: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports there is a “pretty good chance” Rico Dowdle returns in Week 5 against the Colts.
news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) has 'pretty good chance' to return in Week 5
news.impact: Dowdle was ruled out for Thursday’s game against the Browns. He'll miss a second straight game with Jaylen Warren continuing to lead the Steelers backfield in his place.

news.body: Rico Dowdle (toe) has been ruled out for Thursday night's game against the Cleveland Browns.
news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) ruled out for Thursday
news.impact: The veteran running back is going to be sidelined for a second-straight game on Thursday night. He's still dealing with a toe injury and was not able to take part in any of Pittsburgh's practice this week. He could miss more time beyond this game, and Jaylen Warren will continue to serve as the team's clear-cut RB1 in Dowdle's absence.

news.body: Rico Dowdle did not practice on Tuesday.
news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) misses practice Tuesday
news.impact: Dowdle is likely to remain sidelined on Thursday against the Browns. Jaylen Warren should remain in the lead role.

news.body: Rico Dowdle is listed as a DNP on Monday's estimated practice report.
news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) listed as 'DNP' on Monday’s estimated practice report
news.impact: Dowdle was sidelined this past week. He is likely to remain sidelined for the Steelers on a short week against the Browns. Jaylen Warren would remain the clear lead back for Pittsburgh.

news.body: J.K. Dobbins rushed 11 times for 40 yards, while RJ Harvey had seven carries for 25 yards in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Harvey also caught 10 passes for 68 yards out of the backfield.
news.head: RJ Harvey, J.K. Dobbins struggle in loss Sunday
news.impact: Denver couldn't get much going on the ground, with Dobbins and Harvey combining for just 65 rushing yards. Dobbins continued to handle more of the rushing work, but Harvey was much more involved as a receiver and ended up leading the Broncos in both receptions and receiving yards. The backfield remains a split, with Dobbins having the better chance at early-down work and Harvey carrying more upside in the passing game.

news.body: RJ Harvey is off the injury report on Wednesday.
news.head: RJ Harvey (concussion) off injury report
news.impact: Harvey was checked for a concussion in Week. He will be good to go in his complimentary role next to J.K. Dobbins.

news.body: RJ Harvey hauled in 6-of-7 targets for 41 yards and rushed the ball two times for six yards in Sunday night's 30-26 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: RJ Harvey hauls in six passes Sunday
news.impact: The young running back was able to make his return to the lineup on Sunday night after missing last week's game due to a hamstring issue. He looked okay in his first game back, seeing a lot of involvement as a receiver but very little work as a rusher against the Rams. His role will continue to be limited for the team moving forward, though he might have to step up and play a bigger role than usual with Jonah Coleman (ankle) set to miss several weeks at least.

news.body: RJ Harvey (hamstring) will play in Sunday night's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: RJ Harvey (hamstring) will play Sunday
news.impact: Harvey is set to make his return to the field in Week 3 after being sidelined for one game due to a hamstring issue. He should see a full workload against the Rams this week, especially with rookie Jonah Coleman (ankle) set to be sidelined in that matchup.

news.body: Samaje Perine rushed the ball three times for seven yards in Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: Samaje Perine uninvolved in loss Sunday
news.impact: The veteran didn't do much on Sunday, finishing with just seven yards in the team's loss to the Jaguars. He is clearly the team's backup at this point and doesn't project to be an effective fantasy asset for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Samaje Perine tallied nine rushing yards on three carries in a 30-27 loss to the Steelers. He caught 1-of-3 targets for five yards.
news.head: Samaje Perine sees four touches in Week 3
news.impact: Perine continues to serve as the primary backup behind Chase Brown, but has not logged enough volume to be on the fantasy radar. Fantasy managers can leave him on the wire ahead of a matchup with Jacksonville in Week 4.

news.body: Samaje Perine ran for six yards on two carries in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also caught his lone target for 16 yards receiving.
news.head: Samaje Perine sees three touches Sunday
news.impact: Perine remains a pure stash behind Chase Brown.

news.body: Samaje Perine (illness) was on the sideline at the start of Friday's practice session.
news.head: Samaje Perine (illness) on the sidelines Friday
news.impact: Perine has missed Thursday's practice as well due to an illness. The veteran back was a significant part of the Bengals' offense in Week 1, rushing for 20 yards on five carries and grabbing three passes for 30 yards. Perine still has a couple of days to get ready for Sunday's matchup with the Texans.

news.body: Saquon Barkley is considered week-to-week with his hamstring injury.
news.head: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) considered week-to-week
news.impact: It is not believed to be a serious injury, but Barkley will likely be sidelined in Week 5 against the Jaguars.

news.body: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said he’ll “have more answers Wednesday” on Saquon Barkley’s hamstring injury.
news.head: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) without update on injury
news.impact: Barkley went down early in Sunday’s game against the Rams. His status is up in the air heading into Week 5 against the Jaguars.

news.body: Saquon Barkley rushed the ball two times for eight yards and caught one pass for two yards before leaving Sunday's loss to the Rams with a hamstring injury.
news.head: Saquon Barkley suffers hamstring injury Sunday
news.impact: Barkley suffered a hamstring injury during Sunday's loss to the Rams. The severity of the injury is unknown at this point, so fantasy managers should keep close tabs on updates about his status throughout the week. Tank Bigsby will be primed for more work if the veteran has to miss any time.

news.body: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of the Week 4 contest between the Philadelphia Eagles and Los Angeles Rams according to Ian Rapoport.
news.head: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) ruled out Sunday
news.impact: Barkley will remain sidelined after suffering the hamstring injury in the first half Sunday, carrying the ball twice for eight yards and catching his lone target for two yards prior to exiting. Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley take over backfield duties for head coach Nick Sirianni.

news.body: Sione Vaki rushed the ball one time for seven yards and caught one pass for 13 yards in Thursday's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Sione Vaki uninvolved in loss Thursday
news.impact: Vaki continues to make minimal impact on Detroit's offense. He has squarely established himself as the RB2 behind Jahmyr Gibbs, but that role hasn't furnished him with many opportunities over the first two weeks of the season. He remains nothing more than a mid-tier handcuff option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Sione Vaki caught his only target for 11 yards while also rushing twice for seven yards in the Lions' 31-30 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1.
news.head: Sione Vaki sees three touches in Week 1
news.impact: Vaki was an afterthought out of the backfield, being out-carried by Jahmyr Gibbs 29-2 in the win. The running back remains little more than an underwhelming handcuff to Gibbs ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Buffalo Bills.

news.body: Sione Vaki (thumb) remained limited for another practice session on Wednesday.
news.head: Sione Vaki (thumb) remains limited Wednesday
news.impact: Vaki has been dealing with this thumb injury for a while already and will remain limited for another practice on Wednesday as a result. He remains off of the fantasy radar at this point in the season, however, so fantasy managers shouldn't read much into his availability for Sunday's game.

news.body: Sione Vaki (thumb) was limited at practice again on Wednesday.
news.head: Sione Vaki (thumb) limited again Wednesday
news.impact: Vaki has been managing this thumb injury for a little while and was limited at another practice on Wednesday because of it. It remains to be seen whether or not it will leave him with an injury designation for Week 15, but either way fantasy managers shouldn't put much weight into his status.

news.body: The Eagles placed RB Tank Bigsby on injured reserve.
news.head: Tank Bigsby (core) lands on IR
news.impact: Bigsby will miss at least the next four games for the Eagles.

news.body: Eagles RB Tank Bigsby suffered an injury on Sunday and will be placed on injured reserve.
news.head: Tank Bigsby (core) to be placed on IR
news.impact: Bigsby now requires core muscle surgery to repair his injury. He is expected to miss at least 5-to-6 weeks.

news.body: Tank Bigsby rushed the ball 14 times for 55 yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Tank Bigsby leads team in rushing Sunday
news.impact: Bigsby stepped up on Sunday and took over as the team's top running back when Saquon Barkley left the game with a hamstring injury. He did okay in the absence of the veteran, though he left something to be desired with his efficiency and involvement in the passing game. He could be a big-time waiver pickup this week if the Eagles don't get good news regarding the severity of Barkley's injury.

news.body: Tank Bigsby caught his lone target for a five-yard gain in a 27-7 loss to the Bears in Week 3.
news.head: Tank Bigsby loses fumble in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Bigsby did not record any carries and lost a fumble on his lone catch of the contest. The veteran running back will look to bounce back in Week 4 against the Rams. He remains a solid fantasy handcuff moving forward.

news.body: Tony Pollard rushed for 48 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Titans' loss to the Ravens. Pollard caught 2-of-4 targets for two yards.
news.head: Tony Pollard finds the end zone in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Pollard entered the game as the favorite to see the bulk of the carries for the Titans, with Tyjae Spears receiving just two carries. Pollard continues to see plenty of carries, but has not been able to do much yardage wise this season. Pollard and the Titans will take on the Texans in Week 5.

news.body: Tony Pollard (foot) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens.
news.head: Tony Pollard (foot) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: Pollard is going to be good to go for Sunday's game, despite being on the injury report all week due to a foot issue. He will see the vast majority of touches in this backfield if Tyjae Spears (ankle) is sidelined for this matchup.

news.body: Tony Pollard (foot) practiced in a full capacity on Thursday.
news.head: Tony Pollard (foot) practices in full Thursday
news.impact: Pollard was able to log a full practice session on Thursday after being absent on Wednesday as part of the team's injury management for his foot. He should be good to go for Week 4 and will be primed for a large workload if Tyjae Spears (ankle) is limited or sidelined against the Ravens on Sunday.

news.body: Tony Pollard (foot) was officially a non-participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Tony Pollard (foot) officially a non-participant Wednesday
news.impact: We knew earlier in the day that Pollard wasn't going to practice, but it turns out that he is listed with a foot injury rather than an ankle issue. Fantasy managers should continue to monitor his status throughout the week, especially with Tyjae Spears (ankle) also not practicing for the Titans.

news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) has been placed on injured reserve and will be out for at least four weeks.
news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) placed on injured reserve
news.impact: The Saints have decided to place Etienne on injured reserve, which means that he is going to be sidelined for at least the next four weeks. He may be out longer than that as well, but the team has yet to place a concrete timetable on his recovery. Look for Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller to both shoulder a much bigger workload in this backfield for the foreseeable future as a result of his absence.

news.body: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Travis Etienne Jr. “will miss time."
news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) to miss extended time
news.impact: Etienne does not hold a clear timetable to return. Alvin Kamara should take on a bigger role in the Saints backfield with Kendre Miller also taking on a bigger role behind him.

news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. exited Sunday’s contest between the New Orleans Saints against the Las Vegas Raiders according to Ross Jackson.
news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. exits early Sunday
news.impact: Etienne Jr. headed to the locker room for further evaluation, rushing 13 times for 57 yards while also hauling in both of his targets for 13 yards prior to exiting. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller will take over backfield duties in the running back’s absence.

news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. has been cleared for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: Etienne has been dealing with a hamstring injury this week. He'll be a risky RB2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: TreVeyon Henderson rushed for 42 yards on 14 carries in the Patriots win over the Bills. He did not record a reception on his two targets.
news.head: TreVeyon Henderson sees 14 touches in Week 4 win
news.impact: Henderson saw just one more carry that Rhamondre Stevenson, but failed to do much on his 14 touches. Fantasy managers should expect Stevenson and Henderson to continue to split time in the backfield in Week 5 against Las Vegas.

news.body: TreVeyon Henderson rushed the ball eight times for 23 yards and caught one pass for six yards in Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: TreVeyon Henderson totals 29 yards in loss Sunday
news.impact: New England's offense wasn't able to get anything going on Sunday, and Henderson was no exception to that. He totaled just 29 yards on nine opportunities against the Jaguars, which burned any fantasy managers who started him in this matchup. He should not be started in most leagues until New England figures out their offensive issues.

news.body: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson tallied 76 rushing yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
news.head: TreVeyon Henderson finds the end zone in season debut
news.impact: Henderson missed Week 1 with an ankle injury, but made an immediate impact with a 39-yard touchdown early in the win over Pittsburgh. Rhamondre Stevenson lost a fumble and saw the bulk of the work go to Henderson after the turnover. Fantasy managers should expect both Stevenson and Henderson to have roles against the Jaguars in Week 3.

news.body: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is off of the injury report and officially good to go for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) officially good to go for Sunday
news.impact: New England's offense is set to get a much-needed boost this week with their young running back off of the injury report and set to make his season debut on Sunday. Henderson projects to be something of a 'boom-or-bust' fantasy option on a week-to-week basis while he continues to split work with Rhamondre Stevenson in the Patriots' backfield.

news.body: Ty Johnson rushed for three yards on one carry in the loss to the Patriots. He caught both of his targets for nine yards.
news.head: Ty Johnson sees three touches in Week 4
news.impact: Johnson continues to operate as the change of pace back, but has limited fantasy value right now. Fantasy managers can leave Johnson on the waiver wire heading into a matchup with the Rams.

news.body: Ty Johnson hauled in each of his four targets for 50 yards in the Bills' 24-16 Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Ty Johnson hauls in four passes in Week 3 win
news.impact: Johnson found a way to make an impact in his first game action of the season, finishing second on the team in receiving yards in the win. The running back remains an impactful pass-catching option out of the backfield when healthy, with a Week 4 contest against the New England Patriots up next.

news.body: Ty Johnson (hamstring) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
news.head: Ty Johnson (hamstring) practices in full Wednesday
news.impact: The veteran running back seems very close to a return to the field, as he was able to practice in full on Wednesday after being sidelined for last week's game. He is trending towards playing in Week 3, but his potential return would be unlikely to have a substantial impact on Buffalo's backfield moving forward.

news.body: Ty Johnson (hamstring) is inactive for the Bills game against the Lions on Thursday.
news.head: Ty Johnson (hamstring) inactive for Thursday against Lions
news.impact: Johnson missed the Bills Week 1 contest against Houston, and is inactive yet again. He will rest up and hope to be available for Week 3. In his absence, Ray Davis will handle primary RB2 duties.

news.body: Tyjae Spears rushed for seven yards on two carries in the Titans loss to the Ravens. He caught his lone target for a loss of a yard.
news.head: Tyjae Spears sees three touches in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Spears continues to mange an ankle injury, but continues to see limited rushing attempts by Tony Pollard. With just 15 rushing attempts this season, he is a handcuff at best heading into Week 5.

news.body: Titans RB Tyjae Spears (ankle) is officially active for a Week 4 matchup with the Ravens.
news.head: Tyjae Spears (ankle) officially active for Week 4
news.impact: Spears was listed as questionable to play Sunday, but his full practice Friday was encouraging. He will work with Tony Pollard out of the Titans' backfield in a tough matchup against Baltimore.

news.body: Tyjae Spears (ankle) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens.
news.head: Tyjae Spears (ankle) questionable to play Sunday
news.impact: Spears is uncertain to play on Sunday. He's still managing an ankle injury, so the team officially has him listed as questionable to play right now. Tony Pollard will be the team's clear-cut RB1 if Spears if ruled out ahead of game time against the Ravens.

news.body: Tyjae Spears (ankle) returned to practice in a limited fashion on Thursday.
news.head: Tyjae Spears (ankle) returns to practice in limited fashion Thursday
news.impact: Spears was able to return to practice in a limited fashion on Thursday after being absent on Wednesday due to an ankle issue. He seems likely to play in Week 4, although it remains to be seen whether or not he will be limited in any capacity.

news.body: Tyler Allgeier rushed the ball eight times for 42 yards and a touchdown while catching two passes for seven yards through the air in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Tyler Allgeier finds end zone Sunday
news.impact: The veteran was able to contribute on Sunday, finishing with 49 total yards and a touchdown in the team's loss to the Giants. It seems like rookie Jeremiyah Love is dealing with some bumps and bruises right now too, so Allgeier could see more work in the future if the rookie is limited by that at all.

news.body: Tyler Allgeier ran for -1 yard on two carries in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday. He also caught 4-of-4 targets for 10 yards receiving.
news.head: Tyler Allgeier has quiet day Sunday
news.impact: Allgeier took a step back to rookie RB Jeremiyah Love for the first time this season on the day. If this trend continues, he'll remain a pure stash for fantasy managers.

news.body: Tyler Allgeier ran five times for 10 yards and caught both of his targets for 9 yards in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
news.head: Tyler Allgeier gets seven touches in loss
news.impact: Allgeier played second fiddle to Jeremiyah Love on Sunday, which is to be expected. He wasn't particularly efficient on his limited work, but no one in the offense really got going anyway. It was tough sledding for the veteran, but hopefully things will get a little easier against San Fransisco next Sunday.

news.body: Tyler Allgeier gained 61 yards on 17 carries and nine yards on two receptions in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Tyler Allgeier leads Arizona rushing attack in Week 1
news.impact: Allgeier shouldered the majority of the backfield load for the Cardinals on Sunday, getting six more carries than Jeremiyah Love. Allgeier was not especially impressive, averaging just 3.6 yards per carry with a long of 11.
