news.head: Carnell Tate leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: The rookie was arguably the lone bright spot for the Titans on Sunday. He led the team with 58 receiving yards on the afternoon and flashed some real talent in the process. He's a good player but isn't likely to be a consistent fantasy producer on this offense, which is among the NFL's worst.

news.body: Carnell Tate caught three of his five targets for 27 yards in a 24-20 loss to the Eagles in Week 2.
news.head: Carnell Tate catches three passes in Week 2
news.impact: Tate finished fourth on the team in receiving yards in the close loss to Philly. The rookie has caught seven of his 11 targets for 65 scoreless yards through the first two games of the season. Tennessee will now get ready to take on the Giants in Week 3. Tate will be tough to start in fantasy until Tennessee's passing attack starts to show more life.

news.body: Carnell Tate caught four of his six targets for 38 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.head: Carnell Tate catches four passes in Week 1
news.impact: Tate tied for the team lead in targets and receiving yards while finishing second in receptions in his NFL debut. The rookie receiver will surely have bigger games going forward, as the entire Tennessee offense struggled in the season opener. Tate will be a low-end WR3 heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

news.body: CeeDee Lamb was a full participant in practice on Tuesday.
news.head: CeeDee Lamb (thigh) practices in full Tuesday
news.impact: Lamb remains a locked and loaded WR1 for Thursday’s game against the Buccaneers.

news.body: CeeDee Lamb was listed as a full participant on Monday's estimated practice report.
news.head: CeeDee Lamb (thigh) logs full practice Monday
news.impact: Lamb will remain a locked and loaded WR1 for Thursday’s game against the Buccaneers.

news.body: CeeDee Lamb caught 17-of-21 targets for 189 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys 34-30 win over the Texans.
news.head: CeeDee Lamb hauls in 17 passes Sunday
news.impact: Lamb had the go-ahead touchdown with less than 30 seconds left in the game. It was a career day for him getting targeted all throughout the second half. He remains a locked and loaded WR1.

news.body: CeeDee Lamb caught seven of his eight targets for 112 yards and caught a two-point conversion in a 34-31 loss to the Ravens in Brazil in Week 3.
news.head: CeeDee Lamb goes for 112 yards in Week 3
news.impact: Lamb led the Cowboys in receiving yards in the close loss to Baltimore. The veteran wideout has topped 100 receiving yards in two of his three games this season, compiling 20 catches for 309 yards and three touchdowns overall. He will be a locked-in WR1 in fantasy in Week 4 despite a matchup against a tough Texans defense.

news.body: Chris Bell did not bring in any of his three targets in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Chris Bell catchless in loss Sunday
news.impact: The rookie had one big touchdown that got called back due to penalty, and outside of that, he wasn't able to do anything at all. He didn't catch any of his three targets and ended up with a goose egg for fantasy purposes. He should not be started moving forward, even if he has enough talent to break out at some point in the season.

news.body: Chris Bell (knee) will play in Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Chris Bell (knee) will play Sunday
news.impact: The rookie is going to be available to play on Sunday, despite being listed on Miami's injury report due to a knee issue of some kind. He will be primed for a lot of work with Caleb Douglas (ankle) already ruled out ahead of Week 4's matchup against the Vikings.

news.body: Chris Bell (knee) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: Chris Bell (knee) limited again Thursday
news.impact: The rookie was limited for a second-straight practice on Thursday as the team continues to limit his workload at practice. He should be available to play this week, however, and will be primed for more work than usual with Caleb Douglas (ankle) trending towards missing another game.

news.body: Chris Bell (knee) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Chris Bell (knee) listed as limited Wednesday
news.impact: The rookie was limited to start the practice week on Wednesday due to a knee issue. It seems unlikely to affect his availability for Week 4, however, and he seems primed to see more work against the Vikings with Caleb Douglas (ankle) trending towards missing another game for Miami.

news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught six of his seven targets for 31 yards in a 17-14 loss to the Packers in Week 4.
news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. hauls in six catches in Week 4
news.impact: Godwin led the Bucs in targets and catches but managed just 5.2 yards per catch in rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels' debut. The veteran wideout has 16 catches for 142 scoreless yards through four games this year. He will be a low-end flex option in Week 5 against Dallas.

news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. (ankle) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers.
news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. (ankle) off injury report for Sunday
news.impact: Godwin will be available to play on Sunday after logging a full practice on both Thursday and Friday. He shouldn't have any limitations but still doesn't project to be a good fantasy option against the Packers, especially with rookie Jalon Daniels starting at quarterback for the Buccaneers.

news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. (ankle) logged a full practice session on Thursday.
news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. (ankle) logs full practice Thursday
news.impact: The veteran was back at practice and participated in a full capacity on Thursday, meaning that he will almost certainly be a full go in Week 4. His absence on Wednesday was likely a load management move on the part of the team.

news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. returned to practice on Thursday.
news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. (ankle) returns to practice Thursday
news.impact: Godwin missed practice to open the week on Wednesday. He will be playing with UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels as his quarterback.

news.body: Chris Olave caught 8-of-12 targets for 116 yards in Monday night's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Chris Olave leads team in receiving Monday
news.impact: Olave was a bright spot for the Saints on Monday, leading the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in their loss to the Falcons. It briefly looked like he suffered a lower-body injury at the end of the game, but it sounds like he will be just fine, although it would still be smart for fantasy managers to monitor his status at practice throughout the week.

news.body: Chris Olave caught 9-of-13 targets for 107 yards in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday.
news.head: Chris Olave records 107 yards Sunday
news.impact: Olave continues to lead the Saints in receiving on a week in and week out basis. He is a WR1 moving forward for fantasy managers with his involvement to start the season.

news.body: Chris Olave caught 8-of-10 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the Saints 24-17 win over the Ravens.
news.head: Chris Olave finds the end zone in Week 2 win
news.impact: Olave was considered questionable to play due to a hamstring injury, but that did not appear to impact him at all against the Ravens. Olave caught a 21-yard touchdown pass in the fourth quarter to tie the game and help pace the Saints to the upset win. Olave will look to continue his strong start to the season in Week 3 against Las Vegas.

news.body: Saints WR Chris Olave (hamstring) is officially active for a Week 2 matchup with the Ravens.
news.head: Chris Olave (hamstring) officially active for Week 2
news.impact: Olave was a late addition to the injury report this week and was listed as questionable to play in Week 2. He immediately becomes the top pass catching option for QB Tyler Shough and the Saints.

news.body: Christian Watson caught all three of his targets for 47 yards in a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers in Week 4.
news.head: Christian Watson goes for 47 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Watson turned in his quietest game of the season but he still wound up leading the Packers in receiving yards. It was the first game all season where Watson failed to find the end zone, snapping a three-game scoring streak. Overall, Watson has 20 catches for 331 yards and four touchdowns through four games. He will be a WR1 in fantasy heading into Week 5 against the Bears.

news.body: Christian Watson carries no injury designation and will be good to go for Week 4's matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
news.head: Christian Watson good to go for Week 4
news.impact: There was some public concern when Watson seemed to favor one of his legs towards the end of last Thursday's game, but he is not listed on Green Bay's injury report for Week 4 and should be a full go against the Buccaneers. He remains a must-start fantasy option as often as he is healthy and on the field moving forward.

news.body: Christian Watson caught 7 of 10 targets for 96 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
news.head: Christian Watson extends touchdown streak to three games
news.impact: It might not have been in a win, but fantasy managers won't care. Watson has been a clear favorite target for Jordan Love, especially down in the red zone, with Tucker Kraft still working his way back to full health. He should be in your lineup whenever he is playing.

news.body: Christian Watson hauled in four of his team-high 11 targets for 41 yards and one touchdown in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: Christian Watson finds end zone in Week 2 win over Jets
news.impact: Watson has been impactful as part of an inconsistent Green Bay offense to begin the season, catching one or more touchdowns on eight or more targets in each of the first two games. The wideout offers fantasy managers one of the few stable options in an underperforming Packer offense ahead of a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.body: The Raiders signed WR Cody White to their active roster.
news.head: Cody White signs with Raiders' active roster
news.impact: White has scored three touchdowns in the past two weeks. He gets the opportunity with Jack Bech (forearm) placed on IR.

news.body: Cody White caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards and a touchdown in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
news.head: Cody White catches touchdown Sunday
news.impact: White now has three touchdowns in the past two weeks coming off the practice squad. Still be remains off the fantasy radar.

news.body: Cody White reverted back to the Raiders practice squad.
news.head: Cody White reverts back to Raiders practice squad
news.impact: White caught two touchdowns last week. He could be elevated again soon.

news.body: Cody White caught two passes for 24 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Cody White hauls in two touchdowns Sunday
news.impact: The Raiders were able to score a lot of points on offense on Sunday. White made a couple big plays for them on that front, catching two touchdowns in the team's win over the Chargers. This was a pretty good game for him but he isn't expected to be a fantasy relevant wideout for a while.

news.body: Cooper Kupp caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Seahawks 30-23 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Cooper Kupp quiet Sunday
news.impact: Kupp remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Cooper Kupp caught four of his five targets for 46 yards and one touchdown in the Seahawks' 33-31 Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Cooper Kupp finds end zone in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Kupp took advantage of increased involvement in the Seattle passing attack, recording more than two receptions for the first time in three contests Sunday. The wideout remains difficult to trust in all formats ahead of a Week 4 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers.

news.body: Cooper Kupp (back) is available to play in Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Cooper Kupp (back) available to play Sunday
news.impact: Kupp is going to play on Sunday. He was dealing with a back injury earlier in the week, but it's nothing serious at this point and won't affect his availability against the Commanders. He isn't expected to be a good fantasy option in this matchup, however, even with Sam Darnold (glute) set to make his return for the Seahawks.

news.body: Cooper Kupp was a full participant in practice on Thursday.
news.head: Cooper Kupp (back) practices fully Thursday
news.impact: Kupp was upgraded after he was limited to start the week on Wednesday. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Courtland Sutton caught one of his six targets for four yards in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
news.head: Courtland Sutton held to four yards Sunday
news.impact: Sutton had a rough day despite tying for the team lead among wide receivers with six targets. He and Bo Nix couldn't connect on several opportunities, leaving Sutton with just one catch. The volume remains encouraging, and fantasy managers shouldn't overreact to one bad game, but Sutton will need to bounce back first after his quiet Week 4 before entering starting lineups.

news.body: Courtland Sutton caught 3-of-7 targets for 46 yards in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Courtland Sutton leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: Sutton was only able to haul in three out of his seven targets on Sunday night, but that was enough for him to rack up a team-high 46 yards on the night. Still, he hasn't been a good fantasy option so far this season and doesn't project to get much better anytime soon.

news.body: Courtland Sutton caught three of his four targets for 25 yards in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
news.head: Courtland Sutton held to 25 yards in Week 2
news.impact: Sutton posted a pedestrian stat line in the Broncos' exciting comeback win. It is becoming a concern after he caught just two passes for 11 yards back in Week 1. The Broncos don't seem to be prioritizing getting him the ball as they have in past years, leaving Sutton as a risky flex option in Week 3 against the Rams.

news.body: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-5 targets for just 11 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Courtland Sutton uninvolved in loss Monday
news.impact: Denver's offense as a whole struggled heavily on Monday night, and Sutton was no exception to that. He caught just two of his five targets over the course of the game and was only able to turn that into a measly 11 yards. He remains off of the fantasy radar for the foreseeable future, even in more favorable matchups.

news.body: Darius Cooper hauled in 3-of-7 targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Darius Cooper hauls in two touchdowns in loss Sunday
news.impact: Cooper was one of the lone bright spots on Philadelphia's offense on Sunday. He caught both of the team's passing touchdowns against the Rams, although he was only able to rack up 33 yards in the process. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be a good fantasy option moving forward, however, especially with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) set to make his return to the lineup at some point.

news.body: Darius Cooper caught three of his five targets for 33 yards in a 24-17 loss to the Commanders in Week 18.
news.head: Darius Cooper hauls in three balls in Week 18
news.impact: Cooper turned in season-highs across the board with the Eagles resting several key starters on offense, including A.J. Brown. He will go back to a depth role next week in a Wild Card matchup against the 49ers.

news.body: The Eagles activated WR Darius Cooper from injured reserve.
news.head: Darius Cooper (shoulder) activated from IR
news.impact: Cooper had been designated to return earlier this week. He will be active on Sunday.

news.body: The Eagles opened the practice window of wide receiver Darius Cooper.
news.head: Darius Cooper (shoulder) has practice window opened
news.impact: Cooper will have 21 days to officially be activated from IR.

news.body: Darnell Mooney failed to haul in either of his two targets in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Darnell Mooney catchless in win Sunday
news.impact: The veteran wideout wasn't able to get in on the action on Sunday, despite New York's offense actually finding success against Arizona's defense. He shouldn't be expected to produce much moving forward, especially from a fantasy perspective.

news.body: Darnell Mooney caught 2-of-3 targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Darnell Mooney ineffective in win Sunday
news.impact: New York's offense failed to score even a single touchdown on Sunday, so it's no surprise that Mooney individually didn't have a good showing either. He caught just two passes for 20 yards, and fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to return to relevance for however long QB Jameis Winston is starting for the Giants.

news.body: Darnell Mooney hauled in 2-of-3 targets for 48 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Darnell Mooney leads team in receiving Monday
news.impact: The veteran was technically the team's leader in receiving yards on Monday night, but he did it with just 48 over the course of the game, which still left him with a poor fantasy total. He shouldn't be rostered in most league formats for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Darnell Mooney caught two passes for 27 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.head: Darnell Mooney quiet in win Sunday
news.impact: The veteran wideout had a quiet game in a win over the Cowboys. He contributed just 27 yards on two catches, which obviously didn't amount to much from a fantasy perspective. He isn't expected to be relevant moving forward, especially with rookie Malachi Fields there to compete for the WR2 spot behind Malik Nabers.

news.body: Davante Adams hauled in 4-of-9 targets for just 32 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Davante Adams disappoints in win Sunday
news.impact: Adams was red-hot coming into this game, but he disappointed against the Eagles by catching just four of his nine targets for a measly 32 yards. He is no longer the top wideout on the team with Puka Nacua back in the lineup and healthy, so he will likely revert to being a boom-or-bust fantasy option on a week-to-week basis moving forward.

news.body: Davante Adams hauled in 7-of-13 targets for 137 yards in Sunday night's 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Davante Adams racks up 137 yards Sunday
news.impact: Adams once again looked great with Puka Nacua (hip) out of the lineup for the Rams. He led the team with 137 yards on the night, although this time he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all. Fantasy managers should continue to regard him as a WR1 for however long Nacua remains out of the lineup.

news.body: Davante Adams hauled in 8-of-10 targets for 195 yards and two touchdowns in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.head: Davante Adams dominant in win Monday
news.impact: Adams had one of his best games as a Ram on Monday night. He put up nearly 200 receiving yards in this blowout win over the Giants, and he was also able to get into the end zone on two separate occasions. He really stepped up in the absence of Puka Nacua (hip), so if he misses more time, fantasy managers should continue to view Adams as a can't-miss option any given week that he's the team's undisputed WR1.

news.body: Davante Adams caught just three of six targets for 26 yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers on Thursday.
news.head: Davante Adams quiet in loss to 49ers
news.impact: Adams could just not get much going against the Niners. On the bright side, his six targets were second on the team, so he's still earning opportunities. It just wasn't his day, as was the story for most of the team. He will try to improve next time out.

news.body: Deebo Samuel caught five of his six targets for 26 yards and a touchdown, adding 44 yards on three carries in Sunday's 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Deebo Samuel scores touchdown in win Sunday
news.impact: Samuel didn't do much with his receptions, but his usage on the ground gave him a productive fantasy day. He averaged 14.7 yards on his three carries and scored San Francisco's first touchdown on a one-yard reception. Samuel's ability to produce as both a receiver and runner keeps his weekly upside high as a flex option.

news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. recorded an 80-yard touchdown on a lateral in the 49ers 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. scores long touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Samuel took a lateral from Mike Evans to the house for an 80-yard touchdown in the opening drive. He could see more involvement next week if Mike Evans (rib) misses time.

news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 31 yards, adding four yards on one carry in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. finished with three receptions in Week 2
news.impact: Samuel fell well short of the 60 total yards and a touchdown he contributed in Week 1, but he was still significantly involved in Week 2. That should remain the case as long as the veteran playmaker is healthy. Samuel has secured 9-of-11 targets for 79 yards through two games. He's also carried the ball once in each contest, gaining 16 yards.

news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday. He also carried the ball once for 12 yards.
news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. snags touchdown in win
news.impact: Samuel looks to have come back to his old role on the 49ers, lining up everywhere and getting the ball put in his hands to make plays. He even had over 70 kick return yards. Samuel just might be a draft-day steal if they are going to use him like this throughout the season.

news.body: DeMario Douglas caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Patriots win over the Bills.
news.head: DeMario Douglas held to two receptions in Week 4
news.impact: Douglas continues to see limited targets in the Patriots' offense. Fantasy managers should feel comfortable leaving him on the waiver wire heading into Week 5.

news.body: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-5 targets for 38 yards in Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: DeMario Douglas catches one pass in loss Sunday
news.impact: Douglas had a tough time connecting with QB Drake Maye on Sunday, catching just one of his five targets for a 38-yard gain. He will continue to see a solid amount of targets on a week-to-week basis moving forward but carries very little fantasy upside for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Patriots WR DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
news.head: DeMario Douglas held to one reception in Week 2
news.impact: Douglas saw his target number drop significantly from Week 1, which is a major concern considering A.J. Brown is injured. Douglas is streaming option at best considering the Patriots' passing attack has struggled to open the season.

news.body: DeMario Douglas caught 5-of-7 targets for 20 yards in Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: DeMario Douglas catches five passes Wednesday
news.impact: Douglas was the most targeted receiver for New England last night, but he wasn't able to turn that into any fantasy success. He ended with just 20 yards on five catches, but he may continue to see high opportunities for the foreseeable future with A.J. Brown (ankle) set to miss some time for the team.

news.body: Denzel Boston hauled in 4-of-7 targets for 89 yards in Thursday's 27-24 win over the Steelers.
news.head: Denzel Boston leads Browns with 89 receiving yards
news.impact: Boston rebounded from just a so-so output in Week 3, leading the Browns in receiving yards Thursday night for the third time in four games. The rookie has quickly acclimated to the NFL, totaling 13 catches for an average of 71 yards per game and two touchdowns to this point.

news.body: Denzel Boston caught 2-of-4 targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: Denzel Boston racks up 41 yards Sunday
news.impact: The rookie had an underwhelming performance against the Panthers, as he was only able to finish with two catches for 41 yards over the course of the afternoon. He has flashed potential but will likely continue to struggle with consistency over the course of the season.

news.body: Denzel Boston caught 5-of-7 targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers.
news.head: Denzel Boston snags another touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Boston connected with Deshaun Watson on a touchdown for the second straight week. He is seemingly emerging as the clear WR1 on the Browns offense. He'll hold some upside WR3 appeal next week for fantasy managers against the Panthers.

news.body: Denzel Boston caught two of four targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
news.head: Denzel Boston snags bomb touchdown in loss
news.impact: Boston had the Browns' only touchdown, though sadly it was in garbage time. His four targets tied with Jerry Jeudy for second on the team, an encouraging sign for his future usage as he gets further acclimated to the NFL game.

news.body: Devaughn Vele caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Devaughn Vele finds end zone Monday
news.impact: Vele's strong start to the season continued on Monday night. He caught six passes for 54 yards over the course of the game, one of which he was able to take to the house for a touchdown. He will continue to have solid week-to-week upside until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is back in the lineup for the Saints.

news.body: Devaughn Vele caught 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards in the Saints 35-27 loss against the Raiders on Sunday.
news.head: Devaughn Vele catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Vele was relatively quiet for most of the afternoon. It was Chris Olave and the tight ends who dominated on the day for New Orleans. He remains an upside flex play heading into next week against the Falcons.

news.body: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-7 targets for 64 yards in the Saints 24-17 win over the Ravens.
news.head: Devaughn Vele hauls in five passes in Week 2 win
news.impact: Vele has put together two solid games to open the season, tallying 12 receptions on 16 targets. Vele is the clear WR2 in the Saints' offense and should be poised for another strong performance against the Raiders in Week 3.

news.body: Devaughn Vele hauled in seven of his nine targets for 69 yards and one touchdown in the Saints' 31-30 Week 1 loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Devaughn Vele finds end zone in Week 1 loss to Lions
news.impact: Vele capitalized on a sizeable role in the New Orleans passing attack, finishing second in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in a losing effort. The wideout looks poised to offer head coach Kellen Moore another impactful pass-catching option in the New Orleans offense moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens up next.

news.body: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) ruled out for Sunday
news.impact: The Eagles will be without their top wide receiver on Sunday. Smith is still dealing with a hamstring injury, and the team wants to take a cautious approach with his recovery at this point in the season. His absence will hurt the fantasy value of QB Jalen Hurts in Week 4, but it could offer a breakout opportunity for Dontayvion Wicks or rookie Makai Lemon in a tough matchup against the Rams.

news.body: DeVonta Smith remained absent from practice on Friday.
news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) not practicing Friday
news.impact: Smith will likely be ruled out when the official injury report is released later in the afternoon. Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon will figure to step into bigger roles in his place.

news.body: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is not expected to play in Sunday's matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) not expected to play Week 4
news.impact: There isn't much optimism surrounding Smith's status for Week 4 because of the hamstring injury that he's dealing with, and now it is being reported that he is expected to be sidelined against the Rams. That will leave the Eagles' offense without their main pass catcher in a tough matchup in Week 4, so their offense won't have a good outlook for that game. Fantasy managers should find someone else to start in place of the injured veteran.

news.body: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is not at Philadelphia's practice on Thursday.
news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) not at practice Thursday
news.impact: The veteran wideout is still dealing with a hamstring injury and is absent for a second-straight practice on Thursday as a result. He will need to practice in some capacity on Friday if he wants a realistic chance to play in Week 4, so this is a situation that fantasy managers should keep close tabs on over the next couple of days.

news.body: The Bills have downgraded WR DJ Moore (shoulder) to doubtful to return against New England.
news.head: DJ Moore (shoulder) doubtful to return
news.impact: Moore was injured in the second quarter and appears unlikely to return. Moore has been dealing with a shoulder injury over the last few weeks. He will end the day with one reception for 11 yards if he does not return.

news.body: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable to return against New England.
news.head: DJ Moore (shoulder) questionable to return
news.impact: Moore was limited in practice throughout the week with a shoulder injury, but was cleared to play. It’s not immediately clear if this is just a flare up of the original injury, but the Bills should provide an update on his status after halftime.

news.body: DJ Moore is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
news.head: DJ Moore (shoulder) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Moore is officially good to go. He'll be a WR2 for fantasy managers against a Patriots defense without Christian Gonzalez.

news.body: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: DJ Moore (shoulder) limited again Thursday
news.impact: The veteran wideout was limited for a second-straight practice on Thursday as he continues to recover from a shoulder injury of some kind. He is likely to play through it this week, however, and remains a high-upside fantasy option on a week-to-week basis moving forward.

news.body: DK Metcalf caught 5-of-9 targets for 115 yards in Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
news.head: DK Metcalf cranks it up in Week 4
news.impact: Metcalf had topped out at four receptions and 40 yards over the first three weeks of the season. He finally got it going on Thursday night. The big, physical receiver leads the Steelers with 16 catches and 213 yards through four games. He's found the end zone just once, but more should be on the way soon enough. Metcalf remains an upside WR3 for fantasy purposes.

news.body: DK Metcalf caught 3-of-5 targets for 31 yards and a touchdown in a 30-27 win over the Bengals.
news.head: DK Metcalf hauls in first TD pass in Week 3 win
news.impact: Metcalf found the end zone on a six-yard connection with Aaron Rodgers in the third quarter. The yardage totals and receptions have not been there for Metcalf yet this season, but he will look for an uptick in production against the Browns in Week 4.

news.body: Steelers WR DK Metcalf caught 4-of-9 targets for 27 yards in a 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
news.head: DK Metcalf leads team in targets in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Metcalf was shadowed by Patriots DB Christian Gonzalez for the majority of the game, limiting his production and forcing Aaron Rodgers to look elsewhere. Metcalf has lead the team in targets in the first two games, so the target volume is encouraging, fantasy managers are just waiting for it to result in more production. Metcalf and the Steelers will take on the Bengals in Week 3.

news.body: DK Metcalf caught four of his 10 targets for 40 yards in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.head: DK Metcalf leads Steelers with 10 targets in Week 1
news.impact: Metcalf didn't do much damage but his usage was encouraging as he easily led the Steelers in targets while newcomer Michael Pittman Jr. saw just three looks from Aaron Rodgers. Metcalf will be a high-end WR3 in fantasy heading into Week 2 against the Patriots.

news.body: Dohnte Meyers hauled in 7-of-9 targets for 82 yards in Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: Dohnte Meyers racks up 82 yards in loss Sunday
news.impact: Meyers stepped up in a big way on Sunday. He finished with 82 yards on seven catches against the Jaguars, although that wasn't enough to propel the Bengals to a win. They will likely need to rely on him more moving forward with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) both currently at risk of missing time due to injuries.

news.body: Dontayvion Wicks caught 3-of-5 targets for just 18 yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Dontayvion Wicks disappoints in loss Sunday
news.impact: Wicks wasn't able to get much going on Sunday. He finished with just 18 yards through the air against the Rams, which of course left him with a poor fantasy total. He should bounce back sometime in the near future, though a big part of his outlook will also depend on the health of Devonta Smith (hamstring) moving forward.

news.body: Dontayvion Wicks caught two of his five targets for 32 yards in a 27-7 loss to the Bears in Week 3.
news.head: Dontayvion Wicks draws five targets in Week 3
news.impact: Wicks finished second on the team in receiving yards on a rough evening for the Philly passing attack. The veteran wideout has been solid for the Eagles thus far, catching nine passes for 179 yards and a touchdown through three games. He will be a flex option in fantasy heading into Week 4 against the Rams.

news.body: Dontayvion Wicks caught five of his six targets for 74 yards in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.head: Dontayvion Wicks goes for 74 yards in Week 2
news.impact: Wicks finished second on the Eagles in all receiving categories in the close win. The veteran wideout could stay involved as the Eagles lost Dallas Goedert to a knee injury in the game. Wicks is on the radar as a flex option in fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Bears.

news.body: Dontayvion Wicks hauled in two of his four targets for 73 yards and one touchdown in the Eagles’ 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Dontayvion Wicks finds end zone in Week 1 win
news.impact: Wicks made the most of his modest target share in the season opener, averaging 36.5 yards per reception in the win. The wideout offers head coach Nick Sirianni another explosive pass-catching option moving forward, with a favorable Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans up next.

news.body: Drake London hauled in 5-of-6 targets for 96 yards in Monday night's 45-24 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Drake London leads team in receiving Monday
news.impact: Most of Atlanta's receiving options didn't see much work on Monday with how dominant the team's running game was, but London was the exception to that. He fell just four yards shy of a 100-yard outing against the Saints and finished with another good performance for fantasy managers. He has looked great ever since QB Michael Penix Jr. took the starting job for the Falcons, so he should continue to be a great fantasy asset for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Drake London caught 9 of 10 targets for 194 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
news.head: Drake London goes for 194 yards in win over Green Bay
news.impact: London was fantastic in this game, spurred on by the return of Michael Penix. When Penix has been at the helm of the offense, London has been among the best fantasy producers in the game, and it showed once again on Thursday. He should be a locked in starter whenever Penix is playing.

news.body: Drake London caught four of five targets for 51 yards in the Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
news.head: Drake London quiet in loss to Panthers
news.impact: London had a better game than last week, but it still is nowhere near what you drafted him to do. The Falcons' quarterback play has been abysmal so far, which is the primary contributor to his struggles. But hopefully Michael Penix can fix things if he can return on Thursday.

news.body: Drake London caught two of his four targets for 29 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1. He also gained six yards on his lone carry in the game.
news.head: Drake London held to two catches in Week 1 loss
news.impact: London was quiet in the close loss, although his 29 receiving yards were good enough for him to finish second on the Falcons in that category. The Falcons were forced to play Cooper Rush, their third-string QB, thanks to injuries, so London should bounce back once either Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix is ready to return to the field. London sets up as a low-end WR1 heading into Week 2 against Carolina.

news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught two of his four targets for 13 yards in a 17-14 loss to the Packers in Week 4.
news.head: Emeka Egbuka held to 13 yards in Week 4 loss
news.impact: Egbuka was quiet with rookie Jalon Daniels making his NFL debut at quarterback for the Bucs. Daniels seemed to key in on Cade Otton and Chris Godwin when dropping back to pass, leaving Egbuka with his least productive performance of the season. Overall, Egbuka has 15 catches for 154 yards and one touchdown through four games. Hard to trust without Baker Mayfield under center, Egbuka will be a flex option in fantasy in Week 5 vs. the Cowboys.

news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught 5-of-9 targets for 62 yards in the Buccaneers 23-16 loss against the Vikings on Sunday.
news.head: Emeka Egbuka totals 62 yards Sunday
news.impact: Egbuka was the leading receiver for Tampa Bay on the day. He has still yet to have one of his huge explosive games. The status of Baker Mayfield will need to be monitored after he left the game late with a dislocated thumb.

news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught 3-of-5 targets for 16 yards and a touchdown in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns.
news.head: Emeka Egbuka has touchdown salvage performance Sunday
news.impact: It would have been a disastrous afternoon for Egbuka if it weren't for a touchdown he hauled in. He'll remain a WR2 play next week against the Vikings.

news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught 5-of-6 targets for 63 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Emeka Egbuka totals 63 yards Sunday
news.impact: Egbuka entered Sunday fully healthy after coming off a toe injury. He got off to a strong start in the first half, but he was not targeted in the second half despite the Bucs trailing. He remains a WR2 heading into Week 2.

news.body: Garrett Wilson caught three of his four targets for 27 yards in a 23-12 loss to the Bears in Week 4.
news.head: Garrett Wilson held to 27 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Wilson and the Jets struggled to get anything going in the loss to Chicago. The Jets were held to just 119 passing yards, with most of the damage coming via a 58-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Williams. Wilson has caught 24 passes for 270 yards and two touchdowns through four games. He will be a low-end WR1/high-end WR2 in fantasy in a Week 5 home matchup against the Browns.

news.body: Garrett Wilson caught 10-of-13 targets for 107 yards and a touchdown in a 31-24 loss to the Lions.
news.head: Garrett Wilson hauls in 10 passes in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Wilson caught a 24-yard strike from Geno Smith in the fourth quarter to tie the game. Fantasy managers will want to monitor Wilson's status early in the week as he did exit with an injury on the final drive. Wilson and the Jets will take on the Bears in Week 4.

news.body: Garrett Wilson exited Sunday’s contest between the New York Jets and Detroit Lions with an apparent injury.
news.head: Garrett Wilson exits Sunday
news.impact: Wilson was seen limping to the sideline late in the fourth quarter for head coach Aaron Glenn, hauling in 10 of his team-leading 13 targets for 107 yards and one touchdown before exiting.

news.body: Garrett Wilson hauled in five of his seven targets for 57 yards and one touchdown in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
news.head: Garrett Wilson finds end zone in Week 2 loss to Packers
news.impact: Wilson continues to make the most of sizeable involvement in an underperforming passing attack to begin the season, recording five or more receptions in each of the first two games. The wideout remains one of the more impactful options as part of a Jets offense filled with more questions than answers early on ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions.

news.body: George Pickens caught 2-of-3 targets for 75 yards in the Cowboys 34-30 win over the Texans.
news.head: George Pickens totals 75 yards Sunday
news.impact: Pickens had a huge 53-yard reception salvage his day. It was the CeeDee Lamb show on Sunday. Pickens remains a WR2 play heading into Thursday’s game against the Buccaneers.

news.body: George Pickens caught seven of his 11 targets for 82 yards in a 34-31 loss to the Ravens in Brazil in Week 3.
news.head: George Pickens draws 11 targets in Week 3
news.impact: Pickens led the way with his 11 targets while finishing second behind CeeDee Lamb in receiving yards. The veteran wideout has now caught 16 passes for 150 scoreless yards through three games this season. He will be on the WR1/WR2 borderline in Week 4 in a matchup against a tough Texans defense.

news.body: George Pickens caught 6-of-8 targets for 40 yards in the Cowboys in a win over the Commanders.
news.head: George Pickens hauls in six passes in Week 2
news.impact: Pickens had a much needed bounce back performance after tallying just three receptions. Although Pickens has not found the endzone yet this season, the increase in targets and receptions over the first week is a strong sign that Pickens will remain a factor in this offense. The Cowboys will take on the Ravens in Week 3.

news.body: George Pickens caught 3-of-6 targets for just 28 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: George Pickens held to 28 yards Sunday
news.impact: Pickens had an extremely disappointing start to the season on Sunday night. He was held to just 28 yards on three catches in the team's first game of the season after being hyped up as an elite fantasy prospect throughout the preseason. He should bounce back and play better than this moving forward, but his week-to-week floor may be lower than some realize if Dallas' offense struggles with consistency this season.

news.body: Isaac TeSlaa hauled in 4-of-8 targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
news.head: Isaac TeSlaa approaches 100 yards on Sunday night
news.impact: TeSlaa had his biggest game of the season so far Sunday night, and has been showing off his big-play ability over the last two games. Over the past two Sundays, the second-year receiver has brought down seven passes for an average of 23.0 yards per catch. TeSlaa has certainly entered the flex conversation as a boom-or-bust option heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Cardinals.

news.body: Isaac TeSlaa caught 3-of-3 targets for 66 yards in a 31-24 win over the Jets.
news.head: Isaac TeSlaa hauls in three passes in Week 3
news.impact: TeSlaa led the team in receiving yardage despite the limited volume. His three receptions and 66 yards both are season highs for the 24-year-old, and he will look to build on this performance in a road matchup against Carolina.

news.body: Isaac TeSlaa caught 2-of-5 targets for 26 yards in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Isaac TeSlaa catches two passes Thursday
news.impact: TeSlaa saw more involvement on Thursday night than he did in the team's season opener last week. He was targeted five times, but he was only able to turn that into two catches for 26 yards. He won't be fantasy relevant moving forward unless someone ahead of him on the depth chart goes down with an injury.

news.body: Isaac TeSlaa failed to catch his only target in the Lions' 31-30 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1.
news.head: Isaac TeSlaa sees one target in Week 1
news.impact: TeSlaa saw minimal involvement in the Detroit passing attack for head coach Dan Campbell, finishing tied for last on the team in targets in the win. The second-year wideout remains difficult to trust in all formats, with a Week 2 road contest against the Buffalo Bills up next.

news.body: Isaiah Williams caught two of his three targets for 73 yards and a touchdown in a 23-12 loss to the Bears in Week 4.
news.head: Isaiah Williams finds the end zone in Week 4
news.impact: Williams was one of the few bright spots for the Jets in the loss as he hauled in a 58-yard touchdown pass from Geno Smith in the fourth quarter. Williams now has 10 catches for 135 yards and one touchdown through four games. If Adonai Mitchell (finger) misses a third straight game in Week 5 vs. the Browns, Williams will be on the flex radar in fantasy.

news.body: Isaiah Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in a 31-24 loss to the Lions.
news.head: Isaiah Williams hauls in one pass in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Williams saw a big drop in his target share after logging six targets in Week 2. The performance is disappointing considering the Jets were without Adonai Mitchell. Williams and the Jets will look to bounce back against the Bears in Week 4.

news.body: Isaiah Williams hauled in all six of his targets for 34 yards while also rushing once for 14 yards in the Jets' 20-17 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.
news.head: Isaiah Williams sees seven touches in Week 2
news.impact: Williams made the most of increased involvement in an underwhelming passing attack, finishing tied for first in receptions in the loss. The wideout remains difficult to trust as another inconsistent pass-catching option ahead of a favorable Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions.

news.body: Isaiah Williams caught 5-of-7 targets for 24 yards in the Jets 35-8 loss to the Bills.
news.head: Isaiah Williams leads Jets in receiving in Week 18
news.impact: Williams led the team in targets, yards, and receptions in the loss to Buffalo. The 24-year-old logged four or more targets in each of the last four games to close out the 2025 season. Williams is under contract with the Jets currently for the 2026 season.

news.body: Jahan Dotson hauled in 2-of-3 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 45-24 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.head: Jahan Dotson hauls in touchdown Monday
news.impact: Dotson contributed well in Week 4, logging over 50 yards and getting into the end zone in a blowout win over the Saints. This was a good game for the veteran, but fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to have consistent value moving forward.

news.body: The Falcons signed WR Jahan Dotson to a two-year contract worth $15 million.
news.head: Jahan Dotson signs two-year deal with Falcons
news.impact: Dotson will have a chance to earn his way into the role held by Darnell Mooney. He had a limited role in Philadelphia behind AJ Brown and DeVonta Smith. He'll be a WR3 at best from a fantasy football perspective, but more likely in the WR4 range.

news.body: Jahan Dotson caught three of his eight targets for 40 yards in a 24-17 loss to the Commanders in Week 18.
news.head: Jahan Dotson goes for 40 yards in Week 18
news.impact: Dotson got some extra looks with the Eagles resting A.J. Brown in the final game of the regular season. The eight targets were a season-high for the veteran wideout. He will go back to a depth role in next week's home matchup against the 49ers in the Wild-Card round of the playoffs.

news.body: Jahan Dotson caught one of his three targets for 12 yards in the Eagles' 24-15 loss to the Bears in Week 15.
news.head: Jahan Dotson catches one pass in Week 13
news.impact: Dotson remains minimally involved in the Philadelphia offense, recording three targets or less in all 12 games. The wideout can remain off rosters in all formats until further notice, with a Week 14 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.body: Jakobi Meyers caught three passes for 33 yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Jakobi Meyers catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: The veteran wasn't able to do much of note on Sunday, finishing with just 33 yards in a narrow win over the Bengals. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be relevant moving forward, however, especially with some tough matchups coming up for Jacksonville's offense over the next two weeks.

news.body: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) listed as limited Thursday
news.impact: As expected, Meyers remained a limited participant for another practice on Thursday. He should be good to go for Sunday's game, however, assuming he doesn't suffer any setbacks between now and then.

news.body: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) limited participant Wednesday
news.impact: The veteran wideout is again listed with thumb injury that left him limited at practice on Wednesday, but it's not a serious issue and shouldn't prevent him from playing in Week 4. He doesn't project to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy option at this point in the season, however.

news.body: Jakobi Meyers caught 7-of-8 targets for 64 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 blowout win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Jakobi Meyers leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: Meyers had a fantastic game against his former team on Sunday. He led the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards over the course of the afternoon and was also able to score a touchdown, which was the cherry on top. This was a good game for the veteran, but fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to put up numbers like this week-in and week-out moving forward.

news.body: Jalen Coker (quad) is inactive for the Panthers game against the Lions on Sunday night.
news.head: Jalen Coker (quad) inactive on Sunday against Lions
news.impact: With Coker out due to his quad injury, Tetairoa McMillan and Darren Waller will operate as the primary one-two for the Carolina passing game. Brycen Tremayne is a sneaky flex start as he will operate as the Panthers WR2.

news.body: Jalen Coker (quad) who is listed as questionable due to a quad injury, is unlikely to play Sunday against the Lions.
news.head: Jalen Coker (quad) unlikely to play on Sunday
news.impact: If Coker sits, Tetairoa McMillan and Darren Waller are priority starts against a weak Lions secondary in a game that profiles as a shootout. Brycen Tremayne is another name to watch in deeper leagues, as he will likely see an aexpanded role if Coker does in fact sit.

news.body: Jalen Coker is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Lions.
news.head: Jalen Coker (quad) listed questionable Sunday
news.impact: Coker remained limited in practice on Friday. His status will need to be monitored heading into kickoff Sunday night, but he appears to be on the favorable side of questionable.

news.body: Jalen Coker (quad) was officially a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Jalen Coker (quad) officially limited Thursday
news.impact: Coker was upgraded to a limited participant on Thursday after being a non-participant on Wednesday. That's a big step in the right direction for his Week 4 availability, and we should get an official injury designation for him sometime after practice on Friday. He should be considered startable if he's cleared to play without limitations on Sunday.

news.body: Jalen Nailor was not targeted in a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs in Week 4.
news.head: Jalen Nailor leaves Week 4 with a concussion
news.impact: Nailor suffered a concussion during the first half and did not return. He will now enter the league's concussion protocol as he attempts to get cleared in time for a Week 5 matchup against the Patriots.

news.body: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
news.head: Jalen Nailor catches one pass Sunday
news.impact: Nailor remains uninvolved in the offense with Las Vegas. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for nine yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Jalen Nailor quiet in win Sunday
news.impact: Nailor was a non-factor on Sunday. He caught just one pass against the Chargers and wasn't able to do much of note with it. He isn't expected to be a good fantasy option moving forward, especially with Brock Bowers (knee) set to return to the lineup in the very near future.

news.body: Jalen Nailor caught three of his five targets for 27 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
news.head: Jalen Nailor catches three passes in Week 1
news.impact: Nailor was one of many that saw involvement in the Las Vegas passing offense, finishing as one of six to catch at least one pass in the win. The wideout will look to offer more impactful potential in a revamped Las Vegas offense as the season moves forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.body: Ja'Marr Chase is going through the league's concussion protocol.
news.head: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) in protocol, labeled day-to-day
news.impact: Chase will need to clear the protocol before having a chance to play Sunday in Miami, but it is a positive sign that head coach Zac Taylor said Monday that the star wideout is day-to-day. Chase was knocked out of Week 4's loss to the Jaguars early, leaving plenty of extra targets for Tee Higgins and the rest of the Bengals' route runners.

news.body: The Bengals have ruled out WR Ja'Marr Chase for the remainder of Week 4 with a concussion.
news.head: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) ruled out
news.impact: Chase was injured on a facemask penalty in the first half and will not return. He caught all three of his targets for 27 yards prior to the injury. Tee Higgins and Dohnte Meyers will serve as the primary wide receivers for the remainder of the game.

news.body: Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase is headed to the locker room. He is now being evaluated for a concussion and is questionable to return.
news.head: Ja'Marr Chase headed to the locker room
news.impact: Chase suffered an apparent injury on the Bengals’ last possession after a face mask penalty by a Jaguars’ defender. The Bengals will turn to Tee Higgins as the primary pass catcher if Chase cannot return.

news.body: Ja'Marr Chase caught 9-of-12 targets for 98 yards and a touchdown in a 30-27 loss to the Steelers.
news.head: Ja'Marr Chase excellent in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Chase led the team in all of the receiving categories for the Bengals Sunday. Chase and Joe Burrow connected on a three-yard touchdown strike in the first quarter. Chase and the Bengals will take on the Jaguars in Week 4.

news.body: Jameson Williams came up with 6-of-8 targets for 102 yards in Sunday's 32-26 loss to the Panthers.
news.head: Jameson Williams clears 100 yards in Week 4 loss
news.impact: After being held under 50 yards and no more than four grabs over the first three weeks of the season, Williams finally got going Sunday night. The big-play blazer had a long gain of 49 yards and averaged 17 yards on his half-dozen receptions. Williams should be viewed as an upside WR3 heading into Week 5.

news.body: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-4 targets for 49 yards in a 31-24 win over the Jets.
news.head: Jameson Williams hauls in four passes in Week 3 win
news.impact: Williams took a back seat in the offense Sunday with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs dominating the targets against the Jets. Williams will look to become more involved in the offense in a Week 4 matchup with the Panthers.

news.body: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 33 yards in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Jameson Williams underwhelming in loss Thursday
news.impact: Williams had another disappointing performance on Thursday night. He caught just two passes in this matchup against the Bills and was only able to turn that into 33 scoreless yards, leaving him with a poor fantasy total on the night. Fantasy managers should recognize his low week-to-week floor when determining whether or not to start him in any given game moving forward.

news.body: Jameson Williams caught four of his nine targets for 45 yards in the Lions' 31-30 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1.
news.head: Jameson Williams sees nine targets in Week 1 win
news.impact: Williams would have offered even more of an explosive impact if not for a couple of deep throw drops on passes from quarterback Jared Goff. The wideout remains a high-impact, explosive pass-catching option for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 2 road contest against the Buffalo Bills.

news.body: Jauan Jennings caught just one pass for eight yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Jauan Jennings held to one catch Sunday
news.impact: Jennings wasn't able to get much going on Sunday, finishing with just one catch in the team's win over Miami. He wasn't able to contribute even with Justin Jefferson (ankle) being out of the lineup for the Vikings, so he surely shouldn't be expected to produce when the star wideout is able to make his return to the lineup.

news.body: Jauan Jennings caught 1-of-2 targets for one yard in the Vikings 23-16 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
news.head: Jauan Jennings catches one pass Sunday
news.impact: Jennings was unable to take advantage of the absence of Justin Jefferson (ankle) leaving early. He remains off the fantasy radar for now.

news.body: Jauan Jennings (personal) will be good to go for Week 3's matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
news.head: Jauan Jennings (personal) good to go for Week 3
news.impact: Jennings missed last week's game due to a personal issue that he was tending to, but he is back and fully good to go ahead of Minnesota's matchup against the Buccaneers in Week 3. He should play but isn't expected to be a relevant fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said Jauan Jennings is expected to return for Week 3.
news.head: Jauan Jennings (personal) expected to return for Week 3
news.impact: Jennings did not play on Sunday due to personal reasons. He was targeted just once in Week 1. He's off the fantasy radar for now.

news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 5-of-6 targets for 76 yards in the Seahawks 30-23 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba totals 76 yards Sunday
news.impact: It was a quiet day for the standards of Smith-Njigba. Sam Darnold also missed him wide open on multiple plays. He remains a WR1 play next week against the 49ers.

news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba hauled in 10 of his team-leading 14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns in the Seahawks’ 33-31 Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba dynamic again in Week 3 loss to Commanders
news.impact: Smith-Njigba continues an explosive start to the season, recording eight or more receptions, over 120 receiving yards, and own or more receiving touchdowns in each of the first three games. The wideout remains another explosive WR1 in all formats ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers.

news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9 of 11 targets for 155 yards and three touchdowns in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has hat trick of touchdowns in win
news.impact: JSN has been on an absolute tear to start the season, with 277 yards through the first two games. He's looking QB-proof at the moment, and as long as Drew Lock can continue to get him the ball with Sam Darnold still out, JSN is an auto start. Not that you were sitting him anyway. He gets a great matchup against the Commanders next week.

news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 8-of-11 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown in Wednesday night's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba electric in win Wednesday
news.impact: On Wednesday, Smith-Njigba picked up right where he left off last season, exploding for 122 yards and a touchdown in a big win over the Patriots. He did that with Drew Lock throwing him passes after starter Sam Darnold went down with a hip injury earlier in the game. Fantasy managers should be happy with his performance in this matchup but should keep a close eye on the health of Darnold, as the young wideout's week-to-week ceiling will certainly take a hit if their starting QB misses significant time.

news.body: Jaylen Waddle caught five of his six targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.
news.head: Jaylen Waddle scores touchdown in loss Sunday
news.impact: Waddle didn't put up many yards, but he saved his fantasy day with a 13-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. He finished second on the team in receptions but was held to just 7.0 yards per catch. Waddle remains one of Denver's top options in the passing game and should continue to see enough targets to remain in fantasy lineups as a WR2.

news.body: Jaylen Waddle is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the 49ers.
news.head: Jaylen Waddle (foot) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Waddle was seen in a walking boot after last Sunday's win. He will be a WR2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Jaylen Waddle (foot) logged a full practice session on Thursday.
news.head: Jaylen Waddle (foot) logs full practice Thursday
news.impact: Waddle's foot injury is nothing more than a minor issue, and he has been able to participate fully at practice all week so far. Look for him to play and see a full workload in Week 4.

news.body: Jaylen Waddle is reportedly “fine” after he was spotted in a walking boot following the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams.
news.head: Jaylen Waddle reportedly 'fine' after being seen in walking boot
news.impact: This was reported by The Denver Post’s Sam Jane. This will be something to monitor in practice this week.

news.body: Jaylin Noel caught 3-of-3 targets for 85 yards in the Texans 34-30 loss against the Cowboys.
news.head: Jaylin Noel totals 85 yards Sunday
news.impact: Noel had a huge catch of 52 yards downfield from C.J. Stroud. He remains an upside flex play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Jaylin Noel caught both of his targets for 17 yards in a 19-17 loss to the Colts.
news.head: Jaylin Noel hauls in two passes in Week 3
news.impact: Noel saw his target share drop from his five targets in Week 2. Fantasy managers can leave the 24-year-old on the waiver wire heading into Week 4.

news.body: Jaylin Noel caught 1-of-5 targets for 31 yards in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Jaylin Noel catches one pass Sunday
news.impact: Noel was one of six players to see at least five targets for Houston on Sunday. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role with the ball being spread around.

news.body: Jaylin Noel hauled in both of his targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.head: Jaylin Noel shows big-play ability on limited targets
news.impact: Noel only got two looks from C.J. Stroud on Sunday, but he had the longest gain of the day with a 35-yard pickup. The second-year receiver out of Iowa State has big-play potential every week, but he may not see enough volume to move beyond being a boom-or-bust fantasy option.

news.body: Jordan Addison caught 4-of-6 targets for 52 yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Jordan Addison solid in win Sunday
news.impact: Addison had an okay game on Sunday. He finished with 52 yards en route to a win over the Dolphins, but many fantasy managers were expecting more from him in the absence of Justin Jefferson (ankle). He should continue to have value if Jefferson misses more time, otherwise he won't be worth starting moving forward.

news.body: Jordan Addison caught 5-of-9 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings 23-16 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
news.head: Jordan Addison leads the way for Vikings Sunday
news.impact: Addison took on a bigger role with Justin Jefferson (ankle) exiting early. He hauled in a 41-yard touchdown pass from Kyler Murray. He'll jump into a WR2/WR3 play next week against the Dolphins if Jefferson is sidelined.

news.body: Jordan Addison hauled in two of his five targets for 21 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Jordan Addison sees five targets in Week 2 win
news.impact: Addison has struggled to make an impact as part of an underwhelming Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, finishing with two receptions or less in each of the first two games. The wideout remains a high-risk pass-catching option in all formats ahead of a Week 3 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

news.body: Jordan Addison did not catch either of his two targets in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.head: Jordan Addison fails to catch pass Sunday
news.impact: Justin Jefferson dominated the targets after Carson Wentz took over behind center. Addison will be in the WR3/WR4 mix heading into Week 2 against a vulnerable Bears defense.

news.body: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is still considered “weeks away” from returning from IR due to his hamstring injury, despite being eligible to return at the conclusion of Week 4. It appears Week 7 is the earliest we could see him return, but the Saints bye is the following week, so Week 9 is sounding more realistic.
news.head: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) still ‘weeks away’ from return
news.impact: It’s a tough blow for Tyson’s stock and for fantasy managers who have held on to him this long. Tyson has loads of promise and could unlock something for a Saints offense that’s already looking good. However, we will have to wait several more weeks to see him on the field, and in his absence, Juwan Johnson and Devaughn Vele will continue to be viable starts.

news.body: The Saints placed Jordyn Tyson on injured reserve.
news.head: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) placed on IR
news.impact: Tyson is expected to miss roughly two months with a hamstring injury. He has been dealing with hamstring issues since college at Arizona State.

news.body: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is out for the next two months with a hamstring injury he suffered in training camp.
news.head: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) out for two months with hamstring injury
news.impact: It’s a tough blow to the Saints, who were hopeful to have their full complement of weapons to start the year. The timeline puts Tyson returning near the middle of October, and expect a ramp-up period for him once he returns. For those who haven’t drafted yet, expect his ADP to fall dramatically as he will be unusable foe the first several weeks of the season, if not longer.

news.body: Saints coach Kellen Moore said the hamstring injury Jordyn Tyson is dealing with is still being evaluated.
news.head: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) still being evaluated
news.impact: It is not ideal for the rookie as he remains without a clear timetable to return. There should be a further update on Tyson at some point in the next week.

news.body: Josh Cameron caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
news.head: Josh Cameron snags touchdown in NFL debut
news.impact: The rookie receiver had the wonderful experience of catching a touchdown in his first-ever regular-season game. However, it's hard to take much from it for fantasy, as the Jaguars' passing attack is incredibly spread out and Cameron is buried on the depth chart. His usage might trend up as the season goes along, and he's at least a name to monitor for dynasty formats. But don't expect anything big in the short term.

news.body: The Jacksonville Jaguars have selected WR Josh Cameron with the No. 191 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.head: Josh Cameron selected No. 191 by Jacksonville Jaguars
news.impact: The Jacksonville Jaguars have a plethora of wide receivers after investing first-round picks in back-to-back years on Brian Thomas Jr. and Travis Hunter. They also have Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington, leaving little to no opportunity for Josh Cameron to have a fantasy impact without significant injuries to the team's wide receiver corps.

news.body: Baylor WR Josh Cameron is on track to be fully healthy by rookie minicamp.
news.head: Josh Cameron (calf) on track to be fully healthy for rookie minicamp
news.impact: Cameron suffered a calf strain at the Combine. He has spent time with 15 teams on visits, including the Falcons most recently.

news.body: Josh Downs caught 3-of-4 targets for 16 yards in the Colts win over the Commanders Sunday.
news.head: Josh Downs quiet in Week 4 win
news.impact: Downs saw a season low in targets Sunday. The Colts did move to a heavy ground game after the Commanders lost Marcus Mariota to a knee injury in the first half. Downs will look to get back on track in Week 5 against the Steelers.

news.body: Josh Downs caught 5-of-11 targets for 77 yards in a 19-17 win over Houston.
news.head: Josh Downs hauls in five passes in Week 3 win
news.impact: Downs led the team in receiving yards and targets in the win over Houston. With Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve, fantasy managers should expect Downs to continue to see plenty of targets from Daniel Jones. Downs and the Colts will take on the Commanders in Week 4.

news.body: Josh Downs hauled in 7-of-9 targets for 72 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Josh Downs leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: The Colts needed Downs to step up on Sunday night, and he did just that, delivering a team-high 72 yards in a narrow loss to the Chiefs. He seems primed to improve as a fantasy option in the near future with Alec Pierce (heel) seemingly set to miss some time after aggravating an injury.

news.body: Josh Downs caught two of his four targets for 37 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.head: Josh Downs catches two passes in Week 1
news.impact: Downs saw modest involvement in an underperforming Indianapolis passing attack, finishing third on the team in targets in the loss. The wideout remains one of the more risky pass-catchers entering a difficult Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.body: Joshua Palmer hauled in 1-of-3 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Joshua Palmer hauls in long touchdown Thursday
news.impact: The veteran wideout wasn't very involved on Thursday night, but he was able to catch one of his three targets and take it 43 yards to the house for a touchdown. Still, fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be fantasy relevant for the foreseeable future, even if DJ Moore (shoulder) misses time for Buffalo.

news.body: Joshua Palmer caught one of two targets for 34 yards and a score in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.head: Joshua Palmer snags touchdown in win over Houston
news.impact: Palmer’s fantasy day was saved by the touchdown, but unless you have him in bestball formats, it didn’t do your team much good. He’s the fifth best target at best in Buffalo right now, so it will be slim pickings with the roster currently healthy.

news.body: Joshua Palmer (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's playoff matchup with the Jaguars.
news.head: Joshua Palmer (ankle) questionable for Sunday
news.impact: Palmer was on the field for 84% of the Bills' offensive snaps in Week 18, but he managed just one catch on three targets for one yard. If Palmer does play, he seems highly unlikely to make much of an impact. The veteran WR finished the regular season with only 22 receptions over 12 games.

news.body: Bills WR Joshua Palmer (ankle) is officially active for Week 15.
news.head: Joshua Palmer (ankle) officially active for Week 15
news.impact: Palmer was considered questionable to play after being limited in practice to close out the week. With Gabe Davis inactive, Palmer should see WR3 looks against New England.

news.body: Justin Jefferson (ankle) optimistic about returning in Week 5.
news.head: Justin Jefferson (ankle) aiming for Week 5 return
news.impact: Jefferson has already been ruled out for Week 4, but the Vikings are planning to try to get him back on the field for Week 5's matchup with the Saints. Jefferson is still rehabbing his injured ankle this weekend and hopes to return to the practice field next week.

news.body: Justin Jefferson (ankle) has been ruled out for the Minnesota Vikings against the Miami Dolphins Sunday according to Tom Pelissero.
news.head: Justin Jefferson (ankle) ruled out Sunday
news.impact: Jefferson will not suit up after struggling to take the practice field all week for head coach Kevin O’Connell, with Jordan Addison in line for a sizeable target share against the Dolphins Sunday.

news.body: Justin Jefferson remained absent from practice on Friday.
news.head: Justin Jefferson (ankle) not seen practicing Friday
news.impact: Jefferson continues to trend towards being ruled out on Sunday. Jordan Addison and TJ Hockenson would both step into bigger roles in the passing game.

news.body: Justin Jefferson (ankle) was officially a non-participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Justin Jefferson (ankle) officially doesn't practice Thursday
news.impact: As expected, Jefferson was sidelined for a second-straight practice on Thursday as he continues to recover from an ankle injury of some kind. His availability for Week 4 will largely hinge on his participation status at practice on Friday, so fantasy managers should continue to keep up with all updates about his health over the next 24 hours or so.

news.body: Kalif Raymond caught both of his targets for six yards in a 23-12 win over the Jets in Week 4.
news.head: Kalif Raymond held to two catches in Week 4
news.impact: Raymond came back to earth in the win after he had been a big part of the Chicago passing attack over the first three games of the season. The veteran wideout now has 21 catches for 220 yards and one touchdown through four games. He will be on the flex radar in Week 5 vs. the Packers.

news.body: Kalif Raymond caught six of his seven targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in a 27-7 win over the Eagles in Week 3.
news.head: Kalif Raymond leads Bears in receiving in Week 3
news.impact: Raymond's surprise involvement in the Chicago passing attack continues as he posted his most productive game of the season. The veteran wideout has caught 19 passes for 214 yards and a touchdown through three games while outproducing both Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Raymond will be a solid fantasy option in Week 4 against the Jets.

news.body: Kalif Raymond caught all five of his targets for 40 yards in the Bears' 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.
news.head: Kalif Raymond catches five passes in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Raymond continues to make the most of solid involvement in the Chicago passing attack to begin the season, recording five or more receptions in each of the first two games. The wideout continues to take advantage of his familiarity with head coach Ben Johnson's offense, with a Week 3 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles up next.

news.body: Kalif Raymond hauled in eight of his team-leading nine targets for 84 yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: Kalif Raymond leads pass-catchers in Week 1 win over Panthers
news.impact: Raymond made an immediate impact after rejoining his former offensive coordinator in the offseason, finishing first in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the win. The wideout remains one of many dynamic options in a crowded wide receiver room, with a Week 2 contest against the Minnesota Vikings up next.

news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-4 targets for 36 yards in the Texans 34-30 loss against the Cowboys.
news.head: Kayshon Boutte catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Boutte remains off the fantasy radar in his current role in the Texans wide receiver room.

news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught both of his targets for 21 yards in a 19-17 loss to the Colts.
news.head: Kayshon Boutte hauls in two passes in Week 3
news.impact: Boutte continues to struggle to carve out a clear role in the Houston offense, even with Nico Collins (hamstring) out of the lineup. The 24-year-old will look to improve on his season long numbers in a Week 4 matchup against a banged up Dallas' secondary.

news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Kayshon Boutte catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Boutte continues to learn the playback in his second game with the Texans. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role as an upside WR4/WR5.

news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.head: Kayshon Boutte makes only catch in Texans debut
news.impact: Boutte was acquired from New England late in the preseason to shore up the Texans' wide receiver corps. His big-play potential is known from the last couple of years with the Patriots, but his targets were predictably limited in an offense that is still relatively new to him. Boutte is a wait-and-see bench stash in standard fantasy leagues.

news.body: KC Concepcion Jr. secured 5-of-8 targets for 64 yards in Thursday's 27-24 win over the Steelers.
news.head: KC Concepcion Jr. hauls in five passes Thursday night
news.impact: After managing to catch just two of his nine targets in Week 3, Concepcion bounced back with a new career high in receiving yards Thursday night. Concepcion has quickly carved out his role in the Browns' offense, as the rookie is tied for the team lead with 17 receptions through four games. He's averaged only 8.5 yards on those catches with a long of 21 and has yet to find the end zone. Still, he is a decent play in deeper PPR formats.

news.body: KC Concepcion Jr. caught 2-of-9 targets for just nine yards in Sunday's 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: KC Concepcion Jr. quiet in win Sunday
news.impact: The rookie was targeted a team-high nine times on Sunday, but he was only able to catch two of those targets for just nine yards in a win over the Panthers. He doesn't project to have consistent fantasy value for the foreseeable future.

news.body: KC Concepcion Jr. caught 6-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
news.head: KC Concepcion Jr. catches six passes Sunday
news.impact: Concepcion caught all six targets he saw, but they only resulted in 28 yards. Denzel Boston has appeared to emerge as the WR1 on the Browns offense.

news.body: KC Concepcion caught four of five targets for 43 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars. He also ran the ball three times for 15 yards.
