news.head: KC Concepcion snags four passes in loss to Jags
news.impact: While it wasn't a massive day, it was encouraging that Concepcion got touches as both a receiver and out of the backfield, showing the team wanted to get the ball in his hands. A loss is a loss, but brighter days should be ahead for Concepcion.

news.body: Keenan Allen (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
news.head: Keenan Allen (groin) out for Week 4
news.impact: Allen has been listed as questionable on Friday, but the veteran will indeed sit out Sunday's game. With both Allen and Alec Pierce out of action, the Colts are very thin at wide receiver. Look for Josh Downs and tight end Tyler Warren to be heavily targeted by QB Daniel Jones. Veterans Laquon Treadwell and Darius Slayton could be in the mix as well.

news.body: Keenan Allen (groin) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Keenan Allen (groin) officially questionable for Sunday
news.impact: Allen was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Friday and is officially questionable for Sunday's game as a result. If he is sidelined, fantasy managers should expect Josh Downs and Ashton Dulin (ankle) to both see more work as a result of his absence.

news.body: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) was limited at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) limited at practice Thursday
news.impact: The veteran is dealing with some kind of a minor groin injury, which contributed to him being a limited participant at Thursday's practice. It's not currently thought to be much of an issue for him, but fantasy managers should keep an eye on what his injury status ends up being heading into the weekend.

news.body: Keenan Allen caught 6-of-9 targets for 63 yards and a touchdown in a 19-17 win over the Texans.
news.head: Keenan Allen finds the end zone in Week 3
news.impact: Allen turned in his best performance of the season and found the end zone for the first time as a Colt. With Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve, fantasy managers should expect Allen to see an increase in playing time. Allen and the Colts will take on the Commanders in Week 4.

news.body: Kendrick Bourne did not log a single target or touch in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Kendrick Bourne fails to log catch Sunday
news.impact: The veteran was entirely uninvolved on Sunday. He didn't register even a single target against the Giants, so he logged a big goose egg as far as fantasy scoring is concerned. He is not expected to be fantasy relevant at any point for the remainder of the season.

news.body: Kendrick Bourne caught 2-of-3 targets for 22 yards in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday.
news.head: Kendrick Bourne catches two passes Sunday
news.impact: Bourne has not been as involved the past two weeks after a big Week 1 performance. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Kendrick Bourne caught 2-of-3 targets for just 11 yards in Sunday's 31-7 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Kendrick Bourne quiet in loss Sunday
news.impact: Bourne came back down to earth in Week 2 after a stellar performance in Arizona's season opener a week before. He only caught two passes for 11 yards on Sunday, but Arizona's offense as a whole struggled in this matchup against Seattle, so there's a good chance that he will bounce back and have relevance as a depth piece in most leagues sometime in the near future.

news.body: Kendrick Bourne caught all eight of his targets for 75 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Kendrick Bourne hauls in eight passes Sunday
news.impact: Well, this was surprising. Bourne outpaced both Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson in Sunday's season opener, finishing just one reception behind TE Trey McBride for the team lead. This effort should make Bourne a popular waiver claim for Week 2, but the Cardinals are headed into a tough matchup against the defending Super Bowl champs.

news.body: Keon Coleman caught 6-of-7 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown in the loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Keon Coleman hauls in a touchdown in Week 4
news.impact: Coleman found the end zone for the first time this season on a 34-yard touchdown reception in the fourth quarter. Coleman set a new season high in yardage and targets in the loss Sunday. Fantasy managers could see Coleman become a bigger part of the offense heading into Week 5 after this performance.

news.body: Keon Coleman (ankle) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
news.head: Keon Coleman (ankle) cleared to play Sunday
news.impact: Coleman was on Buffalo's injury report throughout the week due to an ankle issue that has been bothering him recently, but it's not a serious issue and he has been cleared to play through it in Week 4. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to get a large workload with DJ Moore (shoulder) also inactive, however.

news.body: Bills head coach Joe Brady said Keon Coleman "should be good to go" for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
news.head: Keon Coleman (ankle) 'should be good to go' Sunday
news.impact: Coleman was limited in practice on Thursday. He remains a volatile WR4/WR5 for fantasy managers.

news.body: Keon Coleman was limited in practice on Thursday.
news.head: Keon Coleman (ankle) limited in practice Thursday
news.impact: Coleman was back after missing practice on Wednesday. It puts him on track to be being good to go to play this week.

news.body: Khalil Shakir caught 7-of-8 targets for 82 yards in the Bills loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Khalil Shakir hauls in seven passes in Week 4
news.impact: Shakir led the team in receptions and targets in the loss Sunday. All three marks are new season highs for Shakir, a potential positive sign for fantasy managers that have rostered him in a tough season. Shakir and the Bills will take on the Rams in Week 5.

news.body: Khalil Shakir caught one of his three targets for six yards in the Bills' 24-16 Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Khalil Shakir quiet in Week 3 win
news.impact: Shakir struggled to make an impact Sunday, finishing with less than three receptions for the first time in three contests. The wideout remains one of many risky pass-catching options in the Buffalo offense to this point, with a Week 4 matchup against the New England Patriots up next.

news.body: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 38 yards in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Khalil Shakir totals 38 yards in win Thursday
news.impact: The veteran wideout wasn't very impactful on Thursday night, catching just three passes for 38 yards on a night where Buffalo's offense couldn't be stopped. He isn't expected to be a strong fantasy option for the foreseeable future, although he may be primed for more work than usual for a week or two if DJ Moore (shoulder) has to miss time.

news.body: Khalil Shakir caught four of six targets for 50 yards in the Bills’ 36-31 win over Houston on Sunday.
news.head: Khalil Shakir goes for 50 yards in win
news.impact: Shakir operated as Josh Allen’s safety valve underneath with DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid working over the top. That’s been Shakir’s role in the past, so don’t expect it to stop any time soon. His upside is capped because of it, but he’s a decent flex play in PPR formats if you need a solid floor.

news.body: The Chargers say WR Ladd McConkey is day-to-day.
news.head: Ladd McConkey (foot) now considered day-to-day
news.impact: It was originally reported that McConkey was week-to-week. It is a more positive sign for his status, but he is still likely to sit Week 5 against the Broncos.

news.body: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said WR Ladd McConkey is week-to-week.
news.head: Ladd McConkey (foot) week-to-week
news.impact: McConkey tried to play through the injury on Sunday, but he wound up leaving the game early. He'll likely miss Week 5.

news.body: Ladd McConkey did not catch either of his two targets before leaving Sunday's game early.
news.head: Ladd McConkey exits early Sunday, goes without a catch
news.impact: McConkey had one drop on what would have been a short reception. He was attempting to play through a foot injury. His status will need to be monitored in practice this upcoming week.

news.body: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (foot) is officially active for Week 4.
news.head: Ladd McConkey (foot) officially active for Week 4
news.impact: McConkey was considered questionable to play after being limited in practice throughout the week. The Chargers' offense will need McConkey as the team continues to search for their first win of the season.

news.body: Laquon Treadwell caught 5-of-6 targets for 42 yards in the Colts win over the Commanders.
news.head: Laquon Treadwell hauls in five passes in Week 4 win
news.impact: Treadwell saw an increase in playing time with the Colts dealing with injuries to Alec Pierce and Keenan Allen. Fantasy managers should expect this to be an outlier, as Treadwell's playing time will diminish once Allen and Pierce return.

news.body: Laquon Treadwell caught three passes for 61 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 OT loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Laquon Treadwell racks up 61 yards Sunday
news.impact: The veteran stepped up on Sunday after Alec Pierce left the game due to a heel injury. Treadwell played well and racked up 61 yards on the night, though he still wasn't great from a fantasy perspective. He should be more involved moving forward but still shouldn't be rostered in most league formats.

news.body: Laquon Treadwell failed to catch his only target in the Colts' 41-23 Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens.
news.head: Laquon Treadwell sees one target in Week 1
news.impact: Treadwell operated as more of an afterthought in the Indianapolis passing attack for head coach Shane Steichen, with a difficult Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs up next.

news.body: The Colts have signed WR Laquon Treadwell to their 53-man roster from their practice squad.
news.head: Laquon Treadwell signed to Colts’ active roster
news.impact: The 30-year-old will head to the active roster to provide depth at wide receiver. Fantasy managers should expect the veteran to remain primarily on special teams, as he has yet to see an offensive snap this season.

news.body: Luther Burden III caught four of his six targets for 63 yards and added an 11-yard run in a 23-12 win over the Jets in Week 4.
news.head: Luther Burden III goes for 63 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Burden got off to a fast start, catching three of his four passes in the first quarter, but was held to just one catch the rest of the way. He has been trending up, but fantasy managers are still waiting for a blow-up game from the second-year receiver. He will be a high-end WR3 in fantasy in Week 5 vs. the Packers.

news.body: Luther Burden III caught seven of his 11 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown while adding a seven-yard rush in a 27-7 win over the Eagles in Week 3.
news.head: Luther Burden III finds the end zone in Week 3
news.impact: Burden found the end zone on an eight-yard pass from Case Keenum in the first quarter. The veteran wideout led the Bears in targets and receptions on Monday night, although Kalif Raymond topped him with 90 receiving yards. Burden has 15 catches for 156 yards and one touchdown through three games. He will be a solid fantasy option in Week 4 against the Jets.

news.body: Luther Burden III hauled in three of his seven targets for 32 yards in the Bears' 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.
news.head: Luther Burden III sees seven targets in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Burden III has provided mixed results to begin the season, finishing with less than 50 receiving yards in one of the first two games. The wideout remains difficult to trust as part of an inconsistent Chicago offense early on, with a Week 3 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles up next.

news.body: Luther Burden III hauled in all five of his targets for 63 yards while also rushing once for two yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: Luther Burden III sees six touches in Week 1
news.impact: Burden III saw steady involvement in the Chicago passing attack, finishing second on the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the win. The wideout offers head coach Ben Johnson another dynamic pass-catcher as part of an explosive Chicago offense ahead of a Week 2 divisional matchup with the Minnesota Vikings.

news.body: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel did not have an update on Mack Hollins’ calf injury on Monday.
news.head: Mack Hollins without update on calf injury
news.impact: Hollins exited Week 4’s game against the Bills with a non-contact injury. His status will need to be monitored throughout the week.

news.body: Mack Hollins caught 3-of-4 targets for 53 yards in the Patriots win over the Bills.
news.head: Mack Hollins hauls in three passes in Week 4 win
news.impact: Hollins continues to excel in his role as a chain mover, but the veteran did exit the game with a calf injury. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders.

news.body: Mack Hollins hauled in 6-of-9 targets for 87 yards in Sunday's 35-6 blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: Mack Hollins leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: Hollins was one of the lone bright spots for the Patriots on Sunday. He led the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards against the Jaguars, but that wasn't enough to even keep things close against the Jaguars. He will continue to play a big role for the Patriots moving forward but shouldn't be trusted as a fantasy option at this point in the season.

news.body: Patriots WR Mack Hollins caught both of his targets for 18 yards in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
news.head: Mack Hollins hauls in two passes in Week 2 win
news.impact: Hollins saw his target numbers drop from Week 1, but the passing attack struggled as a whole again. Hollins has a great rapport with QB Drake Maye, which should lead to a potential in increased chances until A.J. Brown returns from injured reserve. Hollins and the Patriots will travel to Jacksonville in Week 3.

news.body: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Makai Lemon underwhelming in loss Sunday
news.impact: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was sidelined for the Eagles on Sunday, but the rookie still wasn't able to take advantage and ended up with just three catches for 27 yards against the Rams. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect much value out of Lemon for the foreseeable future after his slow start to the season.

news.body: Makai Lemon caught three of his four targets for 29 yards in a 27-7 loss to the Bears in Week 3.
news.head: Makai Lemon catches three passes in Week 3
news.impact: Lemon turned in his best game as a pro on Monday night, finishing third on the team in targets and second in catches. The rookie wideout has now caught seven passes for 38 yards through three games. He remains a bench stash in fantasy heading into Week 4 against the Rams.

news.body: Makai Lemon caught his lone target for a 14-yard gain while losing five yards on his only carry in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.head: Makai Lemon sees one target in Week 2
news.impact: Lemon was quiet in the close win as Philly leaned on DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks in the passing attack. Lemon now has just four catches for nine yards through two games as he looks to carve out a larger role in the Eagles' offense. He will not be a recommended fantasy option in Week 3 against the Bears.

news.body: Makai Lemon caught three of his four targets for a loss of five yards on the Eagles’ 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 1.
news.head: Makai Lemon quiet in Week 1
news.impact: Lemon struggled to find any success in the season opener, as the pass-catcher was bottled up by the Commanders defense in the win. The wideout will look for more impactful output in a favorable Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

news.body: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-3 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Malachi Fields hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Fields looked pretty good on Sunday, finishing with over 50 yards and a touchdown en route to a nice win over the Cardinals. It looks like his rookie season is not yet a wash even with QB Jaxson Dart out of the lineup, but there still isn't a big expectation of fantasy success from the young wideout at this point in the season.

news.body: Malachi Fields caught two passes for 19 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Malachi Fields catches two passes Sunday
news.impact: The rookie only caught two passes on Sunday, but considering the very low offensive output of New York's offense as a whole, it doesn't come as much of a surprise. He has flashed some talent over the first few weeks of the season, but his poor situation renders him an irrelevant fantasy option moving forward.

news.body: Malachi Fields hauled in 2-of-6 targets for 30 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Malachi Fields hauls in two passes Monday
news.impact: The Giants were trying to get the rookie wideout the ball on Monday night, but he was only able to haul in two out of his six targets over the course of the game. He finished with just 30 yards and isn't expected to get much better over the next couple of weeks with QB Jaxson Dart (knee) seemingly set to miss some time for New York.

news.body: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-4 targets for 25 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.head: Malachi Fields catches two passes Sunday
news.impact: The rookie saw the field a decent amount on Sunday night. He wasn't able to put up big numbers from a fantasy perspective, however, totaling just 25 yards on two catches against the Cowboys. His debut was a solid performance overall but fantasy managers shouldn't have high hopes for him for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Malik Nabers caught 6-of-7 targets for 112 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Malik Nabers leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: The star wideout seemed to be back to form on Sunday. He finished as the team's top receiver with over 100 yards and a touchdown in their nice win over the Cardinals. It finally looked like he and QB Jameis Winston were on the same page, which bodes well for his future fantasy value moving forward.

news.body: Malik Nabers hauled in 5-of-6 targets for just 26 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Malik Nabers underwhelming in win Sunday
news.impact: Nabers led the team with six targets on Sunday, but he was only able to turn that into five catches for a measly 26 yards over the course of the afternoon. He's a very talented player, but it looks like his fantasy output is going to be sparse for the foreseeable future with QB Jameis Winston currently at the helm for the Giants.

news.body: Malik Nabers (shoulder) was officially a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Malik Nabers (shoulder) officially a full participant Thursday
news.impact: The star wideout was able to log a full practice session on Thursday after suffering this shoulder injury last week. It shouldn't affect his availability moving forward, but his fantasy value is still expected to be lower than it was before with Jameis Winston set to be New York's starting quarterback in place of the injured Jaxson Dart (knee) moving forward.

news.body: Malik Nabers (shoulder) was seen practicing for the Giants on Thursday.
news.head: Malik Nabers (shoulder) seen practicing Thursday
news.impact: Nabers is at practice and was seen participating on Thursday. He recently suffered a shoulder injury, but it looks like he is going to be able to play through it in Week 3, barring any setbacks between now and then. Fantasy managers should keep tabs on his status throughout the week.

news.body: Malik Washington caught five passes for 67 yards in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Malik Washington leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: Washington played pretty well on Sunday, finishing with most of the team's receiving yards in their loss to the Vikings. He's one of their only competent receivers at this point, but he still shouldn't be started in most league formats for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Malik Washington hauled in five of his team-high 10 targets for 56 yards while also rushing twice for five yards in the Dolphins' 24-10 Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Malik Washington sees seven touches in Week 3 loss to Chiefs
news.impact: Washington has made the most of steady involvement as part of an underwhelming Miami passing attack, posting over 40 receiving yards in each of the first three games. The wideout remains another risky option in a disappointing Dolphins offense to this point, with a Week 4 contest against a disruptive Minnesota Vikings defense up next.

news.body: Malik Washington secured 4-of-5 targets for 43 yards, adding four yards on one carry in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
news.head: Malik Washington grabs four passes in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Washington has now hauled in seven combined passes over the first two weeks for an average of 13.7 yards. His production to this point is likely an indicator of what to expect for the duration of the season in the Dolphins' anemic offensive attack.

news.body: Malik Washington caught three of his eight targets for 53 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
news.head: Malik Washington catches three passes in Week 1 loss
news.impact: Washington made a modest impact despite leading the team in targets, finishing third on the team in receptions in the loss. The wideout remains another high-risk pass-catching option as part of a Miami offense searching to establish their identity as the season continues, with a Week 2 contest against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.body: Marvin Harrison Jr. hauled in 1-of-4 targets for 12 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Harrison started out Sunday's game well by catching a touchdown somewhat early, but he wasn't able to do anything beyond that, failing to catch any of his other three targets against the Giants. He shouldn't be considered a viable fantasy asset moving forward, especially with Michael Wilson clearly emerging as the top wideout on this roster.

news.body: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday.
news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. totals 40 yards Sunday
news.impact: The talk around the NFL the past two weeks has been Harrison not being targeted by Jacoby Brissett. He was a little more involved this week, but still not enough to be trustworthy in fantasy lineups.

news.body: Marvin Harrison Jr. failed to catch his only target in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to Seattle on Sunday.
news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. sees one target in loss
news.impact: This is a big development for Harrison. He only caught one pass in the season opener, and now that has escalated to just a single target in this game. It's unclear if the team has given up on him, or if it's more of a lack of effort on his part, QB Jacoby Brissett looking elsewhere when targeting receivers, or some combination of all three. Either way, the team needs to figure out a way to use their 2024 first-round investment. That, or trade him away to a new team and acquire assets while he gets a fresh start.

news.body: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught only 1-of-3 targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. finishes with one grab in season opener
news.impact: Aside from one big play, Harrison did not make much of a mark for the Cardinals in Sunday's win. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett looked Harrison's way just three times, which was good for only fifth on the team. After finishing well behind fellow wide receivers Kendrick Bourne (8) and Michael Wilson (7) in targets, Harrison might be best viewed as a wait-and-see bench stash for now.

news.body: Matthew Golden caught three of his seven targets for 21 yards and a touchdown while adding a six-yard rush in a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers in Week 4.
news.head: Matthew Golden finds the end zone in Week 4
news.impact: Golden found the end zone on a two-yard pass from Jordan Love in the second quarter. The second-year wideout now has 18 catches for 274 yards and two touchdowns through four games. Golden sets up as a WR2 in fantasy heading into a Week 5 matchup against the Bears.

news.body: Matthew Golden caught 5 of 12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
news.head: Matthew Golden snags touchdown in loss to Falcons
news.impact: Golden had several passes intended for him tipped by defensive backs after being undethrown, and another target where the DB committed a pass interference penalty. So, the five catches on 12 targets may not seem great; there is still context to be had. He is startable each week for the Packers.

news.body: Matthew Golden hauled in four of his six targets for a team-high 58 yards in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: Matthew Golden leads pass-catchers in Week 2 win over Jets
news.impact: Golden has been one of the few bright spots in an underperforming Packers offense to begin the season, recording four or more receptions for over 50 receiving yards in each of the first two contests. The wideout will look for another impactful performance in a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.body: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-12 targets for 95 yards in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings.
news.head: Matthew Golden totals 95 yards Sunday
news.impact: After a lost rookie season, Golden opened this year leading Green Bay receivers in targets on Sunday. He is in the WR3/WR4 mix heading into Week 2 for fantasy managers.

news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. came up with only 2-of-4 targets for 15 yards in Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. frustrates fantasy managers again in Week 4
news.impact: Even though Pittman got just three targets during his Steelers' debut back in Week 1, he caught all of them for 58 yards. That was a fairly promising start. Since then, it's been all frustration for Pittman's fantasy managers. He missed Week 2 with an injury, following that up with just four catches for 31 yards over the last two games. If Pittman cannot get going against his former mates from Indy in Week 5, it will probably be time to cut bait in standard-depth leagues.

news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. caught 2-of-5 targets for 16 yards in a 30-27 win over the Bengals.
news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. quiet in Week 3 win
news.impact: Pittman was making his return from a foot injury that sidelined him in Week 2. The expectation is that Pittman would immediately eat into Roman Wilson's playing time, but Wilson turned in a 3-60-1 performance in the win. Fantasy managers may want to avoid Pittman in Week 4 against the Browns.

news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) is expected to play on Sunday against the Bengals after being considered questionable with a foot injury.
news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) expected to play on Sunday against Cincy
news.impact: Pittman should give Aaron Rodgers a reliable possession receiver over the middle of the field, opening things up for the offense. Germie Bernard tried to play that role last week, but didn’t quite have the same fluidity as Pittman. He should be a decent WR3 with upside.

news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) questionable for Sunday
news.impact: Pittman missed last week's game due to a foot injury, but he is officially questionable for Week 3 and will have a chance to make his return against the Bengals this week. He was able to practice this week, but he remained limited, so he looks like a true 50-50 at this point. Pat Freiermuth will continue to see more work if the veteran misses another game.

news.body: Michael Wilson brought in 7-of-13 targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Michael Wilson leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: The young wideout was one of the bright spots for the Cardinals on Sunday. He led the team with 95 yards over the course of the afternoon, and he continues to build on the success that he has already found in the first quarter or so of the season. He should continue to be a worthy starter in most fantasy league formats for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Michael Wilson caught 11-of-17 targets for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday.
news.head: Michael Wilson hauls in 11 passes Sunday
news.impact: Wilson posted his biggest performance of the early season fresh off his contract extension this past offseason. He hauled in a touchdown from Jacoby Brissett in the third quarter. He profiles as a WR3 heading into next week against the Giants.

news.body: Michael Wilson caught two of seven targets for 18 yards in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
news.head: Michael Wilson sees seven targets in loss
news.impact: Wilson failed to connect with QB Jacoby Brissett in this game, and fantasy managers will be wishing for more after such a bad showing. He wil look to bounce back against the Niners next Sunday.

news.body: Michael Wilson secured 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.head: Michael Wilson comes up with five catches in Week 1
news.impact: With his next lucrative contract extension in hand, Wilson turned in a decent performance during Sunday's win. The fourth-year receiver finished third on the team in receptions, targets, and receiving yards, maintaining a solid rapport with QB Jacoby Brissett.

news.body: Mike Evans caught five of his eight targets for 76 yards in Sunday's 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Mike Evans leads 49ers in receiving Sunday
news.impact: Evans didn't find the end zone, but he led San Francisco in both targets and receiving yards. He averaged 15.2 yards per catch and continued to make plays down the field despite playing through a rib injury. The volume remains encouraging for fantasy managers heading into Week 5 against Seattle to make Evans a WR3.

news.body: Mike Evans (ribs) is officially active for Week 4 for the San Francisco 49ers against the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Mike Evans (ribs) active for Week 4
news.impact: Evans is good to go after passing through pregame warmups without any issues with the injured ribs, setting the wideout up for a prominent role in the San Francisco passing attack against a tough Denver secondary Sunday.

news.body: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Mike Evans will be a game-time decision heading into Sunday.
news.head: Mike Evans (ribs) to be game-time decision Sunday
news.impact: Evans has been managing an injury to his ribs that he suffered last week. There is some risk that he may be limited if he is ruled active. He would be a risky WR2 play for fantasy managers this week.

news.body: Mike Evans (ribs) was officially a non-participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Mike Evans (ribs) officially a non-participant Thursday
news.impact: The veteran was able to work off to the side a bit at practice on Thursday, but he didn't participate in any team drills and is officially considered a non-participant. It looks like he's slightly trending the wrong way for Week 4, although we won't get an official injury designation for him until after practice on Friday.

news.body: Mitch Tinsley caught 3-of-7 targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: Mitch Tinsley solid in loss Sunday
news.impact: Tinsley was able to step up and make a few big plays for the Bengals on Sunday, finishing with 49 yards after signing with Cincinnati less than a week ago. He will likely continue to be a solid contributor for the team next week, with one or both of Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) likely to be sidelined against the Dolphins.

news.body: The Bengals are signing WR Mitch Tinsley off the Texans practice.
news.head: Mitchell Tinsley signs with Bengals
news.impact: Tinsley will be added to the active roster for Cincinnati. He'll add depth in the Bengals wide receiver room.

news.body: The Bengals waived WR Mitch Tinsley.
news.head: Mitch Tinsley waived by Bengals
news.impact: Tinsley previously spent time in a depth role in the Bengals wide receiver room. He will seek another opportunity.

news.body: The Bengals signed WR Mitchell Tinsley to a one-year extension.
news.head: Mitch Tinsley signs one-year extension with Bengals
news.impact: Tinsley was set to be an exclusive rights free agent. He showed some flashes when Tee Higgins was sidelined. He figures to remain off the fantasy radar.

news.body: Nico Collins caught 7-of-8 targets for 118 yards and two touchdowns in the Texans 34-30 loss against the Cowboys.
news.head: Nico Collins explodes in return Sunday
news.impact: Collins picked right up where he left off in his return from injury. He scored the first touchdown of the day for Houston and continued to dominate all afternoon despite the loss. He'll be a WR1 next week against the Titans.

news.body: Nico Collins (hamstring) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
news.head: Nico Collins (hamstring) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: Collins is set to make his return to the lineup on Sunday after missing the last two games due to a hamstring injury. Fantasy managers shouldn't hesitate to start him as often as he's healthy and on the field moving forward. His return will likely mean less work for Dalton Schultz and Xavier Hutchinson for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Nico Collins was at practice again on Friday.
news.head: Nico Collins (hamstring) practices Friday
news.impact: Collins was limited on back-to-back days to start the week. He continues to trend towards making his return on Sunday.

news.body: Nico Collins remained limited in practice on Thursday.
news.head: Nico Collins (hamstring) limited in practice Thursday
news.impact: Collins was limited for the second straight day in practice. He remains on track to have a good chance to return on Sunday against the Cowboys.

news.body: Parker Washington caught 1-of-3 targets for just seven yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Parker Washington held to one catch Sunday
news.impact: Washington had a total disappearing act on Sunday. He was held to just one catch for a measly seven yards against the Bengals after starting out the first three weeks of the season as a red-hot fantasy option. He should bounce back and return to being a quality starter very quickly, but seeing this kind of floor for the veteran was unexpected and not ideal for fantasy managers.

news.body: Parker Washington hauled in 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Parker Washington hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Washington was slightly underwhelming in terms of receptions and yardage on Sunday, but he was able to find the end zone against New England, which left him with a nice fantasy total once again. He has been very good to start the season and should continue to be started in nearly all leagues for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Parker Washington caught seven of his 12 targets for 98 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Parker Washington goes for 98 yards in Week 2
news.impact: Washington led the Jacksonville receivers in all receiving categories while nearly reaching 100 yards in a tough matchup against Denver. The veteran has been excellent through the first two games of the season, posting 12 catches for 181 yards and a touchdown. Clearly the alpha in the Jacksonville receiving room, Washington will be a low-end WR1/high-end WR2 in Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.body: Parker Washington caught five of six targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns.
news.head: Parker Washington snags touchdown in win
news.impact: Washington answered the call of all the offseason hype with flying colors. He scored on a 30-yard bomb from Trevor Lawrence early on in the game and kept showing up to make plays afterwards. Expect Washington to continue to be a focal point in the offense, especially if Brian Thomas Jr. were to miss any time.

news.body: Puka Nacua caught 9-of-12 targets for 125 yards and added one touchdown on the ground in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Puka Nacua stellar in return game Sunday
news.impact: The star wideout made his return to the lineup in Week 4 after missing a bit of time due to an injury of some kind. He looked great in his first game back, finishing with 125 receiving yards and a rushing touchdown in a narrow win over the Eagles. He will continue to be a must-start fantasy option moving forward.

news.body: Puka Nacua (groin) is expected to receive a full workload for the Los Angeles Rams against the Philadelphia Eagles Sunday according to Adam Schefter.
news.head: Puka Nacua (groin) planning on full workload Sunday
news.impact: Nacua has missed the last games due to groin and hip injuries, but seems poised for a return to a major role in the Los Angeles passing attack barring any setbacks for head coach Sean McVay against the Eagles Sunday.

news.body: Rams head coach Sean McVay confirmed that Puka Nacua will play on Sunday against the Eagles.
news.head: Puka Nacua (groin) will play Sunday
news.impact: Barshop notes that "the Rams are still working through how they will navigate Nacua's snap count." It will still be tough to sit him in fantasy lineups.

news.body: Puka Nacua (groin) was officially a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Puka Nacua (groin) officially limited Thursday
news.impact: Some reports early in the day indicated that Nacua would be a full participant at Thursday's practice, but he ended up being limited for a second-straight day. There seems to be optimism surrounding his availability for Week 4, but fantasy managers should continue to keep close tabs on updates about his health over the next day or two to ensure that that will be the case.

news.body: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-2 targets for 44 yards in the Chargers 30-23 loss against the Seahawks.
news.head: Quentin Johnston totals 44 yards Sunday
news.impact: Johnston hauled in one 44 yard pass from Justin Herbert. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Quentin Johnston caught three of his six targets for 40 yards in the Chargers' 24-16 Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Quentin Johnston sees six targets in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Johnston has struggled to capitalize on a generous target share early in the season, recording three receptions or less on 17 total targets in the first three contests. The wideout remains one of many risky pass-catching options in an underperforming Chargers offense early on, with a Week 4 contest against the Seattle Seahawks up next.

news.body: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-5 targets for just seven yards and rushed the ball one time for seven yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.head: Quentin Johnston struggles in loss Sunday
news.impact: Los Angeles' offense as a while struggled on Sunday, and Johnston was no exception to that. He wasn't able to haul in all but one of his five targets against the Raiders, and he only ended up contributing 14 total yards over the course of the game. He isn't worth rostering in most league formats at this point in the season.

news.body: Quentin Johnston came up with only 2-of-6 targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.head: Quentin Johnston does little in Week 1 loss
news.impact: Johnston has finished each of the last two seasons with more than 50 grabs, over 700 yards, and exactly eight touchdowns. Some have him pegged to take the next big step up in his fourth season, but some of that hype will be quelled with this season-opening disappointment. The Chargers' offense just had a difficult time getting much going at all in their first game under new OC Mike McDaniel. Johnston should still produce some valuable stats, and he may have just become a nice buy-low option for fantasy purposes.

news.body: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice is questionable to return against the Raiders with a hamstring injury.
news.head: Rashee Rice (hamstring) questionable to return
news.impact: Rice suffered the injury after a reception and hobbled off the field. Fantasy managers should expect the team to provide an update after halftime.

news.body: Rashee Rice hauled in seven of his team-high nine targets for 88 yards in the Chiefs' 24-10 Week 3 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Rashee Rice leads pass-catchers in Week 3 win over Dolphins
news.impact: Rice has heated up in the Kansas City offense of late, posting over 80 receiving yards in each of his last two contests. The wideout remains one of the more dynamic pass-catching options in the Chiefs passing attack moving forward, with a Week 4 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders up next.

news.body: Rashee Rice (knee) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Rashee Rice (knee) without injury designation for Sunday
news.impact: Rice's knee injury is nothing more than a minor issue at this point and won't affect his availability for Week 3. Fantasy managers should be starting him this week, though maybe expectations should be tempered for him after an underwhelming first two games of the season.

news.body: Rashee Rice was a full participant in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Rashee Rice (knee) logs full practice Wednesday
news.impact: Rice remains on the injury report with a knee issue, but it shouldn't impact his status heading into Week 3. He remains a borderline WR1/WR2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks 30-23 win over the Chargers. He also saw two carries for 33 yards and a touchdown.
news.head: Rashid Shaheed scores touchdown on ground Sunday
news.impact: With Jadarian Price on IR, Emanuel Wilson was the workhorse in the Seahawks backfield. Shaheed saw two traditional handoffs from Sam Darnold with one of them resulting in a 28-yard touchdown. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Rashid Shaheed was a full participant in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Rashid Shaheed (hip) logs full practice Wednesday
news.impact: Shaheed is a volatile WR4 with upside in his current role.

news.body: Rashid Shaheed hauled in two of his three targets for 14 yards in the Seahawks’ 33-31 Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Rashid Shaheed catches two passes in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Shaheed has made minimal impact in the Seattle offense to behind the season, finishing under 40 receiving yards in each of the first three contests. The wideout remains another risky pass-catching option to this point, with a Week 4 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.body: Rashid Shaheed caught three of six targets for 35 yards and ran once for four yards in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over the Cardinals.
news.head: Rashid Shaheed goes for 39 yards in win
news.impact: Shaheed was second on the team in targets, but it all amounted to less than a quarter of the yards teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba had on his 11 targets. Shaheed can have some spike performances, but especially with Drew Lock being more conservative and locked onto JSN, he's more of a flex play at best right now.

news.body: Rashod Bateman caught 2-of-2 targets for 46 yards in the Ravens win over the Titans.
news.head: Rashod Bateman held to two receptions in Week 4
news.impact: Bateman has not been able to replicate his Week 2 success with Zay Flowers in the lineup. Fantasy managers should view Bateman as a risky option heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Falcons.

news.body: Rashod Bateman caught two of his three targets for 37 yards in a 34-31 win over the Cowboys in Week 3.
news.head: Rashod Bateman held to two catches in Week 3
news.impact: Bateman was quiet in the high-scoring win over the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday. After a big game in Week 2, Bateman went back to a complementary role with Zay Flowers returning following a one-week absence. Bateman now has nine catches for 125 yards and a touchdown through three games on the year. He will be a low-end flex heading into Week 4 against the Titans.

news.body: Rashod Bateman caught 7-of-9 targets for 88 yards and a touchdown in the 24-17 loss to the Saints.
news.head: Rashod Bateman scores in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Bateman found the end zone on a 22-yard touchdown to close out the second half. Bateman was the target of the interception late in the game that allowed the Saints to close out the game. If Zay Flowers (hamstring) is unavailable to play in Week 3, Bateman would serve as the primary wide receiver against Dallas.

news.body: Rashod Bateman failed to catch his lone target in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1.
news.head: Rashod Bateman sees one target in Week 1
news.impact: Bateman operated as more of an afterthought in a Baltimore passing attack that lost both Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) to injury, but could be in line for increased usage if either of the pass-catchers misses time ahead of a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

news.body: Roman Wilson caught 3-of-6 targets for 74 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
news.head: Roman Wilson scores again in Week 4
news.impact: Wilson has now scored in two straight weeks, as he's become a consistently reliable target for QB Aaron Rodgers. Wilson has gotten exactly six targets in each of the first four games of the season, catching at least three of them each time out. Overall, he's second on the team with 188 receiving yards and tied for second with 14 receptions. Wilson should be fairly popular pickup in Week 5.

news.body: Roman Wilson caught 3-of-6 targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in a 30-27 win over the Bengals.
news.head: Roman Wilson finds the end zone in Week 3 win
news.impact: Wilson was expected to potentially see his playing time fall with the return of Michael Pittman, but the 25-year-old tallied his first touchdown of the season and a season high in receiving yards. Wilson will look to build on this performance against the Browns in Week 4.

news.body: Steelers WR Roman Wilson caught 5-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Roman Wilson hauls in five passes in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Wilson has now seen six targets in both games this season and should continue to see an increase in usage as long as Michael Pittman is dealing with an ankle injury. Wilson's five receptions lead the team, but the Steelers' passing attack really failed to get anything consistent going. Wilson and the Steelers will take on the Bengals at home in Week 3.

news.body: Roman Wilson saw reps with the Steelers first-team at practice on Saturday.
news.head: Roman Wilson sees first-team reps Saturday
news.impact: Farabaugh notes that Wilson also took reps as a punt returner during practice. He is continuing to take on a larger role during training camp.

news.body: Rome Odunze caught six of his seven targets for 94 yards in a 23-12 win over the Jets in Week 4.
news.head: Rome Odunze goes for 94 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Odunze led the Bears in all receiving categories in what was his best game of the season. The veteran receiver has now caught 14 passes for 233 yards and no touchdowns through four games. Odunze will be a low-end WR3 in fantasy in Week 5 vs. the Packers.

news.body: Rome Odunze caught three of his six targets for 44 yards in a 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
news.head: Rome Odunze goes for 44 yards in Week 3
news.impact: Odunze finished third on the Bears in targets and receiving yards but he was unable to find the end zone for the third straight game. The veteran wideout has been outproduced by both Luther Burden III and Kalif Raymond this season, catching just eight passes for 139 yards thus far through three games. He will be a fantasy flex option in Week 4 against the Jets.

news.body: Rome Odunze caught three of his four targets for 43 yards in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Rome Odunze catches three passes in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Odunze has struggled to make an impact in a slow-starting Chicago passing attack to begin the season, finishing with three receptions or less in each of the first two games. The pass-catcher remains difficult to trust with the potential absence of quarterback Caleb Williams ahead of a Week 3 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

news.body: Rome Odunze (calf) carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Rome Odunze (calf) off injury report for Week 2
news.impact: Odunze has been recovering from a calf injury for a while, but it seems that he is fully over it at this point, as he isn't listed on Chicago's injury report at all heading into Week 2. It's likely that his workload will ramp up this week after he was limited in the season opener, which should help him to produce a fantasy finish better than his underwhelming performance in Week 1.

news.body: Romeo Doubs caught 6-of-9 targets for 58 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots win over the Bills.
news.head: Romeo Doubs hauls in two touchdowns in Week 4 win
news.impact: Doubs caught passes of two and 14 yards to account for two of Drake Maye's three touchdown passes on the day. This was easily Doubs' best day as a Patriot. Fantasy managers should expect Doubs to continue to see plenty of targets heading into a Week 5 matchup with Las Vegas.

news.body: Romeo Doubs caught 3-of-4 targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: Romeo Doubs underwhelming in loss Sunday
news.impact: Doubs looked good with nearly 100 yards in Week 2, but he didn't find the same success this week, catching just three passes for 49 scoreless yards in a blowout loss to the Jaguars. He isn't a reliable fantasy option at this point in the season and shouldn't be started in most leagues, even if he continues to have decent upside on a week-to-week basis.

news.body: Patriots WR Romeo Doubs caught 3-of-4 targets for 96 yards in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
news.head: Romeo Doubs rebounds after a tough Week 1
news.impact: Doubs had a rough Week 1 but bounced back to lead the Patriots' wide receivers in yardage in Week 2, including an impressive 63-yard reception. With A.J. Brown on injured reserve, Doubs has the opportunity to lead the Patriots' wide receiver room until he returns. Doubs and the Patriots will travel to Jacksonville in Week 3.

news.body: Romeo Doubs didn't haul in any of his three targets in Wednesday night's 10-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Romeo Doubs fails to log catch Wednesday
news.impact: Doubs did not get off to a good start with his new team on Wednesday night. He failed to haul in even a single catch against a tough Seattle defense, and he had a costly drop on a very important play late in the game. He should bounce back in the near future and may be a worthwhile fantasy option short-term with A.J. Brown (ankle) expected to miss a bit of time due to injury.

news.body: Ryan Flournoy caught 4-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Cowboys 34-30 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.head: Ryan Flournoy hauls in four passes Sunday
news.impact: Flournoy continues to have a limited role in the offense for Dallas. He is a WR4 for fantasy managers.

news.body: Ryan Flournoy caught two of his eight targets for 22 yards in a 34-31 loss to the Ravens in Brazil in Week 3.
news.head: Ryan Flournoy draws eight targets in Week 3
news.impact: Flournoy didn't do much damage through the air but he drew an encouraging eight targets in the loss. If he can continue to get that type of work consistently, Flournoy might work his way into the flex conversation in fantasy leagues. For now, he's best left on the bench heading into a Week 4 matchup against a tough Houston Texans defense.

news.body: Ryan Flournoy caught 5-of-6 targets for 23 yards in the Cowboys win over the Commanders.
news.head: Ryan Flournoy hauls in five passes in Week 2
news.impact: Flournoy continues to operate as the WR3 in the Cowboys' offense. Fantasy managers could view him as a flex play in deeper leagues heading into Week 3.

news.body: Ryan Flournoy caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in Sunday's loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Ryan Flournoy totals 22 yards Sunday
news.impact: Flournoy wasn't able to contribute much on Sunday night, being held to just 22 yards in the team's upset loss at the hands of the Giants. He won't have enough opportunities to be a relevant fantasy option anytime soon.

news.body: Stefon Diggs caught 5-of-9 targets for 35 yards in the Commanders loss to the Colts in London.
news.head: Stefon Diggs hauls in five passes in Week 4
news.impact: Diggs led the team in targets and receptions in the loss Sunday. If Terry McLaurin (hamstring) is unable to play, Diggs could serve as the WR1 for the Commanders against the Giants next week. Fantasy managers will want to monitor the situation, as the quarterback could be rookie Athan Kaliakmanis if Jayden Daniels (elbow) does not return.

news.body: Stefon Diggs hauled in four of his seven targets for 33 yards in the Commanders’ 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Stefon Diggs hauls in four passes in Week 3 win
news.impact: Diggs has made the most of his involvement in the Washington passing attack early on, recording four or more receptions in each of the first three games. The veteran wideout remains one of the few stable pass-catching options in an inconsistent offense to this point, with a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts up next.

news.body: Stefon Diggs caught 5-of-6 targets for 47 yards and two touchdowns in the Commanders loss to the Cowboys.
news.head: Stefon Diggs hauls in two touchdowns in Week 2
news.impact: Diggs caught touchdowns from both Jayden Daniels and Marcus Maroita to account for both of the team's touchdowns. Diggs has turned in two strong games in his first season in Washington. Diggs and the Commanders will take on the Seahawks in Week 3.

news.body: Stefon Diggs hauled in four of his nine targets for 55 yards and one touchdown in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Stefon Diggs finds end zone in Week 1 loss to Eagles
news.impact: Diggs saw plenty of volume as part of a Washington passing attack held in check, leading the team in targets in a losing effort. The veteran wideout offers fantasy managers a stable WR2/3 option while the Commanders offense looks to get back on track in a Week 2 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

news.body: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said Tank Dell will have his practice window opened.
news.head: Tank Dell (knee) will have practice window opened
news.impact: Dell will have 21 days to officially be activated. He is unlikely to be fantasy relevant when he first returns.

news.body: The Texans agreed to terms with Tank Dell on a one-year, $1.7 million contract restructure.
news.head: Tank Dell restructures contract with Texans
news.impact: The move saves Houston $2 million against the cap. Dell is nearing his return from a gruesome knee injury he suffered late in the 2024 season.

news.body: Texans GM Nick Caserio said Tank Dell is “close” but “not quite there.”
news.head: Tank Dell (knee) is 'close' but 'not quite there'
news.impact: Dell was placed on injured reserve, so he’ll miss the first four games of the season. It is unclear when he'll be activated.

news.body: Tank Dell (knee) has been placed on IR and will miss at least the first four games of the season.
news.head: Tank Dell (knee) placed on IR, designated to return
news.impact: Dell last played in an NFL game all the way back in 2024. The 26-year-old wideout has been practicing for the Texans, but he will be given a bit more time to get fully back up to speed. The earliest Dell could see the field is now Week 5.

news.body: Ted Hurst III caught two of his three targets for 25 yards in a 17-14 loss to the Packers in Week 4.
news.head: Ted Hurst III goes for 25 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Hurst made a 21-yard catch early in the second quarter but would go on to post just one more catch for a four-yard gain in the loss. The rookie wideout has looked explosive in limited chances this season, catching eight passes for 128 yards and a touchdown through four games. He will face the Cowboys in Week 5.

news.body: Ted Hurst III caught 1-of-4 targets for 40 yards receiving and a touchdown in the Buccaneers 23-16 loss against the Vikings on Sunday.
news.head: Ted Hurst III hauls in deep touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Hurst caught a 40-yard deep ball from Baker Mayfield in the first half for a score. It was his lone catch on the day. The status of Mayfield will need to be monitored after he left late in the loss.

news.body: Ted Hurst III caught 2-of-7 targets for 27 yards in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns.
news.head: Ted Hurst III sees seven targets Sunday
news.impact: Hurst led Tampa Bay in targets, but they did not result in much of anything production wise. He is on the upside WR4 radar right now for fantasy managers.

news.body: Ted Hurst III caught 3-of-3 targets for 36 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss on Sunday against the Bengals.
news.head: Ted Hurst III catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Hurst saw more opportunity as the WR3 with Jalen McMillan sidelined and he was able to flash. He'll still remain off the fantasy radar heading into Week 2.

news.body: Tee Higgins (adductor) was labeled day-to-day by Bengals head coach Zac Taylor on Monday.
news.head: Tee Higgins (adductor) listed day-to-day
news.impact: Higgins had a huge game Sunday after fellow Cincy receiver Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) was knocked out of the loss to the Jaguars early. Higgins was clearly dealing with an injury of his own late in the game, however. It was later revealed to be an adductor issue, but it appears the injury is considered mild. Higgins should be monitored at practice this week.

news.body: Bengals WR Tee Higgins suffered an adductor injury late in Sunday's loss to Jacksonville.
news.head: Tee Higgins suffers adductor injury Sunday
news.impact: Higgins had an excellent day against Jacksonville, but suffered the injury late and was unable to go back into the game. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status ahead of a Week 5 matchup with Miami.

news.body: Tee Higgins caught 6-of-7 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in a 30-27 loss to the Steelers.
news.head: Tee Higgins finds the end zone in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Higgins was just behind Ja'Marr Chase in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the loss Sunday. He found the end zone for the first time this season on an impressive 28-yard reception prior to halftime. Higgins and the Bengals will welcome the Jaguars to town in Week 4.

news.body: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-10 targets for 95 yards in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.head: Tee Higgins racks up 95 yards Sunday
news.impact: Higgins recorded several big catch and runs in the first half against a strong Texans defense. He remains an upside WR2 heading into next week against the Steelers.

news.body: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) is officially inactive for Week 4 for the Washington Commanders against the Indianapolis Colts according to Ian Rapoport.
news.head: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) inactive for Week 4
news.impact: McLaurin will not suit up after being unable to progress throughout the week from a hamstring injury suffered in Week 3. Veteran Stefon Diggs slides into a WR1 role for head coach Dan Quinn, with Antonio Williams also expected to see increased targets against the Colts Sunday.

news.body: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) is likely to sit out Sunday's game against the Colts.
news.head: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) not expected to play Sunday
news.impact: McLaurin was listed as questionable on Friday, but the strong belief is that the Commanders will be without their No. 1 receiver on Sunday. Veteran Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams should see the highest snap shares among Washington wide receivers.

news.body: Terry McLaurin is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Colts.
news.head: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) listed questionable Sunday
news.impact: McLaurin was a late addition to their injury report after he was limited in practice on Friday. His status will need to be monitored closer to kickoff Sunday morning.

news.body: Terry McLaurin hauled in six of his nine targets for 77 yards and one touchdown in the Commanders’ 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Terry McLaurin leads pass-catchers in Week 3 win over Seahawks
news.impact: McLaurin has heated up in the Washington offense of late, registering 50 or more receiving yards in each of the last two contests. The wideout offers fantasy managers one of the few explosive options in the Washington passing attack ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

news.body: Tetairoa McMillan collected 14 receptions on 16 targets for 192 yards and a pair of touchdowns in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
news.head: Tetairoa McMillan shreds Lions secondary Sunday night
news.impact: For those frustrated by McMillan's paltry output in Week 3, the second-year star erupted for career highs in receptions and yards Sunday night. He also recorded the second multi-touchdown game of his career. It's important to note that this performance came with both Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee) out, but McMillan still displayed his immense upside. He's a solid WR2 for fantasy purposes at present.

news.body: Tetairoa McMillan caught 2-of-5 targets for just 17 yards in Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Cleveland Browns.
news.head: Tetairoa McMillan disappears in loss Sunday
news.impact: McMillan got shut down on Sunday. He was only able to catch two passes for just 17 yards against the Browns, despite being the team's clear WR1 after Jalen Coker (quad) left the game. He should bounce back in the near future, but it's possible that his week-to-week floor will be lower than managers hoped coming into the season.

news.body: Tetairoa McMillan caught 5 of 10 targets for 101 yards in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
news.head: Tetairoa McMillan leads Panthers receivers in win
news.impact: McMillan's ten targets led the team, with Jalen Coker falling close behind with nine. It's a bummer he didn't connect on more than five, as he could have had a much bigger day. He and Coker are forming a formidable receiving duo in Carolina, and both are startable every week.

news.body: Tetairoa McMillan hauled in five of his eight targets for 75 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Tetairoa McMillan hauls in five receptions in Week 1 loss
news.impact: McMillan made the most of his sizeable volume in the Carolina passing attack, finishing second in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the loss. The wideout remains one of the more dynamic pass-catching options in the Carolina offense moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.body: Tre' Harris caught 3-of-5 targets for 60 yards in the Chargers 30-23 loss against the Seahawks.
news.head: Tre' Harris totals 60 yards Sunday
news.impact: Harris was the leading receiver for Justin Herbert and the Chargers on the day. He'll be a flex play next week if Ladd McConkey (foot) is sidelined.

news.body: Tre' Harris hauled in six of his team-high seven targets for 76 yards in the Chargers' 24-16 Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.head: Tre' Harris leads pass-catchers in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Harris has capitalized on inconsistent usage in the Los Angeles offense of late, leading the team in receiving yards in each of the last two games. The wideout remains one of the more stable pass-catching options as part of an underwhelming Chargers offense to begin the season, with a Week 4 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks up next.

news.body: Tre' Harris caught 1-of-3 targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.head: Tre' Harris leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: Harris was the leading receiver for the Chargers on Sunday, and he was able to earn that title with just one 53-yard catch on the afternoon. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high hopes for him moving forward after two underwhelming games to start the season.

news.body: Tre' Harris caught 3-of-6 targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.head: Tre' Harris finishes with three receptions in Week 1
news.impact: Harris was at least significantly involved in the passing game Sunday, as the second-year wideout tied a career high in targets set in Week 18 of last season. Harris did not do much with those targets, however, totaling only 20 yards with a long of 11. The second-round pick from 2025 is a fringe redraft option at present.

news.body: Tre Tucker caught four of his eight targets for 44 yards in a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs in Week 4.
news.head: Tre Tucker goes for 44 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Tucker tied for third on the team with his eight targets in a game where Kirk Cousins attempted 52 passes. Tucker has been a solid fantasy option this season, posting 15 catches for 233 yards and a touchdown through four games. He will be a fantasy flex in Week 5 vs. the Patriots.

news.body: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-4 targets for 43 yards in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
news.head: Tre Tucker hauls in four passes Sunday
news.impact: Tucker led Raiders wide receivers in receptions and yards. Still his upside remains limited for fantasy managers.

news.body: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 119 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Tre Tucker stellar in win Sunday
news.impact: The Raiders were able to pick up an upset win over the Chargers on Sunday, and Tucker played a big part in that. He led the team in receptions and yards over the course of the afternoon, and he also caught a touchdown, which further helped his fantasy total. He will likely have other big games moving forward, but they will be inconsistent and hard to predict, especially with Brock Bowers (knee) soon to return to the lineup.

news.body: Tre Tucker caught two of his four targets for 27 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
news.head: Tre Tucker catches two passes in Week 1
news.impact: Tucker was one of six to catch at least one pass from Kirk Cousins in the season opener, averaging a team-high 13.5 yards per reception. The wideout remains one of many pass-catching options as part of a revamped Las Vegas offense, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.body: Tyreek Hill is expected to sign with a team in the coming days, per his agent. He’s been linked to the Chiefs, but other teams are in the mix.
news.head: Tyreek Hill expected to sign in the coming days
news.impact: Hill could give the Chiefs some depth, but it will be interesting to see how much of an impact he could make at this stage of his career while also coming off of a major knee injury. He’s worth stashing, but keep expectations low.

news.body: Tyreek Hill is not expected to sign with a team before the season begins, according to his agent Drew Rosenhaus.
news.head: Tyreek Hill not expected to sign before Week 1
news.impact: Hill has been on the long road to recovery after sustaining a major knee injury in Week 4 last season, and it looks like he will remain a free agent when the 2026 season begins. However, the 32-year-old could receive interest from contenders as the season goes on if he continues to progress in his rehab.

news.body: Tyreek Hill says that he still has “no power” in his left leg that he injured early on in 2025 while playing for the Miami Dolphins. The free agent receiver still has a ways to go before playing football again.
news.head: Tyreek Hill says he still has ‘no power’ in left leg
news.impact: Hill suffered a gruesome knee dislocation and multiple ligament tears in Week 4 of 2025, missing the rest of the season. It’s a big blow to his chances of finding a team and making his way back onto the field in 2026, especially if he is still struggling to find power in his injured leg. More than likely he will miss the majority of 2026, and its possible he will not see the field again until 2027.

news.body: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said Tyreek Hill “might not be ready until midway through the season.”
news.head: Tyreek Hill (knee) 'might not be ready till midway through season'
news.impact: Hill suffered a gruesome knee injury in Week 4 of last season when he dislocated his knee, while also tearing his ACL and LCL. He has undergone multiple surgeries since his injury. He remains without a clear timetable to return as a free agent.

news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson caught 3-of-5 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Titans loss to the Ravens.
news.head: Wan'Dale Robinson hauls in three passes in Week 4
news.impact: Robinson caught the lone touchdown pass from Cam Ward against the Ravens, giving Robinson a touchdown in back-to-back games. The 25-year-old will look to continue that streak in Week 5 against the Texans.

news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson caught 7-of-11 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Wan'Dale Robinson finds end zone Sunday
news.impact: Robinson played well against his former team on Sunday. He led the team in targets and receptions against the Giants, and he also scored the team's only touchdown over the course of the afternoon. Despite the good game, fantasy managers should not consider him a viable option moving forward.

news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson caught his lone target for a nine-yard gain in a 24-20 loss to the Eagles in Week 2.
news.head: Wan'Dale Robinson held to one catch in Week 2
news.impact: Robinson was quiet in what was almost an upset win over the Eagles. The Titans only passed for 183 yards in the contest with Elic Ayomanor leading the way. Through two games in Tennessee, Robinson has caught six of his seven targets for 47 scoreless yards. He will need to see more frequent work moving forward to be trustworthy in fantasy. The Titans will face the Giants in Week 3.

news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson caught five of his six targets for 38 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.head: Wan'Dale Robninson goes for 38 yards in Week 1
news.impact: Robinson tied for the team lead in targets and receiving yards while leading the way with his five catches. The entire Tennessee offense struggled to move the ball in Week 1, which cut into Robinson's final stats. He will look to bounce back as a decent flex option in PPR leagues heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-5 targets for 46 yards in the Texans 34-30 loss against the Cowboys.
news.head: Xavier Hutchinson sees five targets Sunday
news.impact: Hutchinson made the most of his playing time despite seeing just 16 snaps. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 51 yards in a 19-17 loss to the Colts.
news.head: Xavier Hutchinson hauls in three passes in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Hutchinson was expected to step into a larger role with Nico Collins (hamstring) out of the lineup. The Houston offense struggled as a whole against the Colts and will look to pick up their first win of the season against Dallas in Week 4.

news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-9 targets for 37 yards in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Xavier Hutchinson sees nine targets Sunday
news.impact: With Nico Collins sidelined, Hutchinson led Houston in targets. It did not lead to much production. He could be in the streaming conversation in deeper leagues next week if Collins remains sidelined.

news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.head: Xavier Hutchinson finishes with three grabs in Week 1
news.impact: Hutchinson saw the third-most targets from C.J. Stroud on Sunday. The Texans are looking for a No. 2 wide receiver to emerge behind Nico Collins, and though Hutchinson's upside may be limited, he might be the guy at the moment. The fourth-year pro hauled in 35 passes for 428 yards and three scores over 17 games last season.

news.body: Xavier Worthy caught four of his seven targets for 70 yards in a 30-27 win over the Raiders in Week 4.
news.head: Xavier Worthy goes for 70 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Worthy got some extra looks with Rashee Rice injuring his hamstring during the game. The veteran did most of his damage on a 41-yard catch from Patrick Mahomes II. With Week 4 being by far his best game of the season, Worthy will look to stay hot in Week 6 against the Chargers after his Week 5 bye.

news.body: Xavier Worthy caught both of his targets for 20 yards in the Chiefs' 24-10 Week 3 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Xavier Worthy quiet in Week 3 win
news.impact: Worthy was bottled up by a surprising Miami defensive effort Sunday, finishing with less than three receptions for the first time in three contests. The wideout has struggled to offer fantasy managers a reliable pass-catching option to begin the season, with a Week 4 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders up next.

news.body: Xavier Worthy caught 5-of-7 targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Xavier Worthy finds end zone in overtime win Sunday
news.impact: Worthy saw good involvement with seven targets on Sunday night, although he was only able to turn that into five catches for 25 yards against the Colts. He was able to score on one of those catches, however, which salvaged his night from a fantasy perspective. He should not be considered a strong option at the wide receiver position until we see some more consistent production from him.

news.body: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 18 yards in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Xavier Worthy quiet in win Monday
news.impact: Worthy was Kansas City's most targeted player on Monday night, but he wasn't able to do much with his opportunities, finishing with just three catches for 18 yards against the Broncos. He isn't expected to be a relevant fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-10 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens win over the Titans.
news.head: Zay Flowers eclipses 100 receiving yards in Week 4
news.impact: Flowers found the end zone on a 19-yard touchdown pass from Lamar Jackson early in the second quarter. Flowers has recorded a touchdown in two of the three games he's played this season. He will look to continue his early season momentum against the Falcons in Week 5.

news.body: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) is officially active for a Week 4 matchup with the Titans.
news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) officially active for Week 4
news.impact: Flowers was tagged as questionable after being limited in practice twice this week. Fantasy managers should expect the Ravens' WR1 to see his usual share of targets against a struggling Titans' team.

news.body: Zay Flowers (hamstring) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) questionable to play Sunday
news.impact: Flowers is officially considered questionable to play heading into the weekend. It seems more likely than not that he will play on Sunday, but we won't know for sure until sometime closer to game time. Fantasy managers shouldn't hesitate to start him in this matchup if he's cleared to play without any major limitations.

news.body: Zay Flowers (hamstring) logged a full practice session for the Baltimore Ravens Thursday according to Mike Garafolo.
news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) logs full practice Thursday
news.impact: Flowers continues to make progress throughout the practice week for head coach Jesse Minter, putting the dynamic wideout in line to reclaim his No. 1 pass-catching role against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4 barring any setbacks during practice Friday.
